title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試小錄序
聖天子君臨
大寶于茲二十有二載天下以鄉
舉選士凡七科矣成化丙午
復當大比之期廣東藩臬重
臣恪遵
成憲預期禮聘儒紳以司文衡
===
瑭等濫竽而至于時都察院
右都御史宋旻受
命宣撫作興士類太監劉倜韋眷
總兵安遠侯柳景皆飭武備
衛文教而敦崇儒雅巡按監
察御史徐同愛以登庸髦俊
國家首事凡百規畫靡不究心
punctuated:
廣東鄉試小錄序

聖天子君臨大寶，于茲二十有二載，天下以鄉舉選士凡七科矣。成化丙午，復當大比之期，廣東藩臬重臣恪遵成憲，預期禮聘儒紳以司文衡。瑭等濫竽而至。于時，都察院右都御史宋旻受命宣撫，作興士類；太監劉倜、韋眷，總兵安遠侯柳景，皆飭武備，衛文教，而敦崇儒雅。巡按監察御史徐同愛以登庸髦俊，國家首事，凡百規畫，靡不究心。
translation_en:
Preface to the Short Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

It is now twenty-two years since the sagely Son of Heaven ascended the imperial throne. Throughout the realm, seven rounds of provincial examinations have been held to select scholars. In the bingwu year of Chenghua [1486], the time for the great triennial examination came again. The senior officials of Guangdong’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions scrupulously observed established regulations and, well before the appointed date, ceremonially invited Confucian scholars of standing to judge the examination essays. I, Tang, and my colleagues arrived, unworthily filling these posts.

At that time, Song Min, Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, had received orders to conduct a pacification mission and was encouraging and fostering the scholars. The Grand Eunuchs Liu Ti and Wei Juan, together with the Regional Commander Liu Jing, Marquis of Anyuan, all put military defenses in order, protected civil learning, and earnestly honored Confucian scholarship and refinement. Xu Tong’ai, the Investigating Censor on regional inspection, regarded the advancement and appointment of outstanding men as the foremost business of the state; in every aspect of planning, he devoted the utmost care.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乃合諸郡邑士之可舉者重
加精選得預試者千四百有
竒鎖院而三試之内而提調
監試則右叅政周瑛左叅議
姜英僉事翁晏周啓外而綜
理彌範則右布政使熊懷按
察使馮俊陶魯左叅政李芳
===
謝瑀副使俞俊李瑢僉事張
穀彭頎陳英李〔元鎮〕若後先匡
賛則提學僉事張習躬親任
之與凡執事者皆懋簡以充
而御史徐〔同愛〕實監臨焉比撤
棘得中式者七十有五人遵
定額也爰第其姓名及文之純
punctuated: 乃合諸郡邑士之可舉者，重加精選，得預試者千四百有竒。鎖院而三試之。内而提調監試，則右叅政周瑛、左叅議姜英、僉事翁晏、周啓；外而綜理彌範，則右布政使熊懷、按察使馮俊、陶魯、左叅政李芳、謝瑀、副使俞俊、李瑢、僉事張穀、彭頎、陳英、李〔元鎮〕。若後先匡賛，則提學僉事張習躬親任之。與凡執事者，皆懋簡以充，而御史徐〔同愛〕實監臨焉。比撤棘，得中式者七十有五人，遵定額也。爰第其姓名及文之純
translation_en: They then assembled the scholars from the prefectures and counties who were eligible for recommendation and subjected them to further rigorous selection. More than fourteen hundred qualified to sit the examination. The examination compound was sealed, and they were examined in three sessions. Within the compound, the proctoring and oversight of the examination were undertaken by Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhou Ying, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Jiang Ying, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Weng Yan and Zhou Qi. Outside, general administration and ‘mi fan’ [?] were handled by Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Xiong Huai; Provincial Surveillance Commissioners Feng Jun and Tao Lu; Left Administration Vice Commissioners Li Fang and Xie Yu; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yu Jun and Li Rong; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Zhang Gu, Peng Qi, Chen Ying, and Li Yuanzhen. Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Zhang Xi, who was in charge of education, personally undertook the work of assistance and support throughout. All those serving in the proceedings were likewise carefully selected for their duties, while Censor Xu Tong’ai served as Supervising Official. When the thorn barriers were removed, seventy-five candidates had passed, in accordance with the prescribed quota. Their names were then arranged in order, together with those of their examination writings that were pure …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
粹者具錄以
進謂瑭宜序諸首竊惟
國家求賢雖非一途恒以科目
爲重賢才入官之階雖非一
致率以科目爲榮我
太祖高皇帝受
天景命奄有萬方惓惓欲以人文
===
化成天下
詔有司三年一開科取士重之以
選舉榮之以賓興期得賢才
以爲化理之本
列聖相承率由舊典
皇上繼承大統克篤前烈而於興
賢之典益加慎重惟欲上當
punctuated: 粹者，具錄以進，謂瑭宜序諸首。竊惟國家求賢，雖非一途，恒以科目爲重；賢才入官之階，雖非一致，率以科目爲榮。我太祖高皇帝受天景命，奄有萬方，惓惓欲以人文化成天下，詔有司三年一開科取士，重之以選舉，榮之以賓興，期得賢才，以爲化理之本。列聖相承，率由舊典。皇上繼承大統，克篤前烈，而於興賢之典益加慎重，惟欲上當
translation_en:
…those of purest quality were fully recorded for submission to the throne, and it was proposed that I, Tang, should place a preface at the beginning. I humbly reflect that, although the state seeks worthy men through more than one avenue, it consistently gives greatest weight to the examinations; and although talented and worthy men enter official service by various routes, they generally regard advancement through the examinations as an honor.

Our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s great mandate and came to possess all lands. Earnestly desiring to transform the realm through cultural cultivation, he commanded the responsible authorities to hold examinations every three years to select scholars. He accorded them importance through selection for office and honored them through the ceremonial reception and recommendation of worthy men, hoping to obtain men of worth and talent as the foundation of moral transformation and good government. Successive sage emperors followed one another in observing these established institutions. His Majesty has inherited the imperial succession and has faithfully carried forward his predecessors’ illustrious achievements. He exercises still greater care in the institutions for advancing worthy men, desiring only, above, to accord with…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天心下安黎元爲
宗社億萬年靈長之計也猗歟盛
哉廣東嶺南大藩海嶽靈淑
之氣鍾爲俊英百餘年來士
由科目以進昭崇勳揚休烈
卓然爲世名臣者不可稱數
先正有云豪傑之士繇科目
===
而進斯言信矣夫
國家以科目取士以賢才之士
待之也士君子荷
國家之造出而致用求無愧於
科名盍以賢才之士自待乎
爾多士登名薦書行將試禮
闈奉
punctuated:
天心，下安黎元，爲宗社億萬年靈長之計也。猗歟盛哉！廣東，嶺南大藩，海嶽靈淑之氣鍾爲俊英。百餘年來，士由科目以進，昭崇勳，揚休烈，卓然爲世名臣者，不可稱數。先正有云：「豪傑之士繇科目而進。」斯言信矣！
夫國家以科目取士，以賢才之士待之也。士君子荷國家之造，出而致用，求無愧於科名，盍以賢才之士自待乎？爾多士登名薦書，行將試禮闈，奉
translation_en:
…the will of Heaven above and bring peace to the common people below, thereby securing the enduring prosperity of the ancestral temples and altars of state for countless ages. Ah, how magnificent! Guangdong, a great province south of the mountains, gathers the numinous and beneficent energies of seas and peaks into men of outstanding talent. For more than a hundred years, scholars have advanced through the examinations, displayed lofty achievements, and made illustrious their admirable deeds. Those who have distinguished themselves as renowned ministers of their age are beyond counting. A former worthy said, “Men of exceptional ability advance through the examinations.” These words are indeed true!
Now, when the state selects scholars through the examinations, it treats them as men of virtue and talent. You gentlemen, having benefited from the state's nurturing, go forth to put your abilities to use and seek to be worthy of your examination distinction. Should you not hold yourselves to the standards of men of virtue and talent? You assembled scholars, whose names have been entered on the list of recommended candidates, will soon sit the examination at the Ministry of Rites and receive …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廷對而荐陟華要其所以自待
者必賢足以正君而善俗才
足以脩政而立事宏文碩學
足以賛
謀謨而黼黻乎治道爲
上爲德爲下爲民躋斯世於唐虞
三代之盛庶無愧賢才之稱
===
而亦無負
朝廷期待之德意矣其或靜言
而庸違枉己以徇人計而利
禄謀而身家賢才之實漠乎
其無聞則科目之榮且重者
適足以取辱而致輕非士君
子之所以自待也非
punctuated: 廷對，而荐陟華要。其所以自待者，必賢足以正君而善俗，才足以脩政而立事，宏文碩學足以賛謀謨而黼黻乎治道，爲上爲德，爲下爲民，躋斯世於唐虞三代之盛，庶無愧賢才之稱，而亦無負朝廷期待之德意矣。其或靜言而庸違，枉己以徇人，計而利禄，謀而身家，賢才之實漠乎其無聞，則科目之榮且重者，適足以取辱而致輕，非士君子之所以自待也，非
translation_en:
…respond at the Palace Examination and successively rise to distinguished and important posts. The standards you set for yourselves must be such that your virtue suffices to rectify the ruler and improve customs, your ability suffices to put government in order and accomplish affairs, and your outstanding literary accomplishment and profound learning suffice to assist imperial deliberations and lend lustre to the way of governance. In serving those above, work for virtue; in serving those below, work for the people. Raise this age to the flourishing heights of the reigns of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties. Thus you may deserve the designation of men of virtue and talent, and not disappoint the benevolent intentions underlying the court’s expectations.

Should any of you, however, speak agreeably at leisure but act contrary to your words in practice, compromise yourselves to comply with others, scheme for profit and official emoluments, and plan only for yourselves and your households, with no evidence whatever of actual virtue and talent, then the honour and distinction conferred by examination success will serve only to bring disgrace and contempt upon you. This is not how a gentleman should regard his obligations, nor is it …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
朝廷設科取士之初意也亦非
瑭等今日之所顒望也庸序
諸卷首以為多士勗
河南開封府許州儒學學正
朱瑭謹序
punctuated:
朝廷設科取士之初意也，亦非瑭等今日之所顒望也。庸序諸卷首，以為多士勗。
河南開封府許州儒學學正朱瑭謹序。
translation_en:
…the court’s original intention in establishing examinations to recruit officials, nor is it what I, Tang, and my colleagues earnestly hope for today. Accordingly, I have written this preface at the beginning of the volume to encourage the assembled scholars.
Respectfully prefaced by Zhu Tang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.

text:

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
主忠信徙義崇德也
中也者天下之大本也和也者天下之達
道也致中和天地位焉萬物育焉
夫義路也禮門也惟君子能由是路出入
是門也
易
===
應乎天而時行
進得位往有功也進以正可以正邦也其
位剛得中也止而巽動不窮也
以言乎遠則不禦以言乎邇則靜而正
有事而後可大故受之以臨臨者大也物
大然後可觀故受之以觀可觀而後
有所合故受之以噬嗑嗑者合也物
不可以苟合而已故受之以賁
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

主忠信，徙義，崇德也。

中也者，天下之大本也；和也者，天下之達道也。致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉。

夫義，路也；禮，門也。惟君子能由是路，出入是門也。

易

應乎天而時行。

進得位，往有功也。進以正，可以正邦也。其位，剛得中也。止而巽，動不窮也。

以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正。

有事而後可大，故受之以臨。臨者，大也。物大然後可觀，故受之以觀。可觀而後有所合，故受之以噬嗑。嗑者，合也。物不可以苟合而已，故受之以賁。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

To make loyalty and trustworthiness one's guiding principles and to move toward righteousness is to exalt virtue.

Equilibrium is the great foundation of all under Heaven; harmony is the universal Way of all under Heaven. When equilibrium and harmony are fully realized, Heaven and Earth take their proper places, and the myriad things flourish.

Righteousness is the road; ritual propriety is the gate. Only the gentleman can follow this road and pass in and out through this gate.

Book of Changes

Responding to Heaven and acting in accordance with the time.

Advancing and attaining one's position means that going forward brings achievement. Advancing with correctness enables one to set the state right. As for its position, the firm occupies the center. With stillness and yielding, movement is inexhaustible.

Speaking of what is distant, it is without bounds; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct.

Only after there are undertakings can there be greatness; therefore the next hexagram is Approach (Lin). Approach means greatness. Only after things become great can they be viewed; therefore the next hexagram is Viewing (Guan). Only after they can be viewed can there be a joining together; therefore the next hexagram is Biting Through (Shihe). He means joining together. Things cannot merely join together indiscriminately; therefore the next hexagram is Adornment (Bi).

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書
日宣三德夙夜浚明有家日嚴祗敬六德
亮采有邦翕受敷施九德咸事俊乂
在官百僚師師百工惟時撫于五辰
庶績其凝
若虞機張往省括于度則釋
予惟往求朕攸濟敷賁敷前人受命
乃命重黎絕地天通罔有降格羣后之逮
===
在下明明棐常鰥寡無蓋皇帝清問
下民鰥寡有辭于苗德威惟畏德明
惟明乃命三后恤功于民伯夷降典
折民惟刑禹平水土主名山川稷降
播種農殖嘉穀三后成功惟殷于民
士制百姓于刑之中以教祗德
詩
天保定爾以莫不興如山如阜如岡如陵
punctuated:
書

日宣三德，夙夜浚明，有家；日嚴祗敬六德，亮采，有邦。翕受敷施，九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師，百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績其凝。

若虞機張，往省括于度，則釋。

予惟往求朕攸濟，敷賁敷前人受命。

乃命重黎，絕地天通，罔有降格。羣后之逮在下，明明棐常，鰥寡無蓋。皇帝清問下民，鰥寡有辭于苗。德威惟畏，德明惟明。乃命三后，恤功于民。伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以教祗德。

詩

天保定爾，以莫不興。如山如阜，如岡如陵。
translation_en:
Documents (Shu)

One who daily manifests three virtues, discerning them profoundly morning and night, may possess a noble house; one who daily observes six virtues with solemn reverence and conducts affairs faithfully may possess a state. When all are embraced and put into practice, and all nine virtues are employed in service, men of outstanding ability hold office. The hundred officials learn from one another, and all officers attend to their duties in due season. In harmony with the five heavenly periods, their many achievements will be firmly established.

Be like a huntsman with his crossbow drawn: examine whether the arrow is aligned with the mark, and only then release it.

I shall seek the means by which I may accomplish my task, spreading glory and extending the mandate received by my predecessors.

Then he commanded Chong and Li to sever communication between earth and heaven, so that there would be no descending or ascending. The various lords extended their influence below, making enlightened virtue manifest and supporting the enduring norms; the widowers and widows were not left unheard. The august emperor carefully inquired among the common people, and the widowers and widows brought accusations against the Miao. The majesty of virtue alone was to inspire awe; the illumination of virtue alone was to bring enlightenment. He then commanded three lords to labor solicitously for the people. Bo Yi promulgated the statutes, guiding the people through prescribed standards; Yu brought the waters and lands into order and assigned names to the mountains and rivers; Ji taught sowing, and the people cultivated fine grain. The three lords completed their work, bringing abundance to the people. The judicial officer regulated the people through the proper balance of punishments, teaching them to revere virtue.

Odes (Shi)

Heaven protects and establishes you, so that nothing fails to flourish. Like mountains, like hills, like ridges, like great mounds…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
如川之方至以莫不增
鎬京辟廱自西自東自南自北無思不服
皇王烝哉考卜維王宅是鎬京維龜
正之武王成之武王烝哉豐水有芑
武王豈不仕詒厥孫謀以燕翼子武
王烝哉
即有邰家室誕降嘉種維秬維秠維穈維
芑恒之秬秠是穫是畝恒之穈芑是
===
任是負以歸肇祀誕我祀如何或舂
或揄或簸或蹂釋之叟叟烝之浮浮
載謀載惟取蕭祭脂取羝以軷載燔
載烈以興嗣歲卬盛于豆于豆于登
其香始升上帝居歆胡臭亶時后稷
肇祀庶無罪悔以迄于今
我將我享維羊維牛維天其右之
春秋
punctuated:
如川之方至，以莫不增。

鎬京辟廱，自西自東，自南自北，無思不服。皇王烝哉！考卜維王，宅是鎬京。維龜正之，武王成之。武王烝哉！豐水有芑，武王豈不仕？詒厥孫謀，以燕翼子。武王烝哉！

即有邰家室，誕降嘉種，維秬維秠，維穈維芑。恒之秬秠，是穫是畝；恒之穈芑，是任是負，以歸肇祀。誕我祀如何？或舂或揄，或簸或蹂。釋之叟叟，烝之浮浮。載謀載惟，取蕭祭脂，取羝以軷。載燔載烈，以興嗣歲。卬盛于豆，于豆于登。其香始升，上帝居歆。胡臭亶時！后稷肇祀，庶無罪悔，以迄于今。

我將我享，維羊維牛，維天其右之。

春秋
translation_en:
…Like a river whose waters are just arriving, ever increasing.

At the royal ceremonial hall in Haojing, from west and east, from south and north, none failed to submit. How magnificent was the august king! The king examined the divination and settled here in Haojing. The tortoise shell determined the site; King Wu completed it. How magnificent was King Wu! Qi plants grow beside the Feng River. Did King Wu not attend to his duties? He bequeathed plans to his descendants, to bring peace and aid to his children. How magnificent was King Wu!

He settled in Tai and made his home there. Then he bestowed fine seeds: black millet, double-grained black millet, red millet, and white millet. Everywhere he planted the black millet and double-grained black millet; these were harvested and piled in the fields. Everywhere he planted the red millet and white millet; these were carried in their arms and on their backs, brought home to begin the sacrifices. How, then, do we perform our sacrifices? Some pound the grain, some scoop it out; some winnow it, some tread it. They wash it with a rustling sound and steam it until vapour rises. They deliberate and consider, take southernwood to offer with fat, and take a ram for the sacrifice to the road. They roast and broil, to usher in the coming year. We fill the wooden and earthenware offering vessels. As the fragrance begins to rise, the Lord on High takes pleasure in it. How truly timely is that fragrance! Hou Ji began these sacrifices; may we be free of fault and regret, continuing down to the present.

I bring forward my offerings: sheep and oxen. May Heaven accept them.

Spring and Autumn Annals

宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光同盟于雞澤。〔襄公三年〕公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘，同盟于平丘。〔昭公十三年〕

楚人、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男圍宋。公會諸侯盟于宋。〔僖公二十七年〕晉侯侵曹。晉侯伐衛。〔僖公二十八年〕楚子、蔡侯次于厥貉。〔文公〕〔十年〕公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，同盟于新城。〔文公十四年〕晉郤缺帥師伐蔡，戊申，入蔡。〔文公十五年〕晉人執鄭伯。晉欒書帥師伐鄭。〔成公九年〕

禮記

次國之上卿位當大國之中，中當其下，下當其上大夫。小國之上卿位當大國之下卿，中當其上大夫，下當其下大
translation_en:

The senior minister of a small state ranks with the junior minister of a large state; its middle-ranking minister ranks with the latter’s senior grand master, and its junior minister with the latter’s junior grand master…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夫其有中士下士者數各居其上之
三分
德盛而教尊五穀時熟然後賞之以樂
三代之王也必先其令聞
率法而强之資仁者也
第貳塲
論
帝王之治一本於道
===
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢高帝定元功十八人位次詔〔漢高帝六年〕
擬唐以張九齡爲中書侍郎同平章事誥
〔開元二十一年〕
擬宋以唐介參知政事謝表〔熙寧元年〕
判語五條
上言大臣德政
人戶以籍爲定
punctuated:
夫。其有中士、下士者，數各居其上之三分。

第貳塲
論
帝王之治，一本於道。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢高帝定元功十八人位次詔〔漢高帝六年〕。
擬唐以張九齡爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔開元二十一年〕。

判語五條

translation_en:
…grand masters. Where there are middle-ranking and lower-ranking servicemen, their numbers are each one-third those of the rank above.
When virtue flourishes, instruction is honored, and the five grains ripen in season, only then are they rewarded with music.
Those who became kings of the Three Dynasties invariably first established their good reputation.
Those who follow the standards and exert themselves draw upon benevolence.
Second Session
Discourse
The governance of emperors and kings is rooted entirely in the Way.
Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of Emperor Gao of Han establishing the order of precedence of the eighteen foremost meritorious servants. 〔Sixth year of Emperor Gao of Han.〕

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禁止師巫邪術
縱放軍人歇役
詐欺官私取財
第叁塲
策五道
問有善無惡天之命也自古帝王之興體
天致治其勸善懲惡莫不有典法以
詔誥臣民篤尚倫理弼成治化之隆
===
姑舉一二言之若成湯之誕告萬方
成王之訓迪百官其所懲勸攷之於
經槩可見矣洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝大誥三編
太宗文皇帝為善陰隲孝順事實
宣宗章皇帝五倫一書嘉惠臣民至精至悉盖
與商周之君異世而同心也
punctuated:
禁止師巫邪術。
縱放軍人歇役。
詐欺官私取財。

第叁塲
策五道

問：有善無惡，天之命也。自古帝王之興，體天致治，其勸善懲惡，莫不有典法，以詔誥臣民，篤尚倫理，弼成治化之隆。姑舉一二言之，若成湯之誕告萬方、成王之訓迪百官，其所懲勸，攷之於經，槩可見矣。洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》，宣宗章皇帝《五倫》一書，嘉惠臣民，至精至悉，盖與商周之君異世而同心也。
translation_en:
Prohibiting the illicit arts of shamans and spirit mediums.
Allowing military personnel to evade service.
Obtaining public or private property by fraud.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: That there should be goodness and no evil is Heaven’s command. From antiquity, when emperors and kings arose, they patterned themselves on Heaven to establish good government. In encouraging goodness and punishing evil, all had authoritative statutes and regulations through which they issued proclamations to their officials and people, earnestly upheld ethical relationships, and helped bring government and moral transformation to flourishing perfection.

To cite just one or two examples: Cheng Tang proclaimed widely to the myriad regions, and King Cheng instructed and guided the hundred officials. What they punished and encouraged can be broadly discerned by examining the Classics. We reverently reflect upon our dynasty’s August Emperor Taizu Gao and his three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao); Emperor Taizong Wen and his Doing Good and Hidden Blessings (Weishan Yinzhi) and True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi); and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang and his book, The Five Relationships (Wulun). These bestowed gracious benefits upon officials and people with the utmost refinement and thoroughness. Though they lived in different ages from the rulers of Shang and Zhou, they surely shared the same intentions.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
三聖之書其間懲勸之條凡幾見而其旨之同
於湯之誕告成王之訓迪果安在哉
方今
聖天子在上治教休明普天率土相安於皥皥
之天善有勸而惡有懲迹其所自皆
聖學緝熙率由舊典之明驗也斯世斯民何其
幸歟諸士子博古通今願詳著于篇
以觀膺
===
聖訓之功
問諸史浩瀚固難以一二議也今姑舉司
馬遷班固二家言之或謂固優於遷
或謂遷優於固然不能無可疑者甞
即其書觀之遷曰天官固曰天文遷
曰河渠固曰溝洫遷之封禪而固以
郊祀易之遷之食貨而固以平準更
之遷爲十表八書固志五行地里而
punctuated:
三聖之書，其間懲勸之條凡幾見，而其旨之同於湯之誕告、成王之訓迪，果安在哉？方今聖天子在上，治教休明，普天率土，相安於皥皥之天。善有勸而惡有懲，迹其所自，皆聖學緝熙、率由舊典之明驗也。斯世斯民，何其幸歟！諸士子博古通今，願詳著于篇，以觀膺聖訓之功。

問：諸史浩瀚，固難以一二議也。今姑舉司馬遷、班固二家言之。或謂固優於遷，或謂遷優於固，然不能無可疑者。甞即其書觀之，遷曰《天官》，固曰《天文》；遷曰《河渠》，固曰《溝洫》；遷之《封禪》，而固以《郊祀》易之；遷之《食貨》，而固以《平準》更之；遷爲十表八書，固志五行、地里，而
translation_en:
In the books of the three sage emperors, how many provisions for admonition and encouragement occur, and precisely wherein does their purport accord with Tang’s proclamation to the myriad regions and King Cheng’s instruction of the officials? Today the sagely Son of Heaven reigns above us; government and moral instruction are excellent and enlightened, and throughout all the land under Heaven people live together peacefully beneath a serene sky. Goodness receives encouragement and evil punishment. Tracing these effects to their source, we find clear evidence everywhere of His Majesty’s ever more luminous sagely learning and adherence to established precedents. How fortunate are this age and its people! You candidates possess broad knowledge of antiquity and understand the present. Please set forth your views fully in writing, so that we may observe the fruits of your reception of the imperial teachings.

Question: The histories are vast; certainly they cannot readily be discussed in a few words. For now, let us consider just the two historians Sima Qian and Ban Gu. Some say that Gu surpasses Qian; others that Qian surpasses Gu. Yet there remain points open to doubt. On examining their books, we find that Qian calls one treatise “Celestial Offices,” while Gu calls his “Astronomy”; Qian uses “Rivers and Canals,” while Gu uses “Ditches and Channels.” Gu replaces Qian’s “Feng and Shan Sacrifices” with “Suburban Sacrifices,” and Qian’s “Food and Money” with “Price Equalization” [?—the attribution of these last two titles appears reversed]. Qian composed ten tables and eight treatises, while Gu wrote treatises on the Five Phases and geography, and…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其書之同異若此豈無優劣之可議
歟遷序三千年事僅五十萬言固叙
二百年事已餘八十萬言遷傳循吏
止五人固傳循吏六人而其書之繁
簡若此亦豈無優劣之可言歟或又
謂遷有二失固有二得又謂遷固易
地而處本無優劣是果至當之評歟
諸生博學待問久矣其於二史優劣
===
必有定論願以語我
問格物窮理學者事也試舉天地萬物而
質之可乎夫天覆地載天地何依附
歟日照月臨日月何主宰歟日月運
行何周天有遲速之異四時錯行何
四仲有分至之殊天左旋矣日月麗
天何為乎右行日常盈矣月受日光
何為乎有虧同一陰陽也何以分大
punctuated:
其書之同異若此，豈無優劣之可議歟？遷序三千年事，僅五十萬言；固叙二百年事，已餘八十萬言。遷傳循吏止五人，固傳循吏六人，而其書之繁簡若此，亦豈無優劣之可言歟？或又謂遷有二失，固有二得；又謂遷固易地而處，本無優劣。是果至當之評歟？諸生博學待問久矣，其於二史優劣，必有定論，願以語我。
問：格物窮理，學者事也。試舉天地萬物而質之，可乎？夫天覆地載，天地何依附歟？日照月臨，日月何主宰歟？日月運行，何周天有遲速之異？四時錯行，何四仲有分至之殊？天左旋矣，日月麗天，何為乎右行？日常盈矣，月受日光，何為乎有虧？同一陰陽也，何以分大
translation_en:
…With such similarities and differences between their works, is there no room to discuss their relative merits? Sima Qian recounts three thousand years of events in only five hundred thousand words; Ban Gu recounts two hundred years of events in more than eight hundred thousand words. Sima Qian includes biographies of only five exemplary officials, while Ban Gu includes biographies of six. With such differences in the fullness and brevity of their works, is there likewise no room to speak of their relative merits? Some further say that Sima Qian had two failings and Ban Gu two strengths; others say that, had Sima Qian and Ban Gu exchanged circumstances, neither would have been superior or inferior. Are these truly the most fitting judgments? You candidates have studied widely and long stood ready to be questioned. You must have reached a settled judgment on the relative merits of these two histories, and I hope you will tell me.
Question: Investigating things and fathoming principles are the scholar’s business. May we put this to the test by considering Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things? Heaven covers and Earth bears, but on what do Heaven and Earth depend? The sun shines and the moon looks down, but what governs the sun and moon? As the sun and moon move, why do they differ in the speed with which they complete a circuit of the heavens? As the four seasons proceed in succession, why are the equinoxes and solstices distinguished among the middle months of the four seasons? Heaven turns to the left; why do the sun and moon, attached to Heaven, move to the right? The sun is always full; since the moon receives the sun’s light, why does it wane? Yin and yang are the same throughout; why distinguish greater…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
少勻一閏位也何以置又近日長日
短何稽生明生魄何主南極何常隱
而不見北極何常見而不隱月受日
光似矣中間黑者何物歟雷無形像
信矣聲之震霆何物歟風雨霜露自
何成歟烟雲霾霧自何起歟風土一
也西北多寒東南多暖何歟人品一
也西□多强東南多弱何歟禽蟲之
===
鳴伏□化何為有時草木之榮悴開
落何為有節潛者不能飛何神龍或
潛而或飛生者皆有種何麟鳳無種
而亦生有角皆能觸麒麟何以角端
有肉獸皆食生物騶虞何以不食生
物石入水則沉地在水中何不沉歟
器載滿則溢水歸滄海何不溢歟海
潮乘子胥之怒然歟黃河自天上而
punctuated: 少？勻一閏位也，何以置？又近日長日短，何稽？生明生魄，何主？南極何常隱而不見，北極何常見而不隱？月受日光似矣，中間黑者何物歟？雷無形像信矣，聲之震霆何物歟？風雨霜露自何成歟？烟雲霾霧自何起歟？風土一也，西北多寒，東南多暖，何歟？人品一也，西□多强，東南多弱，何歟？禽蟲之鳴伏□化，何為有時？草木之榮悴開落，何為有節？潛者不能飛，何神龍或潛而或飛？生者皆有種，何麟鳳無種而亦生？有角皆能觸，麒麟何以角端有肉？獸皆食生物，騶虞何以不食生物？石入水則沉，地在水中何不沉歟？器載滿則溢，水歸滄海何不溢歟？海潮乘子胥之怒，然歟？黃河自天上而
translation_en: …and lesser? As for the placement of intercalation [?], how is it determined? Further, how are the lengths of long and short days ascertained [?]? What governs the emergence of the moon’s light and its dark portion? Why is the southern celestial pole always hidden from view, while the northern celestial pole is always visible and never hidden? It seems plausible that the moon receives the sun’s light, but what is the dark matter within it? It is indeed true that thunder has no visible form, but what produces its crashing sound? From what are wind, rain, frost, and dew formed? From what do smoke, clouds, haze, and fog arise? The natural environment is alike: why is the northwest mostly cold and the southeast mostly warm? Human nature is alike: why are people in the west □ mostly strong, while those in the southeast are mostly weak? Why do the calls, dormancy, and □ transformations of birds and insects occur at particular times [?]? Why do the flourishing and withering, flowering and falling of plants have their seasons? Creatures that dwell underwater cannot fly; why can divine dragons sometimes remain submerged and sometimes fly? All living creatures come from breeding stock; why do qilin and phoenixes appear even without breeding stock? All horned creatures can gore; why do qilin have flesh at the tips of their horns? Beasts all eat living things; why does the zouyu not eat living things? A stone sinks when put into water; why does the earth, situated amid water, not sink? A vessel overflows when filled; why does the sea not overflow when waters flow into it? Is it true that the sea’s tides ride upon the anger of Zixu? Does the Yellow River, from heaven above …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
來信歟此皆諸生耳目所見聞必講
究之有素矣請吐胸中之蘊以觀格
物之學
問民惟邦本本固邦寧古聖王之治天下
非有異常絕特之事其所謂仁政者
不過省刑罰薄稅斂二者而已以固
邦國之本以結天下之心此其要歟
仁政之化民夫豈微哉因天討而作
五刑糾邦國以叙八刑明一成而不
變也又有赦過肆眚議獄緩死於義
何在辨五物而制地征則三壤而成
田賦明一定不可輕重也又有散利
薄征弛力舍禁其要奚從虞周之制
刑無容議矣或謂王者任德不任刑
刑其可偏廢歟禹貢之為法無間然
矣或謂治地莫不善於貢弊若是其
punctuated:
來，信歟？此皆諸生耳目所見聞，必講究之有素矣。請吐胸中之蘊，以觀格物之學。

問：民惟邦本，本固邦寧。古聖王之治天下，非有異常絕特之事，其所謂仁政者，不過省刑罰、薄稅斂二者而已。以固邦國之本，以結天下之心，此其要歟？仁政之化民，夫豈微哉？因天討而作五刑，糾邦國以叙八刑，明一成而不變也。又有赦過肆眚、議獄緩死，於義何在？辨五物而制地征，則三壤而成田賦，明一定不可輕重也。又有散利薄征、弛力舍禁，其要奚從？虞周之制刑，無容議矣。或謂王者任德不任刑，刑其可偏廢歟？禹貢之為法，無間然矣。或謂治地莫不善於貢，弊若是其
translation_en:
…comes from heaven—is this credible? These are all things that you candidates have seen or heard, and surely you have long studied and investigated them. Please set forth what you have stored in your minds, so that we may observe your learning in the investigation of things.

Question: The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is at peace. In governing the realm, the sage kings of antiquity did nothing extraordinary or exceptional. What they called benevolent government amounted simply to two things: reducing punishments and lightening taxation. Were these not the essentials for securing the foundation of the state and winning the hearts of all under heaven? How could benevolent government have only a slight influence in transforming the people?

The five punishments were established in accordance with Heaven’s chastisement, and the eight categories of punishment were arranged to correct the states. Clearly, once established, these were not to change. Yet there were also provisions for pardoning faults and forgiving inadvertent offenses, deliberating on criminal cases and delaying executions. What principle underlies these measures? The five kinds of land and their products were distinguished to determine land levies, and the three grades of soil served as the standard for establishing field taxes. Clearly, once fixed, these assessments were not to be made lighter or heavier. Yet there were also provisions for distributing benefits and reducing levies, relaxing labor obligations and lifting prohibitions. What essential principle should be followed?

The penal institutions of Yu and Zhou surely admit of no criticism. Yet some say that a true king relies on virtue, not punishment. Can punishment then be dispensed with altogether? The Tribute of Yu provides a system beyond reproach. Yet some say that, in administering the land, no system is worse than the tribute system. Could its abuses be so…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
甚歟今律令非不明也有司按四方
之罪非少怠也宜天下無不化之民
矣然刑罰未盡清而民心未盡服者
抑何故耶貢賦非無常制也
朝廷寬恤之典非不屢下也宜海內無不獲
之夫矣然賦斂未盡平而民心未盡
安者豈無自耶伊欲獄孚於下而民
不寃賦供於上而民不擾行何道而
===
可願聞所以折衷
問兵戎有國之大事學者所當講也夫用
兵有法而法昉於何時禦敵有戰而
戰始於何人若太公之六韜黃石公
之三畧所宜知也若孔明之八陣司
馬之一成所當識也有曰伐曰侵曰
戰曰圍曰入曰遷可詳其事議得失
歟有曰敗曰取曰襲曰追曰戍曰以
punctuated:
甚歟？今律令非不明也，有司按四方之罪非少怠也，宜天下無不化之民矣。然刑罰未盡清，而民心未盡服者，抑何故耶？貢賦非無常制也，朝廷寬恤之典非不屢下也，宜海內無不獲之夫矣。然賦斂未盡平，而民心未盡安者，豈無自耶？伊欲獄孚於下而民不寃，賦供於上而民不擾，行何道而可？願聞所以折衷。
問：兵戎，有國之大事，學者所當講也。夫用兵有法，而法昉於何時？禦敵有戰，而戰始於何人？若太公之《六韜》、黃石公之《三畧》，所宜知也；若孔明之八陣、司馬之一成，所當識也。有曰伐、曰侵、曰戰、曰圍、曰入、曰遷，可詳其事、議得失歟？有曰敗、曰取、曰襲、曰追、曰戍、曰以，
translation_en:
…so severe? Today the statutes and ordinances are certainly clear, and the responsible officials are by no means remiss in investigating offenses throughout the realm [?]. It would seem that no one under Heaven should remain untransformed. Yet punishments are not yet entirely just, and the people's hearts are not yet fully won over. Why is this? Tribute and taxation certainly have established regulations, and the court has repeatedly issued measures of leniency and relief. It would seem that everyone within the seas should enjoy their benefits. Yet the burdens of taxation are not yet entirely equitable, and the people's hearts are not yet wholly at ease. Surely this has a cause? If we wish judicial decisions to command confidence among those below, so that the people suffer no injustice, and taxes to be supplied to those above, so that the people suffer no disturbance, what course should we follow? We would like to hear how these considerations may be duly reconciled.
Question: Military affairs are a great concern of any state and a subject that scholars ought to study. There are methods for employing troops: when did these methods originate? There is battle to resist an enemy: with whom did battle begin? Works such as Taigong's Six Secret Teachings and Huangshi Gong's Three Strategies ought to be known; formations such as Kongming's Eight Formations and Sima's “single formation” [?] ought to be understood. There are actions termed punitive expedition, invasion, battle, siege, entry, and relocation. Can you explain the events in detail and discuss their successes and failures? There are also terms such as defeat, capture, surprise attack, pursuit, garrisoning, and leading troops (yi) [?]…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
可悉其目别是非歟古之帝王有七
旬而苗來格者有一怒而安天下者
用何兵法而然昔之將帥有八戰八
克者有七擒七縱者以何兵法而能
夫兵法之善莫備於孫武子本義始
計有曰經之以五事其事可指陳歟
謀攻有曰知勝有五其勝可歷言歟
軍形有曰度量數稱勝其意安在兵
===
勢有曰五聲五色五味其事何居將
通九變之利者知用兵與將有五危
者孰得地形六者地之道將不可不
察與六者非天地之災將之過孰失
犯三軍之衆若使一人與并敵一向
千里殺將者孰優始如處女敵人開
戶與戰勝攻取不脩其功者孰劣火
攻有五以何爲先用間有五以何爲
punctuated: 可悉其目，别是非歟？古之帝王，有七旬而苗來格者，有一怒而安天下者，用何兵法而然？昔之將帥，有八戰八克者，有七擒七縱者，以何兵法而能？夫兵法之善，莫備於《孫武子本義》。《始計》有曰：「經之以五事。」其事可指陳歟？《謀攻》有曰：「知勝有五。」其勝可歷言歟？《軍形》有曰：「度量數稱勝。」其意安在？《兵勢》有曰：「五聲五色五味。」其事何居？「將通九變之利者，知用兵」與「將有五危」者，孰得？「地形六者，地之道，將不可不察」與「六者非天地之災，將之過」，孰失？「犯三軍之衆，若使一人」與「并敵一向，千里殺將」者，孰優？「始如處女，敵人開戶」與「戰勝攻取，不脩其功」者，孰劣？火攻有五，以何爲先？用間有五，以何爲
translation_en:
…Can you enumerate all these categories and distinguish right from wrong? Among the emperors and kings of antiquity, there was one to whom the Miao came in submission after seventy days, and one who, in a single outburst of wrath, brought peace to all under Heaven. By what methods of warfare did they accomplish this? Among the commanders of former times, there was one who fought eight battles and won all eight, and one who captured and released his opponent seven times. Through what methods of warfare were they able to do so?

Nowhere are excellent methods of warfare more fully set forth than in The Original Meaning of Master Sun Wu (Sun Wuzi benyi). The chapter “Initial Calculations” says: “Assess it by means of five matters.” Can you identify and explain these matters? “Planning an Attack” says: “There are five ways to know victory.” Can you explain each of these? “Military Dispositions” speaks of “measurement, estimation, calculation, weighing, and victory.” What does this mean? “Military Strategic Power” speaks of “the five notes, the five colors, and the five flavors.” What is the significance of these? Compare “The commander who understands the advantages of the nine variations knows how to employ troops” with “There are five dangers for a commander”: which exemplifies sound practice? Compare “The six types of terrain are the principles governing the ground, which a commander must examine” with “These six are not calamities caused by Heaven and Earth, but faults of the commander”: where does the fault lie? Compare “Directing [?] the multitude of the three armies as though employing a single man” with “Concentrating against the enemy in one direction and killing his commander a thousand li away”: which is superior? Compare “At first be like a maiden, so that the enemy opens his door” with “Winning battles and taking objectives, yet failing to consolidate those achievements”: which is inferior? There are five forms of attack by fire: which should take precedence? There are five kinds of employment of spies: which is to be considered…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
最夫兵貴速不貴久興師十萬日費
千金是尚拙速不尚巧遲也且如廣
之瀧水猺蠻為患久矣渠魁近已授
首餘孽尚多潛遁今欲拙速耶則彼
巢穴險阻急莫能進將欲巧遲耶則
彼剽掠不息事不可緩欲以古人兵
法治之不知何法為善諸士子生長
是鄉必有定見明以告我毋曰軍旅
===
之事非之學也
punctuated: 最？夫兵貴速，不貴久。興師十萬，日費千金，是尚拙速，不尚巧遲也。且如廣之瀧水猺蠻為患久矣，渠魁近已授首，餘孽尚多潛遁。今欲拙速耶，則彼巢穴險阻，急莫能進；將欲巧遲耶，則彼剽掠不息，事不可緩。欲以古人兵法治之，不知何法為善。諸士子生長是鄉，必有定見，明以告我，毋曰：「軍旅之事，非之學也。」
translation_en: …is best? In warfare, speed is prized, not protraction. To mobilize an army of a hundred thousand costs a thousand pieces of gold each day. Thus clumsy swiftness is preferred to skillful delay. Take, for example, the Yao tribespeople of Longshui in Guangdong, who have long caused trouble. Their ringleaders have recently been beheaded, but many remaining followers are still hiding or fleeing. If we now seek clumsy swiftness, their strongholds lie amid difficult and dangerous terrain, where a hasty advance is impossible. If we seek skillful delay, their plundering continues unabated, and action cannot be postponed. We wish to deal with them through the military methods of the ancients, but do not know which method would be best. You candidates were born and raised in this region and must have considered views. Explain them clearly to me, and do not say: “Military affairs are not what we have studied [?].”

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
四書
主忠信徙義崇德也
張紹齡
同考試官訓導左批德不外於仁義禮知作
者多不知此惟此篇得之是用錄出
考試官敎諭鄭批發揮明白足見作手
考試官學正朱批非得身心體驗之真者不
能到此錄之
===
實其心而宜其事此所以崇德也蓋主忠信則
存於心者無不實徙義則見於事者無不宜德
之崇也夫豈外於此哉聖人因子張問崇德而
告之以此蓋謂忠信所以進德也人不忠信則
事皆無實德無自而進矣是故曰仁曰義必實
心以體之使仁義之存於心者無一息之虚假
焉曰禮曰智必實心以存之俾禮智之具乎內
者無一毫之偽妄焉然心之實也固爲進德之
punctuated:
四書

主忠信，徙義，崇德也。

張紹齡

同考試官訓導左批：德不外於仁義禮知，作者多不知此，惟此篇得之，是用錄出。

考試官敎諭鄭批：發揮明白，足見作手。

考試官學正朱批：非得身心體驗之真者，不能到此，錄之。

實其心而宜其事，此所以崇德也。蓋主忠信，則存於心者無不實；徙義，則見於事者無不宜。德之崇也，夫豈外於此哉？聖人因子張問崇德而告之以此，蓋謂忠信所以進德也。人不忠信，則事皆無實，德無自而進矣。是故曰仁曰義，必實心以體之，使仁義之存於心者無一息之虚假焉；曰禮曰智，必實心以存之，俾禮智之具乎內者無一毫之偽妄焉。然心之實也，固爲進德之
translation_en:
Four Books

“Make loyalty and trustworthiness your guiding principles, and move toward righteousness: this is how to exalt virtue.”

Zhang Shaoling

Comment by Associate Examiner Zuo, Assistant Instructor: “Virtue does not lie outside benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom. Most writers do not understand this; this essay alone grasps it. For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The exposition is clear and lucid, amply demonstrating the writer’s skill.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Without genuine understanding gained through personal experience in body and mind, one could not attain this level. Include it.”

To make one’s heart sincere and one’s actions fitting: this is how to exalt virtue. For when loyalty and trustworthiness are one’s guiding principles, everything harbored in the heart is sincere; when one moves toward righteousness, everything manifested in action is fitting. Could the exaltation of virtue lie anywhere outside this? When Zizhang asked about exalting virtue, the Sage instructed him in these terms. His meaning was that loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue. If a person lacks loyalty and trustworthiness, all his undertakings lack substance, and his virtue has no means of advancing.

Thus, in speaking of benevolence and righteousness, one must embody them with a sincere heart, so that benevolence and righteousness as they abide in the heart are free of falsity for even a single instant. In speaking of ritual propriety and wisdom, one must preserve them with a sincere heart, so that ritual propriety and wisdom as they are possessed within are free of even the slightest trace of deceit or falsehood. Yet sincerity of heart is indeed the … of advancing virtue …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
本而不徙義則專於内而遺乎外進德之功不
有所乎故日用之間發於心而見於事者或有
未仁未義也必勇以遷之使事事合乎仁而當
乎義焉云為之際由乎中而應乎外者一有未
禮未智也必速以改之但事事循乎禮而周乎
智焉夫内主忠信則心無不誠而本立矣外徙
於義則事無不善而日新矣内外之功交致進
脩之道兩全則仁義之得於己者日備而罔覺
===
禮智之萃於身者日進而無疆孰謂崇德不本
於主忠信徙義也哉大抵子張才高意廣務外
少誠聖人於此既告之以主忠信徙義矣他日
問行則又以忠信篤敬告之皆所以因其失而
教之使之誠善補過以成其德也然忠信徙義
雖所以為子張告實所以示君子造道之門入
德之要也此又非特為子張也此所以為聖人
之言也
punctuated: 本，而不徙義，則專於内而遺乎外，進德之功不有所乎？故日用之間，發於心而見於事者，或有未仁未義也，必勇以遷之，使事事合乎仁而當乎義焉。云為之際，由乎中而應乎外者，一有未禮未智也，必速以改之，但事事循乎禮而周乎智焉。夫内主忠信，則心無不誠而本立矣；外徙於義，則事無不善而日新矣。内外之功交致，進脩之道兩全，則仁義之得於己者日備而罔覺，禮智之萃於身者日進而無疆。孰謂崇德不本於主忠信、徙義也哉？大抵子張才高意廣，務外少誠。聖人於此既告之以主忠信、徙義矣，他日問行，則又以忠信篤敬告之，皆所以因其失而教之，使之誠善補過，以成其德也。然忠信徙義，雖所以為子張告，實所以示君子造道之門、入德之要也。此又非特為子張也，此所以為聖人之言也。
translation_en:
…the foundation; yet if one does not turn toward righteousness, one concentrates on the inner and neglects the outer. Would this not impair the work of advancing virtue [?]? Thus, in daily life, whenever what arises in the heart and manifests itself in action falls short of benevolence or righteousness, one must courageously change it, making every action accord with benevolence and conform to righteousness. In speech and action, whenever what proceeds from within and responds to things outside falls short of ritual propriety or wisdom, one must promptly correct it, so that every action follows ritual propriety and fully accords with wisdom.

When one inwardly makes loyalty and trustworthiness one's guiding principles, the heart is wholly sincere and the foundation is established. When one outwardly turns toward righteousness, one's actions are wholly good and renewed each day. When inward and outward effort are both fully exerted, and both aspects of self-cultivation are perfected, the benevolence and righteousness attained within oneself grow more complete each day without one's noticing, while the ritual propriety and wisdom gathered in one's person advance daily without limit. Who could say that exalting virtue is not rooted in making loyalty and trustworthiness one's guiding principles and turning toward righteousness?

Generally speaking, Zizhang possessed great talent and broad aspirations, but devoted himself to externals and lacked sincerity. Here the Sage had already instructed him to make loyalty and trustworthiness his guiding principles and turn toward righteousness. On another occasion, when he asked about conduct, the Sage again instructed him in loyalty, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence. These teachings all addressed his failings, enabling him to make his goodness sincere and remedy his faults, thereby perfecting his virtue. Yet although the teaching on loyalty, trustworthiness, and turning toward righteousness was addressed to Zizhang, it actually shows gentlemen the gateway to attaining the Way and the essentials of entering into virtue. It was therefore not solely for Zizhang. This is what makes it the word of a sage.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
中也者天下之大本也和也者天下之達
道也致中和天地位焉萬物育焉
何應潮
同考試官訓導王批此作始終以心立說最是且
辭簡理明故錄之
考試官敎諭鄭批體認真切
考試官學正朱批辭足以發理
中庸論心該乎道之體用推而極之則其效大
===
矣夫道之體用不外乎中和而一心有以該之
也苟能加夫推極之功則位育之效不其大歟
昔子思推本天命之性以明由敎而入者謂夫
人之一心性情具焉彼性之渾然在中而無所
偏倚謂之中也中而曰天下之大本于以見中
即天命之性而天下之理皆由是出乃道之體
而心之所該者焉情之發皆中節而無所乖戾
謂之和也和而曰天下之達道于以見和即循
punctuated:
中也者，天下之大本也；和也者，天下之達道也。致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉。
何應潮
同考試官訓導王批：此作始終以心立說，最是；且辭簡理明，故錄之。
考試官敎諭鄭批：體認真切。
考試官學正朱批：辭足以發理。
中庸論心，該乎道之體用，推而極之，則其效大矣。夫道之體用不外乎中和，而一心有以該之也。苟能加夫推極之功，則位育之效不其大歟？昔子思推本天命之性，以明由敎而入者，謂夫人之一心，性情具焉。彼性之渾然在中而無所偏倚，謂之中也。中而曰天下之大本，于以見中即天命之性，而天下之理皆由是出，乃道之體而心之所該者焉。情之發皆中節而無所乖戾，謂之和也。和而曰天下之達道，于以見和即循
translation_en:
“Equilibrium is the great foundation of all under Heaven; harmony is the universally followed Way of all under Heaven. Bring equilibrium and harmony to their utmost, and Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things flourish.”

He Yingchao

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: This composition bases its argument throughout on the mind, which is entirely right. Moreover, its language is concise and its principles clear; hence its inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Its understanding is genuine and penetrating.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Its language adequately elucidates the principles.

The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the mind as encompassing the substance and functioning of the Way. When these are extended to their utmost, the effects are great indeed. The substance and functioning of the Way do not extend beyond equilibrium and harmony, and the single mind encompasses them. If one applies the effort of extending them to their utmost, will not the effects—Heaven and Earth taking their proper places and all things flourishing—be great?

Formerly, Zisi traced things back to the nature conferred by Heaven to explain how one enters through instruction. His meaning was that within a person's single mind, both nature and feelings are present. When that nature remains undivided within, without any leaning or deviation, this is called equilibrium. Calling equilibrium “the great foundation of all under Heaven” shows that equilibrium is precisely the nature conferred by Heaven, and that all the principles under Heaven issue from it. It is the substance of the Way, encompassed by the mind. When the feelings, as they arise, all attain due measure without discord or deviation, this is called harmony. Calling harmony “the universally followed Way of all under Heaven” shows that harmony is precisely following…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
性之謂而天下古今之所共由乃道之用而心
之所統者焉夫道之具於人心者其體用之全
本皆如此然靜而不知所以存之則天理昧而
大本有所不立苟能自戒懼而約之以至於至
靜之中無所偏倚而其守不失則有以極其中
而大本之立益以固矣動而不知所以節之則
人欲肆而達道有所不行苟能自謹獨而精之
以至於應物之處無少差謬而無適不然則有
===
以極其和而達道之行益以廣矣夫靜而無一
息之不中則吾心正而天地之心亦正故陰陽
動靜各止其所天地不於此而位乎動而無一
事之不和則吾氣順而天地之氣亦順故充塞
無間驩欣交通萬物不於此而育乎吁始之所
發端終之所至極其皆不外於吾心也如是彼
由教而入者惡可外心以求道乎抑觀中庸此
章首明道之本原出於天而不可易其實體備
punctuated: 性之謂，而天下古今之所共由，乃道之用，而心之所統者焉。夫道之具於人心者，其體用之全，本皆如此。然靜而不知所以存之，則天理昧而大本有所不立。苟能自戒懼而約之，以至於至靜之中無所偏倚，而其守不失，則有以極其中，而大本之立益以固矣。動而不知所以節之，則人欲肆而達道有所不行。苟能自謹獨而精之，以至於應物之處無少差謬，而無適不然，則有以極其和，而達道之行益以廣矣。夫靜而無一息之不中，則吾心正而天地之心亦正，故陰陽動靜各止其所，天地不於此而位乎？動而無一事之不和，則吾氣順而天地之氣亦順，故充塞無間，驩欣交通，萬物不於此而育乎？吁！始之所發端，終之所至極，其皆不外於吾心也如是。彼由教而入者，惡可外心以求道乎？抑觀《中庸》此章，首明道之本原出於天而不可易，其實體備
translation_en:
…following one’s nature: it is what all under Heaven, past and present, follow in common. It is the functioning of the Way, governed by the heart-mind. Such, fundamentally, is the completeness of the substance and functioning of the Way as it resides in the human heart-mind. Yet if, in stillness, one does not know how to preserve it, Heaven’s principle becomes obscured, and the great foundation is not fully established. If one can begin with vigilance and apprehension and thereby gather oneself inward, reaching the point where, in utmost stillness, there is no deviation or leaning and one never fails to maintain this state, then one can bring equilibrium to its fullest extent, and the great foundation will stand ever more firmly. If, in activity, one does not know how to regulate it, human desires run unchecked, and the universally followed Way is not fully put into practice. If one can begin with watchfulness when alone and refine this practice, reaching the point where one responds to things without the slightest error, wherever one may be, then one can bring harmony to its fullest extent, and the practice of the universally followed Way will extend ever more widely.

If, in stillness, there is not a single moment without equilibrium, then my heart-mind is upright, and the heart-mind of Heaven and Earth is likewise upright. Thus yin and yang, movement and stillness, each rest in their proper place. Is it not through this that Heaven and Earth take their proper positions? If, in activity, there is not a single affair without harmony, then my vital energy flows smoothly, and the vital energy of Heaven and Earth likewise flows smoothly. Thus it fills all space without a gap, joyfully intermingling and circulating. Is it not through this that the myriad things are nourished? Ah! From the initial beginning to the ultimate culmination, everything remains within my own heart-mind in this way. How could those who enter through instruction seek the Way outside the heart-mind? Furthermore, consider this chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean: it first makes clear that the Way’s original source comes from Heaven and cannot be altered, and that its substantial reality is fully present …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於己而不可離次言存養省察之要終言聖神
功化之極然聖神功化之極固有非始學所當
議者而射者之的行者之歸亦學者立志之初
所當知也吁旨哉
夫義路也禮門也惟君子能由是路出入
是門也
謝慶
同考試官教諭黃批順題說理文氣自充無
===
如此篇
考試官教諭鄭批詞達不冗
考試官學正宋批得孟子立言之旨
道之在人為甚切人之賢者為能踐夫義為路
而禮為門道之切於人也尚矣求其能踐之者
其惟君子乎且夫事之合於宜者義也人之出
處去就必惟義是從而不可離義非在人共由
之路乎理之中乎節者禮也人之進退行藏必
punctuated:
於己而不可離。次言存養省察之要，終言聖神功化之極。然聖神功化之極，固有非始學所當議者，而射者之的、行者之歸，亦學者立志之初所當知也。吁，旨哉！
夫義，路也；禮，門也。惟君子能由是路，出入是門也。
謝慶
同考試官教諭黃批：順題說理，文氣自充，無如此篇。
考試官教諭鄭批：詞達不冗。
考試官學正宋批：得孟子立言之旨。
道之在人為甚切，人之賢者為能踐。夫義為路，而禮為門，道之切於人也尚矣。求其能踐之者，其惟君子乎？且夫事之合於宜者，義也。人之出處去就，必惟義是從，而不可離，義非在人共由之路乎？理之中乎節者，禮也。人之進退行藏，必
translation_en:
…within oneself and cannot be departed from. Next, it explains the essentials of preserving and nurturing the mind and of examining oneself; finally, it speaks of the utmost achievements and transforming influence of sages and spirits. These supreme achievements and transforming influence admittedly include matters that beginners ought not yet to discuss. Yet the archer’s target and the traveler’s destination are also things that learners should know when first setting their resolve. Ah, how profound!
“Righteousness is the road; ritual propriety is the gate. Only the gentleman can follow this road and pass in and out through this gate.”
Xie Qing 謝慶
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The exposition of principle follows the topic, and the prose naturally has fullness of vigor; no other piece is like this one [?].”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The wording conveys the meaning without verbosity.”
Comment by Examiner Song, School Instructor: “It grasps the intent behind Mencius’s words.”
The Way is intimately bound up with human life, and it is the worthy who can put it into practice. Righteousness is the road, and ritual propriety is the gate: the Way’s intimate relevance to human life is indeed great. If we seek those capable of practicing it, are they not precisely gentlemen? Now, righteousness means that affairs accord with what is fitting. Whether entering office or remaining in retirement, leaving a position or accepting one, people must follow righteousness alone and never depart from it. Is righteousness not the road that all people alike should follow? Ritual propriety is principle conforming to its proper measure. Whether advancing or withdrawing, acting publicly or remaining in obscurity, people must…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
惟禮是循而不可舍禮非在人出入之門乎夫
義路禮門乃道之切於人者如此苟非君子之
人則不能由是路而出入是門矣彼若庶人召
之役則往役者非徇人也義之宜然也君子知
乎此而守身以義故往役而不往見其所以由
是路也豈衆人所可能哉不傳贄爲臣則不見
諸侯非傲上也禮之當然也君子明乎此而律
身以禮故不爲臣則不敢往見其所以出入是
===
門也豈常人所能及哉吁義路禮門固君子之
所以自處者亦人君之所以處乎賢者也苟見
賢而不以是道是欲其入而閉其門塞其路矣
賢豈爲吾用哉嗟夫戰國之士朝叩秦關暮遊
燕璧不待人君之召而衒玉求售者比比皆然
禮義漠然也孟子以命世亞聖之才因萬章不
見諸侯之問旣反覆告之至此又以禮義之切
於人者曉之其垂世立敎之意有在矣他章有
punctuated: 惟禮是循而不可舍，禮非在人出入之門乎？夫義路禮門，乃道之切於人者如此。苟非君子之人，則不能由是路而出入是門矣。彼若庶人，召之役則往役者，非徇人也，義之宜然也。君子知乎此而守身以義，故往役而不往見，其所以由是路也，豈衆人所可能哉？不傳贄爲臣則不見諸侯，非傲上也，禮之當然也。君子明乎此而律身以禮，故不爲臣則不敢往見，其所以出入是門也，豈常人所能及哉？吁！義路禮門，固君子之所以自處者，亦人君之所以處乎賢者也。苟見賢而不以是道，是欲其入而閉其門、塞其路矣，賢豈爲吾用哉？嗟夫！戰國之士，朝叩秦關，暮遊燕璧，不待人君之召而衒玉求售者，比比皆然，禮義漠然也。孟子以命世亞聖之才，因萬章不見諸侯之問，旣反覆告之至此，又以禮義之切於人者曉之，其垂世立敎之意有在矣。他章有
translation_en:
…must follow ritual propriety alone and never abandon it. Is ritual propriety not the gateway through which people enter and leave? Such is the vital importance to human life of righteousness as the road and ritual propriety as the gateway. Unless one is a gentleman, one cannot follow this road and pass through this gateway. Take the commoner who goes to perform labor service when summoned: he does so not to comply with another person's wishes, but because righteousness requires it. The gentleman understands this and preserves his integrity through righteousness. Thus he goes to perform labor service but does not go merely to seek an audience. Could ordinary people possibly follow this road as he does? If he has not presented an introductory gift and become a subject, he does not seek an audience with the regional lords. This is not arrogance toward his superiors; it is what ritual propriety requires. The gentleman understands this and disciplines himself through ritual propriety. Thus, unless he has become a subject, he does not presume to seek an audience. Could ordinary people match the way he passes through this gateway?

Ah! Righteousness as the road and ritual propriety as the gateway are indeed the means by which the gentleman conducts himself, but they are also the means by which a ruler should treat worthy men. If a ruler seeks an audience with a worthy man without following this Way, he wishes him to enter while shutting his gateway and blocking his road. How could the worthy man serve him? Alas! Among the scholars of the Warring States, those who knocked at Qin's passes in the morning and roamed within Yan's walls [?] in the evening, displaying their jade in search of a buyer without waiting for a ruler's summons, were everywhere. They were heedless of ritual propriety and righteousness. Mencius, endowed with the talents of an epoch-defining figure and Second Sage, responded to Wan Zhang's question about not seeking audiences with regional lords. Having already explained the matter repeatedly up to this point, he further enlightened him about the vital importance of ritual propriety and righteousness to human life. Herein lay his intention to establish teachings for generations to come. In another chapter there is…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
曰居天下之廣居立天下之正位行天下之大
道孟軻氏其以斯言為已任也歟
易
應乎天而時行
張紹齡
同考試官訓導王批題本平易塲中作者多
專指九二為應乾殊失本義之旨此篇體認切而詞
不繁故錄之以冠本房
===
考試官敎諭鄭批辭理兼優於衆作故錄之
考試官學正朱批得本義之旨
順乎天而隨時有為大有之君為然也蓋君道
莫大乎體天而致治也六五之君應天而時行
此其治之所以元亨也歟昔夫子傳彖釋大有
元亨之辭舉卦體而言謂夫下乾為天而六五
應之時有可為而六五乘之六五之君其治有
也應天而時行蓋必心焉同乎天心之至公德
punctuated:
曰：「居天下之廣居，立天下之正位，行天下之大道。」孟軻氏其以斯言為已任也歟？

易
應乎天而時行
張紹齡

同考試官訓導王批：「題本平易，塲中作者多專指九二為應乾，殊失本義之旨。此篇體認切而詞不繁，故錄之以冠本房。」

考試官敎諭鄭批：「辭理兼優於衆作，故錄之。」

考試官學正朱批：「得本義之旨。」

順乎天而隨時有為，大有之君為然也。蓋君道莫大乎體天而致治也。六五之君應天而時行，此其治之所以元亨也歟？昔夫子傳彖，釋大有元亨之辭，舉卦體而言，謂夫下乾為天，而六五應之；時有可為，而六五乘之。六五之君，其治有也，應天而時行，蓋必心焉同乎天心之至公，德
translation_en:
…says: “Dwell in the broad dwelling of all under Heaven, stand in the correct position of all under Heaven, and walk the great Way of all under Heaven.” Did Meng Ke not take these words as his own charge?

Book of Changes
“Responding to Heaven and acting as the time requires”
Zhang Shaoling

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: “The topic is straightforward, yet many candidates in the examination hall exclusively identified the nine in the second place as what ‘responds to Qian,’ departing considerably from the purport of the Original Meaning. This essay shows precise understanding without wordiness, so it has been selected to head the essays from this examining room.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Its language and reasoning both surpass those of the other compositions; therefore it has been selected.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, School Instructor: “It grasps the purport of the Original Meaning.”

To accord with Heaven and undertake action as the time requires—such is the ruler represented by Great Possession. For nothing in the Way of the ruler is greater than embodying Heaven and thereby bringing about good government. The ruler represented by the six in the fifth place responds to Heaven and acts as the time requires: is this not why his government achieves supreme success? Long ago, when the Master composed the Commentary on the Judgment and explained the words ‘supreme success’ in Great Possession, he spoke in terms of the hexagram’s structure. He meant that the lower trigram, Qian, represents Heaven, and the six in the fifth place responds to it; when the time offers an opportunity for action, the six in the fifth place takes advantage of it. The ruler represented by the six in the fifth place, in governing his possessions [?], responds to Heaven and acts as the time requires. Surely, in his heart he must share the utmost impartiality of Heaven’s heart, and in his virtue…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
焉合乎天德之至健天命有善我則命有德而
善必揚之焉天命無惡我則討有罪而惡必遏
之焉一舉措也與天黙契而不違一設施也與
天脗合而不悖夫旣無往而不應乎天尤必無
適而不以其時時可行也於焉乘之以有行時
可為也於焉隨之以有為善必揚之而揚善以
時不先而不後焉惡必遏之而遏惡以時無過
而無不及焉凡設施也必當其時之可凡舉措
===
也必適乎時之宜五之應天而時行如此則治
有之大善而亨也豈不宜哉粤稽諸古堯舜之
承天道而通變宜民湯武之奉天命而志在救
民此皆應天而時行者也故堯舜之世黎民於
變而四方風動湯武之時兆民允殖而萬姓悅
服是皆有元亨之治也然則堯舜湯武其大有
之六五也歟
以言乎遠則不禦以言乎邇則靜而正
punctuated:
焉合乎天德之至健。天命有善，我則命有德而善必揚之焉；天命無惡，我則討有罪而惡必遏之焉。一舉措也，與天黙契而不違；一設施也，與天脗合而不悖。夫旣無往而不應乎天，尤必無適而不以其時。時可行也，於焉乘之以有行；時可為也，於焉隨之以有為。善必揚之，而揚善以時，不先而不後焉；惡必遏之，而遏惡以時，無過而無不及焉。凡設施也，必當其時之可；凡舉措也，必適乎時之宜。五之應天而時行如此，則治有之大善而亨也，豈不宜哉？粤稽諸古，堯舜之承天道而通變宜民，湯武之奉天命而志在救民，此皆應天而時行者也。故堯舜之世，黎民於變而四方風動；湯武之時，兆民允殖而萬姓悅服。是皆有元亨之治也。然則堯舜湯武，其大有之六五也歟？

以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正。
translation_en:
… accords with the utmost vigor of Heaven’s virtue. Heaven decrees that there be goodness; I therefore appoint the virtuous, ensuring that goodness is promoted. Heaven decrees that there be no evil; I therefore punish the guilty, ensuring that evil is checked. Every action accords tacitly with Heaven, without deviation; every measure agrees with Heaven, without contradiction. Since one responds to Heaven in every circumstance, one must also act according to the proper time in every situation. When the time permits action, one seizes it and acts; when the time permits an undertaking, one follows it and undertakes it. Goodness must be promoted, and its promotion must be timely, neither premature nor belated. Evil must be checked, and its suppression must be timely, neither excessive nor insufficient. Every measure must suit what the time permits; every action must accord with what the time requires. When the fifth line responds to Heaven and acts according to the time in this way, is it not fitting that government under Great Possession should attain supreme goodness and success?

Examining antiquity, we find that Yao and Shun followed the Way of Heaven, adapting to change to benefit the people; Tang and Wu upheld Heaven’s Mandate, intent upon rescuing the people. All of them responded to Heaven and acted according to the time. Thus, in the age of Yao and Shun, the common people were transformed, and the four quarters stirred as if moved by the wind. In the time of Tang and Wu, the multitudes truly flourished, and all the people submitted gladly. These were all instances of government attaining supreme success. Were not Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, then, embodiments of the six in the fifth place of Great Possession?

Speaking of what is distant, it knows no bounds; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
張紹齡
同考試官訓導王批此題作者多泛講不切能以
陰陽之理貫於事物立說者僅見此篇
考試官教諭鄭批辭理俱到可取
考試官學正朱批說出易理之所以廣大者甚
明
隨所在而各足者易理之廣大也夫易理無間
於遠近則隨在而各足矣謂之廣大不亦宜乎
===
昔大傳聖人論易之廣大而言及此謂夫易之
爲易陰陽之理而已是理也語遠而有所盡則
周乎近而窮於遠矣非廣大也語近而有不存
則該乎遠而忽於近矣非廣大也今焉以至遠
言之吾知其際天極地事物之充塞乎兩間者
陰陽之理皆有以體之而無遺不以地之至遠
而有限量之可言焉往古來今事物之散殊於
古今者陰陽之理皆有以貫之而無間不以時
punctuated:
張紹齡。
同考試官訓導王批：此題作者多泛講不切，能以陰陽之理貫於事物立說者，僅見此篇。
考試官教諭鄭批：辭理俱到，可取。
考試官學正朱批：說出易理之所以廣大者甚明。
隨所在而各足者，易理之廣大也。夫易理無間於遠近，則隨在而各足矣。謂之廣大，不亦宜乎？
昔大傳聖人論易之廣大而言及此，謂夫易之爲易，陰陽之理而已。是理也，語遠而有所盡，則周乎近而窮於遠矣，非廣大也；語近而有不存，則該乎遠而忽於近矣，非廣大也。今焉以至遠言之，吾知其際天極地，事物之充塞乎兩間者，陰陽之理皆有以體之而無遺，不以地之至遠而有限量之可言焉。往古來今，事物之散殊於古今者，陰陽之理皆有以貫之而無間，不以時
translation_en:
Zhang Shaoling.
Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: Most who wrote on this topic discussed it vaguely and failed to address it closely. This is the only essay I have seen that builds its argument upon the principles of yin and yang as running through affairs and things.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished. Worth selecting.
Examiner Zhu, School Director, comments: The explanation of what makes the principles of the Changes vast and great is exceptionally clear.
That they are complete wherever they are found constitutes the vastness and greatness of the principles of the Changes. Since these principles admit no gaps between far and near, they are complete wherever they are found. Is it not fitting to call them vast and great?
Long ago, in the Great Commentary, the sage spoke these words when discussing the vastness and greatness of the Changes. His meaning was that what makes the Changes the Changes is nothing other than the principles of yin and yang. If these principles, when considered in relation to what is distant, reached some limit, they would encompass what is near but be exhausted in what is far; this would not be vastness and greatness. If, when considered in relation to what is near, there were anything in which they were absent, they would embrace what is far but overlook what is near; this would not be vastness and greatness. Now, speaking of what is most distant, I know that, to the bounds of heaven and the utmost reaches of earth, the principles of yin and yang give substance to all the affairs and things that fill the space between them, leaving nothing out. Even at the greatest distances in space, no limit to them can be spoken of. From antiquity to the present, the principles of yin and yang run without interruption through all the diverse affairs and things dispersed across past and present; nor, on account of time …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之至遠而有涯涘之可擬焉其遠之無有盡也
為何如以至近言之吾知其几席之下事物之
觸乎目者雖至微也不待涉於動作而陰陽之
實理以具初不以地之近而有所違焉瞬息之
際事物之接乎前者雖至小也不待形於施為
而陰陽之正理以存亦不以時之近而有所外
焉其近之無不存也又何如吁言乎遠則不以
遠而窮言乎近則不以近而偏易理之廣大非
===
此而何歟抑嘗觀之中庸所謂語大天下莫能
載即此之遠則不禦也所謂語小天下莫能破
即此之近則靜而正也所謂洋洋乎發育萬物
峻極于天即下文言乎天地之間則備者焉蓋
易之道即中庸之道子思之於夫子得傳道之
心法不然何其言之不異若符節之相合也歟
書
日宣三德夙夜浚明有家日嚴祇敬六德
punctuated:
之至遠而有涯涘之可擬焉。其遠之無有盡也，為何如？以至近言之，吾知其几席之下，事物之觸乎目者，雖至微也，不待涉於動作，而陰陽之實理以具，初不以地之近而有所違焉。瞬息之際，事物之接乎前者，雖至小也，不待形於施為，而陰陽之正理以存，亦不以時之近而有所外焉。其近之無不存也，又何如？吁！言乎遠，則不以遠而窮；言乎近，則不以近而偏。易理之廣大，非此而何歟？抑嘗觀之，《中庸》所謂「語大，天下莫能載」，即此之「遠則不禦」也；所謂「語小，天下莫能破」，即此之「近則靜而正」也；所謂「洋洋乎！發育萬物，峻極于天」，即下文「言乎天地之間則備」者焉。蓋《易》之道，即《中庸》之道。子思之於夫子，得傳道之心法。不然，何其言之不異，若符節之相合也歟？
書
日宣三德，夙夜浚明有家；日嚴祇敬六德，
translation_en:
…nor does the utmost remoteness of time admit of any boundary that could be conceived. How inexhaustible is its reach into the distant! Speaking of what is nearest, I know that even beneath our tables and mats, however minute the things that meet our eyes, the substantive principles of yin and yang are already fully present before any movement or action occurs. Spatial proximity has never placed anything beyond their compass. Within a fleeting instant, however small the things that come before us, the correct principles of yin and yang are already present before they take shape in practical activity. Temporal proximity likewise excludes nothing from them. How all-pervasive, then, is their presence in what is near! Ah! Speaking of the distant, they are not exhausted by distance; speaking of the near, they are not confined by proximity. What else could constitute the breadth and greatness of the principles of the Changes?
I have also considered this: when the Doctrine of the Mean says, “Speak of its greatness, and nothing under Heaven can contain it,” this is precisely what is meant here by “in its remoteness, it knows no bounds.” When it says, “Speak of its smallness, and nothing under Heaven can divide it,” this is precisely what is meant here by “in its nearness, it is still and correct.” When it says, “Vast and abundant, it brings forth and nourishes the myriad things, reaching in its loftiness to Heaven,” this corresponds to the subsequent statement, “Speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it encompasses everything.” Thus the Way of the Changes is the Way of the Doctrine of the Mean. Zisi received from the Master the essential teaching through which the Way was transmitted. Otherwise, how could their words agree as closely as the matching halves of a tally?
Book of Documents
“Daily displaying three virtues, and profoundly discerning them morning and night, one may govern a noble house; daily maintaining solemn reverence and respect for six virtues, …”

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
亮采有邦翕受敷施九德咸事俊乂
在官百僚師師百工惟時撫于五辰
庶績其凝
余敬
同考試官教諭黃批場中作此題者多襲
陳言令人厭觀求其詞氣舂容理致自見此作得之
考試官教諭鄭批發明臯陶知人之㫖精切未有
如此篇者
===
考試官學正朱批說書明盡此卷特優
賢才脩德不同各有以宜其職人君用賢盡道
斯有以成其功蓋德有多寡宜職有大小也人
君誠能用賢而盡其道又豈不致治功之成哉
昔臯陶陳知人之謨於舜及此謂夫官人之道
不求其德之備而取其德之常彼人於九德之
中有其三必日宣而充廣之而使之益以著是
三德爲有常矣是人也而爲大夫必能夙夜匪
punctuated:
亮采有邦。翕受敷施，九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師，百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績其凝。
余敬
同考試官教諭黃批：場中作此題者，多襲陳言，令人厭觀。求其詞氣舂容，理致自見，此作得之。
考試官教諭鄭批：發明臯陶知人之㫖，精切未有如此篇者。
考試官學正朱批：說書明盡，此卷特優。
賢才脩德不同，各有以宜其職；人君用賢盡道，斯有以成其功。蓋德有多寡，宜職有大小也。人君誠能用賢而盡其道，又豈不致治功之成哉？昔臯陶陳知人之謨於舜，及此，謂夫官人之道，不求其德之備，而取其德之常。彼人於九德之中有其三，必日宣而充廣之，而使之益以著，是三德爲有常矣。是人也而爲大夫，必能夙夜匪
translation_en:
…and faithfully discharge the duties of governing a state. Receive them together and distribute appointments: those possessing the nine virtues will all serve. Outstanding and capable men will hold office; the hundred officials will learn from one another; all officers will attend to their proper tasks, keeping in harmony with the five heavenly cycles, and the many achievements will be firmly established.

Yu Jing

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Many candidates answering this topic in the examination merely repeat stale expressions, making them tiresome to read. If one seeks expansive, unhurried language in which the underlying principles reveal themselves naturally, this composition achieves it.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “In elucidating Gao Yao’s meaning concerning the discernment of men, no essay has equaled this one in precision and aptness.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Its explanation of the Book of Documents is lucid and exhaustive. This examination paper is particularly outstanding.”

Worthy and talented men differ in their cultivation of virtue, yet each possesses qualities suited to his office. When the ruler fully follows the proper way of employing worthy men, he thereby brings his work to fruition. For men possess virtues in greater or lesser number, and the offices suitable for them are correspondingly greater or smaller. If the ruler truly employs worthy men in full accordance with the proper way, how could he fail to achieve successful government?

Formerly, when Gao Yao presented to Shun his counsel on discerning men, he came to this point: the proper way to appoint men to office is not to demand that their virtues be complete, but to select them for constancy in the virtues they possess. If a man possesses three of the nine virtues, he must manifest them daily, developing and extending them so that they become increasingly evident. These three virtues will then be constant. If such a man becomes a grand master, he will surely be able, morning and night, never to …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
惔明治夫有家之事焉人於九德之中有其六
充必日嚴而祗敬之而使之益以謹是六德爲
有常矣若人也而爲諸侯必能克勤無怠亮采
夫有邦之政焉夫德之多寡雖不同人君惟能
合而受之寸善片長無或遺布而用之量德隨
才無不當如此則九德之賢或浚明或亮采咸
事其事而野無遺賢矣俊乂之人或有邦或有
家皆在官使而下無遺才矣百僚皆以德而相
===
師善與人同無媚疾也百工皆及時以趨事順
于五辰無玩愒也由是禮樂明備而庶政有惟
和之休刑政脩舉而庶績有咸熈之美治功之
成爲何如哉抑嘗考之人君御世不患治功之
不成惟患賢才之不用不患賢才之不用惟患
任使之無方苟徒求其德之備而不求其德之
常幾何不虚譽隆而實德病哉故皐陶陳知人
之謨拳拳及此無非欲以天下之才任天下之
punctuated:
惔，明治夫有家之事焉。人於九德之中有其六，充必日嚴而祗敬之，而使之益以謹，是六德爲有常矣。若人也而爲諸侯，必能克勤無怠，亮采夫有邦之政焉。夫德之多寡雖不同，人君惟能合而受之，寸善片長無或遺；布而用之，量德隨才無不當。如此，則九德之賢，或浚明，或亮采，咸事其事，而野無遺賢矣；俊乂之人，或有邦，或有家，皆在官使，而下無遺才矣。百僚皆以德而相師，善與人同，無媚疾也；百工皆及時以趨事，順于五辰，無玩愒也。由是禮樂明備，而庶政有惟和之休；刑政脩舉，而庶績有咸熈之美。治功之成爲何如哉！
抑嘗考之，人君御世，不患治功之不成，惟患賢才之不用；不患賢才之不用，惟患任使之無方。苟徒求其德之備，而不求其德之常，幾何不虚譽隆而實德病哉？故皐陶陳知人之謨，拳拳及此，無非欲以天下之才任天下之
translation_en:
…untiring [?], and administer with discernment the affairs of a noble house. If a person possesses six of the nine virtues, he must daily cultivate them with gravity and reverence [?], making his conduct ever more circumspect; these six virtues will then be constant. Should such a person become a feudal lord, he will surely work diligently without slackening and faithfully discharge the governmental duties of a domain. Although people differ in the number of virtues they possess, the ruler need only gather and accept them, overlooking no smallest goodness or slightest strength, and deploy them in service, assigning each appropriately according to his virtue and ability. Thus, worthy men possessing the nine virtues will each attend to their duties, some administering with discernment and others faithfully discharging their responsibilities, leaving no worthy man neglected outside office. Men of outstanding talent and ability, some governing domains and others noble houses, will all hold official appointments, leaving no talent unused among those below. The officials will all learn virtue from one another, sharing goodness with others, without flattery or jealousy. All officers will attend to their duties at the proper times, following the five seasonal phases, without negligence or idling. Consequently, rites and music will be clearly established and fully provided, and the many affairs of government will enjoy the blessing of harmony; punishments and administration will be put in good order, and all undertakings will attain the excellence of flourishing together. How great, then, will the achievement of good government be!
Yet, upon reflection, a ruler governing the world should worry less about failing to achieve good government than about failing to employ worthy and talented men; less about failing to employ them than about lacking the proper means of assigning and using them. If he merely seeks completeness in their virtues rather than constancy, how can he avoid a situation in which empty reputation flourishes while genuine virtue suffers? Thus, when Gao Yao set forth his counsel on discerning men, he earnestly addressed this matter, desiring only to entrust the talent of all under Heaven with the responsibility for all under Heaven’s…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
治也吁有虞雍煕泰和之盛良有以夫
乃命重黎絕地天通罔有降格羣后之逮
在下明明棐常鰥寡無蓋皇帝清問
下民鰥寡有辭于苗德威惟畏德明
惟明乃命三后恤功于民伯夷降典
折民惟刑禹平水土主名山川稷降
播種農殖嘉穀三后成功惟殷于民
士制百姓于刑之中以教祗德
===
吳言
同考試官教諭黃批題頭緒頗多作者甚為
所窘能摹寫穆王訓刑之意殆盡僅見此篇
考試官教諭鄭批文足以發理此作為最
考試官學正朱批辭詳整而理縝密
聖世君臣盡心以圖治允資大臣明刑以輔治
此賢王舉之以訓刑也夫為治之本在德而刑
特以輔其所不及耳賢王歷敘聖世之事以命
punctuated:
治也。吁！有虞雍煕泰和之盛，良有以夫！
乃命重黎絕地天通，罔有降格。羣后之逮在下，明明棐常，鰥寡無蓋。皇帝清問下民，鰥寡有辭于苗。德威惟畏，德明惟明。乃命三后恤功于民：伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以教祗德。
吳言
同考試官教諭黃批：題頭緒頗多，作者甚為所窘，能摹寫穆王訓刑之意殆盡，僅見此篇。
考試官教諭鄭批：文足以發理，此作為最。
考試官學正朱批：辭詳整而理縝密。
聖世君臣盡心以圖治，允資大臣明刑以輔治，此賢王舉之以訓刑也。夫為治之本在德，而刑特以輔其所不及耳。賢王歷敘聖世之事以命
translation_en:
…the governance of the realm. Ah! The flourishing harmony and supreme peace of the age of Youyu surely had their grounds!
“Then he commanded Zhong and Li to sever communication between earth and heaven, so that there would be no descending visitations. The various lords and those serving below them diligently illuminated and supported the constant norms, and widowers and widows were not kept from making their circumstances known. The august emperor carefully inquired among the common people, and widowers and widows brought complaints against the Miao. His virtue inspired awe, and they stood in awe; his virtue brought illumination, and they became enlightened. He then commanded three ministers to undertake work for the people’s welfare. Boyi promulgated the statutes, restraining the people through proper standards; Yu regulated the waters and lands and presided over the naming of mountains and rivers; Ji taught sowing and planting, cultivating fine grain. The three ministers accomplished their work, bringing abundance to the people. The judicial officer regulated the common people through judicious punishments, teaching them to revere virtue.”
Wu Yan.
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, an Instructor: “The topic has many strands, which greatly constrained the writer. This is the only essay I have seen that manages to convey almost fully King Mu’s intention in his instructions on punishments.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, an Instructor: “The writing adequately elucidates the principles. This composition is the best.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, a School Instructor: “The language is detailed and orderly, and the reasoning meticulous.”
In the age of the sages, ruler and ministers devoted themselves wholeheartedly to achieving good government, truly relying on the great ministers to clarify punishments as an aid to governance. The worthy king cited this example in giving his instructions on punishments. Now, the foundation of government lies in virtue; punishments merely supplement what virtue cannot reach. The worthy king recounted in sequence the affairs of the age of the sages to instruct …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
呂侯其知本歟昔穆王之意若謂昔在有虞三
苗昏虐人心蓋泯泯棼棼矣帝舜以為治莫先
於正人心也首命重黎脩明祀典絕地天之通
嚴幽明之分焄蒿妖誕之說舉屏息而不作當
時大小之臣皆精白一心輔助常道雖鰥寡無
告之微亦得以自伸焉尤恐無以盡達下情也
於是虛心而問下民鰥寡得以聲苗之過苗以
虐為威過也帝則以德威而天下無不畏苗以
===
察為明過也帝則以德明而天下無不明焉民
漸吏化如此不命官分任其責治能有成乎乃
命三后致憂民之功伯夷降典折民邪妄以正
人心禹平水土主名山川以定民居稷降播種
農殖嘉穀以厚民生三后成功而致民之殷盛
富庶也治化之盛如此不制刑以輔不及治能
永保乎於是命皐陶為士師之官彼民之漸涵
吾治化固無事於刑其頑慢弗率者則制之于
punctuated: 呂侯，其知本歟？昔穆王之意若謂：昔在有虞，三苗昏虐，人心蓋泯泯棼棼矣。帝舜以為治莫先於正人心也，首命重黎脩明祀典，絕地天之通，嚴幽明之分，焄蒿妖誕之說舉屏息而不作。當時大小之臣皆精白一心，輔助常道，雖鰥寡無告之微，亦得以自伸焉。尤恐無以盡達下情也，於是虛心而問下民，鰥寡得以聲苗之過。苗以虐為威，過也；帝則以德威，而天下無不畏。苗以察為明，過也；帝則以德明，而天下無不明焉。民漸吏化如此，不命官分任其責，治能有成乎？乃命三后致憂民之功：伯夷降典，折民邪妄，以正人心；禹平水土，主名山川，以定民居；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀，以厚民生。三后成功，而致民之殷盛富庶也。治化之盛如此，不制刑以輔不及，治能永保乎？於是命皐陶為士師之官。彼民之漸涵吾治化，固無事於刑；其頑慢弗率者，則制之于
translation_en:
…the Marquis of Lü: did he not understand the foundation? King Mu’s meaning then was as though he were saying: In the time of Youyu, the Sanmiao were benighted and cruel, and people’s hearts had sunk into confusion and disorder. Emperor Shun held that nothing in governing took precedence over rectifying people’s hearts. He first commanded Chong and Li to put the sacrificial statutes in order, sever communication between earth and heaven, and strictly distinguish the unseen realm from the visible. All uncanny and fantastic talk of ghostly vapors was silenced and ceased to arise. At that time, officials great and small all served with pure and single-minded devotion, upholding the constant Way. Even such humble people as widowers and widows with no one to appeal to could make their grievances heard.

Still fearing that the circumstances of those below might not be fully communicated, he consulted the common people with an open mind, and widowers and widows were able to voice the faults of the Miao. The Miao made cruelty their source of awe: this was a fault. The emperor instead inspired awe through virtue, and none under Heaven failed to stand in awe of him. The Miao made intrusive scrutiny their discernment: this was a fault. The emperor instead exercised discernment through virtue, and none under Heaven remained unenlightened. With the people thus imbued and the officials transformed [?], could government achieve success unless officials were appointed to share its responsibilities?

He therefore commanded the three lords to devote their efforts to caring for the people. Boyi promulgated the statutes and checked the people’s perversity and delusion, thereby rectifying their hearts. Yu brought the waters and lands into order and designated the principal mountains and rivers, thereby securing the people’s dwellings. Ji taught sowing and planting, cultivating fine grains to enrich the people’s livelihood. The three lords accomplished their tasks and brought the people prosperity, wealth, and abundance.

With the transforming influence of government thus flourishing, could good government be preserved forever without establishing punishments to supplement what it could not reach? He therefore appointed Gao Yao to the office of Judge. Those people gradually steeped in our government’s transforming influence would certainly have no occasion for punishment; but those who were obstinate, remiss, and unwilling to obey were to be restrained within…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
刑辟之中民之範圍吾治理亦無待於法其泿
棼未信者則制之以刑罰之當非徒繩之以法
也正以檢制其心而教祗德使民心之未正者
悉歸於正焉非直示之以威也所以檢束其心
而教敬德使人心之未善者皆化於善焉吁德
以化之於先君臣圖治為甚詳刑以維之於後
一臣保治為有要此有虞之治所以盡善也歟
雖然德化乃聖人之本心刑罰亦聖人之不得
已二者固不可偏廢也穆王訓刑首及乎此其
亦知所尚矣惜乎專訓贖刑雖罪大辟之科而
亦有金贖之例曾謂有虞之制有是哉夫子錄
之蓋以示戒云
詩
即有邰家室誕降嘉種維秬維秠維穈維
芑恒之秬秠是穫是畝恒之穈芑是
任是負以歸肇祀誕我祀如何或□
punctuated:
刑辟之中。民之範圍吾治理，亦無待於法；其泿棼未信者，則制之以刑罰之當。非徒繩之以法也，正以檢制其心而教祗德，使民心之未正者悉歸於正焉；非直示之以威也，所以檢束其心而教敬德，使人心之未善者皆化於善焉。吁！德以化之於先，君臣圖治為甚詳；刑以維之於後，一臣保治為有要。此有虞之治所以盡善也歟！雖然，德化乃聖人之本心，刑罰亦聖人之不得已，二者固不可偏廢也。穆王訓刑，首及乎此，其亦知所尚矣。惜乎專訓贖刑，雖罪大辟之科，而亦有金贖之例，曾謂有虞之制有是哉！夫子錄之，蓋以示戒云。

詩

即有邰家室，誕降嘉種，維秬維秠，維穈維芑。恒之秬秠，是穫是畝；恒之穈芑，是任是負，以歸肇祀。誕我祀如何？或□
translation_en:
…within the bounds of penal law. The people, encompassed by our orderly government, likewise have no need of legal constraint; those who remain confused and disorderly [?] and do not yet comply are restrained through appropriate punishments. This is not merely to subject them to the law, but precisely to restrain their hearts and teach them to revere virtue, so that all whose hearts are not yet upright return to uprightness. Nor is it simply to display authority before them: it is to discipline their hearts and teach them to respect virtue, so that all whose hearts are not yet good are transformed toward goodness. Ah! Through virtue they were first transformed, and ruler and ministers planned their government with the utmost thoroughness; through punishments order was subsequently maintained, and a single minister had the essential means of preserving good government. Was this not why the government of Youyu achieved complete excellence?

Nevertheless, transformation through virtue is the sage’s original intention, while punishment is something to which the sage resorts only when compelled. Neither may therefore be neglected. When King Mu issued his instructions on punishments, he addressed this first; he too understood what should be esteemed. Regrettably, his instructions concentrated on redeeming punishments through payments: even offenses classified as capital crimes could be redeemed by payments of metal. Could one possibly claim that the institutions of Youyu included such a practice? The Master recorded this, presumably to offer a warning.

The Book of Odes

He settled in Tai and established his household; then he bestowed fine seeds: black millet and double-grained millet, red millet and white millet. He planted the black and double-grained millet, harvested it, and piled it in the fields; he planted the red and white millet, carried it on shoulders and backs, and brought it home to inaugurate sacrifices. How, then, do we perform our sacrifices? Some [illegible]…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或揄或簸或蹂釋之叟叟烝之浮浮
載謀載惟取蕭祭脂取羝以軷載燔
載烈以興嗣歲卬盛于豆于豆于登
其香始升上帝居歆胡臭亶時后稷
肇祀庶無罪悔以迄于今
陳鍾
同考試官訓導黃批后稷以農功封邰而肇
祀後人郊祀而天格之速由后稷有農功也此作
===
深得本旨録之
考試官教諭鄭批始終歸重后稷之農功有
定見者
考試官學正朱批說后稷之功明白
詩人原始祖受封主祭而詳奉祭之事述後王
尊祖配天而推天饗之由蓋后稷以農功受封
而肇祀天心眷之久矣後王尊以配天之祭而
天饗之速者豈不由于此耶昔周公制禮尊后
punctuated:
或揄，或簸，或蹂，釋之叟叟，烝之浮浮。載謀載惟，取蕭祭脂，取羝以軷，載燔載烈，以興嗣歲。卬盛于豆，于豆于登，其香始升，上帝居歆。胡臭亶時？后稷肇祀，庶無罪悔，以迄于今。
陳鍾
同考試官訓導黃批：后稷以農功封邰而肇祀，後人郊祀而天格之速，由后稷有農功也。此作深得本旨，録之。
考試官教諭鄭批：始終歸重后稷之農功，有定見者。
考試官學正朱批：說后稷之功明白。
詩人原始祖受封主祭，而詳奉祭之事；述後王尊祖配天，而推天饗之由。蓋后稷以農功受封而肇祀，天心眷之久矣。後王尊以配天之祭，而天饗之速者，豈不由于此耶？昔周公制禮，尊后
translation_en:
…Some scoop out the grain, some winnow it, and some tread it. They wash it with a rustling sound and steam it until vapors rise. They deliberate and consider; they take southernwood to offer with fat, and take a ram for the sacrifice to the road. They roast and broil, thereby inaugurating the coming year. I fill the offering vessels—the dou dishes and the deng bowls. As their fragrance begins to rise, the Lord on High is pleased to accept them. Why is the fragrance so fitting? Hou Ji began these sacrifices, and, we hope, they have remained free from fault or cause for regret down to the present.

Chen Zhong

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: Hou Ji was enfeoffed at Tai for his achievements in agriculture and began the sacrifices. When his descendants performed the suburban sacrifice, Heaven came swiftly because of Hou Ji’s agricultural achievements. This composition grasps the underlying meaning deeply; include it in the record.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: From beginning to end, it places the emphasis on Hou Ji’s agricultural achievements. The writer has a settled interpretation.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, School Director: It explains Hou Ji’s achievements clearly.

The poet traces how the founding ancestor received his fief and presided over sacrifices, detailing the conduct of the offerings. He recounts how later kings honored their ancestor by associating him with Heaven in sacrifice, and investigates why Heaven accepted the offerings. Hou Ji received his fief for his agricultural achievements and inaugurated the sacrifices; Heaven had long regarded him with favor. When later kings honored him with sacrifices associating him with Heaven, was this not the reason Heaven accepted their offerings so swiftly? In former times, the Duke of Zhou established the rites and honored Hou…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
稷以配天故作此詩謂夫后稷務兹稼穡有功
于民故堯封之有邰之地使主姜嫄之祀斯時
也后稷以嘉種而降之其種伊何不惟有黑黍
之秬而又有一稃二米之秠不惟有赤粱粟之
縻而又有白粱粟之芑徧種之而既成也則穫
而棲之于畝徧播之而已熟也則任而負之以
歸所以然者將以肇宗廟之祭始羣神之祀也
然是祀也后稷之所奉也其事何如或以嘉穀
===
而舂揄之或以嘉穀而簸蹂之釋之聲叟叟也
烝之氣浮浮也謀焉而卜日擇士惟焉而齊戒
具脩祀宗廟之主而蕭脂以爇祀行道之神而
牡羊以將燔焉而尸羞無不具也烈焉而尸羞
無不供也所以然者將以興來歲之祀于無窮
繼往歲之祀于不替也后稷以農功而肇祀如
此後人寧不尊之以配天之祭乎于是我以菹
醢而盛之于豆也我以太羹而薦之于登也馨
punctuated: 稷以配天，故作此詩。謂夫后稷務兹稼穡，有功于民，故堯封之有邰之地，使主姜嫄之祀。斯時也，后稷以嘉種而降之。其種伊何？不惟有黑黍之秬，而又有一稃二米之秠；不惟有赤粱粟之縻，而又有白粱粟之芑。徧種之而既成也，則穫而棲之于畝；徧播之而已熟也，則任而負之以歸。所以然者，將以肇宗廟之祭，始羣神之祀也。然是祀也，后稷之所奉也，其事何如？或以嘉穀而舂揄之，或以嘉穀而簸蹂之。釋之聲叟叟也，烝之氣浮浮也。謀焉而卜日擇士，惟焉而齊戒具脩。祀宗廟之主，而蕭脂以爇；祀行道之神，而牡羊以將。燔焉而尸羞無不具也，烈焉而尸羞無不供也。所以然者，將以興來歲之祀于無窮，繼往歲之祀于不替也。后稷以農功而肇祀如此，後人寧不尊之以配天之祭乎？于是我以菹醢而盛之于豆也，我以太羹而薦之于登也，馨
translation_en:
…Ji to be paired with Heaven in sacrifice, and therefore composed this poem. It says that Hou Ji devoted himself to sowing and reaping and rendered meritorious service to the people. Yao therefore enfeoffed him in the land of Youtai and charged him with presiding over sacrifices to Jiang Yuan. At that time, Hou Ji bestowed fine seeds. What kinds of seeds were they? There was not only ju, the black millet, but also pi, with two grains in a single husk; not only mi [?], the red millet, but also qi, the white millet. When these had been planted everywhere and had grown, he harvested them and stacked them in the fields. When these had been sown everywhere and had ripened, he shouldered them and carried them home. The purpose was to inaugurate sacrifices in the ancestral temple and institute offerings to the many spirits.

These were the sacrifices that Hou Ji performed. How were they conducted? Some pounded and scooped out the fine grain; others winnowed and rubbed it. Washing it made a swishing sound; steaming it sent vapor billowing upward. They deliberated, divined the day, and selected the officiants; they took thought, purified themselves through abstinence, and completed all preparations. To sacrifice to the ancestral tablets in the temple, they burned southernwood with fat; to sacrifice to the spirit of the road, they presented a ram. They roasted the meat, fully preparing the delicacies for the personator of the ancestor; they broiled it, supplying every delicacy for him. The purpose was to carry forward the coming years’ sacrifices without end and continue those of past years without interruption.

Since Hou Ji thus inaugurated sacrifices through his achievements in agriculture, could his descendants fail to honor him with sacrifices pairing him with Heaven? Accordingly, we fill the dou offering vessels with pickled vegetables and meat sauces, and present the unseasoned broth in the deng offering vessels. The fragrant…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
香之氣始芬然而升上帝之神已居然面饗也
何但芳臭之薦信得其時哉蓋自后稷以農功
而受封因稼穡而肇祀則庶無罪悔以至于今
矣然則天應之疾者有由然也豈徒以其物哉
抑觀此詩與思文均爲尊稷配天作也而詳畧
不同何耶蓋此爲序事宜詳不詳無以見其始
終彼爲獻詞宜簡不簡無以見其嚴肅讀詩者
不可不知
===
我將我享維羊維牛維天其右之
田宏
