有志遷之序也固以天文更之不知非關
於漢之一代何益乎河渠有志遷之編也
固以溝洫易之不知非出於漢之所治何
當乎易封禪以郊祀不載原廟宗廟之事
punctuated: 興，人文漸著，百篇之書斷自唐虞，史學之淵源尚矣。筆削之旨載在《春秋》，聖心之要典傳焉。自是以後，代必有史，史必有官。然記者非一時，作者非一手，世之所稱，遷、固二子而已。遷之史始於黃帝，終於麟趾，辨而不華，質而不俚，其文直，其事核。固之史起自高帝，終於平帝，贍而不穢，詳而有體，不激詭，不抑抗。蒐羅千古，錯綜一代，皆富有良史之才，而卓然名家者也。然二子作之，將以傳信方來；君子議之，或致疑於後世。若王充著書，甲班而乙馬；張輔持論，劣固而優遷。各出己見，論者不一。觀其天官有志，遷之序也，固以天文更之，不知非關於漢之一代，何益乎？河渠有志，遷之編也，固以溝洫易之，不知非出於漢之所治，何當乎？易封禪以郊祀，不載原廟、宗廟之事，
translation_en:
…arose, and human culture gradually became manifest. The hundred chapters of the Book of Documents begin with the eras of Tang Yao and Yu Shun: the origins of historical learning are ancient indeed. The principles governing what to retain and what to excise are embodied in the Spring and Autumn Annals, through which the essential canons of the sage’s mind have been transmitted. From that time onward, every dynasty necessarily had its history, and historical recording necessarily had its officials. Yet these records were not made at a single time, nor were they composed by a single hand. Those whom the world praises are simply the two masters, Sima Qian and Ban Gu.

Sima Qian’s history begins with the Yellow Emperor and ends with the unicorn’s appearance [?; the transcription reads “unicorn’s toes”]. It is discriminating without being ornate, plain without being vulgar; its prose is straightforward and its facts sound. Ban Gu’s history begins with Emperor Gao and ends with Emperor Ping. It is ample without being cluttered, detailed yet orderly, neither extravagant nor bizarre, neither unduly disparaging nor excessively laudatory. Gathering material from across the ages and weaving together the affairs of a dynasty, both possessed abundant talent as fine historians and stood out as masters in their own right.

Yet although these two composed their works to transmit trustworthy accounts to future generations, the judgments of learned gentlemen have sometimes occasioned doubts among later readers. Thus Wang Chong, in his writings, ranked Ban first and Sima second; Zhang Fu, in his arguments, judged Gu inferior and Qian superior. Each advanced his own view, and their assessments differed.

Consider the treatise on the Celestial Offices, which Qian arranged: Gu changed its title to Celestial Patterns. Did he not realize that, unless it concerned the Han dynasty specifically, what benefit did this bring? The treatise on Rivers and Canals was compiled by Qian; Gu replaced its title with Ditches and Watercourses. Did he not realize that, unless it dealt with works undertaken by the Han, how was this appropriate? He replaced the title Feng and Shan Sacrifices with Suburban Sacrifices, yet did not record the affairs of the subsidiary ancestral temple and the imperial ancestral temples…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
議失之太簡也易食貨以平準妄比九府
貨泉之周法失之太謬也若夫表以著興
亡理亂之大畧遷有十表而固損其二書
以載制度沿革之大端遷有八書而固增
其二又於八書之外自立私見志五行不
免劉氏之駁其錯志地里終貽邵氏之譏
其疎此遷固之書有同異而同異之間優
劣見矣至若遷之所序合本末三千餘年
===
之事斷於五十萬言之下何其簡也固之
所序以始終二百餘年之事溢乎八十萬
言之外何其繁也遷傳循吏取叔敖子產
公儀休石奢李離五人人雖寡而名實不
副者不與焉固傳循吏取文翁黃霸龔遂
召信臣王成朱邑六人人雖多而偽增戶
口者亦與焉此遷固之書有繁簡而繁簡
之中優劣見矣然遷雖優也序帝紀始於
punctuated:
議失之太簡也。易食貨以平準，妄比九府貨泉之周法，失之太謬也。若夫表以著興亡理亂之大畧，遷有十表，而固損其二；書以載制度沿革之大端，遷有八書，而固增其二。又於八書之外，自立私見，志五行，不免劉氏之駁其錯；志地里，終貽邵氏之譏其疎。此遷固之書有同異，而同異之間優劣見矣。
至若遷之所序，合本末三千餘年之事，斷於五十萬言之下，何其簡也！固之所序，以始終二百餘年之事，溢乎八十萬言之外，何其繁也！遷傳循吏，取叔敖、子產、公儀休、石奢、李離五人，人雖寡，而名實不副者不與焉。固傳循吏，取文翁、黃霸、龔遂、召信臣、王成、朱邑六人，人雖多，而偽增戶口者亦與焉。此遷固之書有繁簡，而繁簡之中優劣見矣。
然遷雖優也，序帝紀始於
translation_en:
…the discussion errs in being too brief. Replacing “Food and Money” with “Price Equalization” [?], and groundlessly equating it with the Zhou system of currency administered by the Nine Treasuries, errs in being altogether too mistaken. As for tables, which set forth the broad outlines of rise and fall, order and disorder, Sima Qian had ten, whereas Ban Gu reduced their number by two. As for treatises, which record the principal developments in institutions and regulations, Sima Qian had eight, whereas Ban Gu increased their number by two. Moreover, beyond those eight treatises, Ban Gu advanced personal views of his own. His treatise on the Five Phases could not escape Liu’s refutation of its errors; his treatise on geography ultimately invited Shao’s criticism of its deficiencies. Thus the works of Sima Qian and Ban Gu have similarities and differences, and through these their relative merits become apparent.
As for Sima Qian’s account, he brought together events spanning more than three thousand years, from beginning to end, and kept them within five hundred thousand words. How concise! Ban Gu’s account covers events spanning just over two hundred years from beginning to end, yet exceeds eight hundred thousand words. How prolix! In his biographies of exemplary officials, Sima Qian selected five men: Shu Ao, Zichan, Gongyi Xiu, Shi She, and Li Li. Though few in number, they included none whose actual conduct failed to match his reputation. In his biographies of exemplary officials, Ban Gu selected six men: Wen Weng, Huang Ba, Gong Sui, Shao Xinchen, Wang Cheng, and Zhu Yi. Though more numerous, they included even one who falsely inflated household and population figures. Thus the works of Sima Qian and Ban Gu differ in prolixity and concision, and within these differences their relative merits become apparent.
Yet although Sima Qian is superior, his account in the Basic Annals of the emperors begins with…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
黃帝而五帝之數不備律管减三分而黃
鍾之制未精遷有二失不可掩爾固誠劣
也然王子侯不稱姓而下卷書姓默寓感
慨之意食貨志言財利而歷載張湯實原
用刑之由固有二得不可誣也由是觀之
遷優於固古人之論審矣君子固不可過
為矯激之論易地皆然後世之說失矣愚
亦未見其為至當之評蓋以作史無定法
===
本之春秋有定法考史無定論本之春秋
有定論秉史筆者有如子長孟堅之才可
謂富矣若求春秋精微之義然專門名家
猶不免後世之議區區管窺蠡測何敢妄
議二子之優劣但明問之下不容或默惟
恕其狂瞽進而教之幸甚
第三問
陳𨫼
punctuated:
黃帝，而五帝之數不備；律管减三分，而黃鍾之制未精。遷有二失，不可掩爾。固誠劣也，然王子侯不稱姓，而下卷書姓，默寓感慨之意；食貨志言財利，而歷載張湯，實原用刑之由。固有二得，不可誣也。由是觀之，遷優於固，古人之論審矣，君子固不可過為矯激之論；易地皆然，後世之說失矣，愚亦未見其為至當之評。蓋以作史無定法，本之春秋，有定法；考史無定論，本之春秋，有定論。秉史筆者，有如子長、孟堅之才，可謂富矣。若求春秋精微之義，然專門名家，猶不免後世之議。區區管窺蠡測，何敢妄議二子之優劣？但明問之下，不容或默，惟恕其狂瞽，進而教之，幸甚！

第三問
陳𨫼
translation_en:
…the Yellow Emperor, yet his account does not include the full complement of the Five Emperors; he reduces the pitch pipes by three parts [?], yet his specification of the Yellow Bell pitch standard is insufficiently precise. These are two faults in Sima Qian that cannot be concealed. Ban Gu is indeed inferior. Yet he omits surnames for imperial sons enfeoffed as marquises, while recording surnames in the lower volume, thereby tacitly expressing his regret; and his Treatise on Food and Money discusses wealth and profit but also recounts Zhang Tang’s activities at length, thus tracing the underlying reasons for the use of punishments. These are two merits in Ban Gu that cannot be denied.

Viewed in this light, the judgment of the ancients that Sima Qian was superior to Ban Gu was well considered; a gentleman certainly should not go too far in advancing provocatively contrarian arguments. The later claim that, had they exchanged places, each would have done as the other did is mistaken. I, too, cannot regard it as an entirely fitting assessment. For although writing history has no fixed method, grounding it in the Spring and Autumn Annals gives it a fixed method; although judging history admits no fixed verdict, grounding that judgment in the Spring and Autumn Annals gives it a fixed verdict. Those who wield the historian’s brush with talents such as those of Zichang and Mengjian [Sima Qian and Ban Gu] may be called richly endowed. Yet if one seeks the subtle and profound meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, even these recognized masters of their respective traditions remain subject to criticism by later generations. With my paltry understanding—like viewing the heavens through a tube or measuring the sea with a ladle—how dare I rashly pronounce upon the relative merits of these two men? But faced with your discerning question, I cannot remain silent. I ask only that you pardon my rashness and blindness and favor me with further instruction; I would be most fortunate!

Third Question
Chen 𨫼 [given-name reading uncertain: ?].

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導黄批天地萬物之理敷說無
遺盖嘗用心於格物之學者
考試官教諭鄭批辨析精詳必刻意於理學者
考試官學正朱批善能窮理格物
欲知天地萬物之詳當窮天地萬物之理
盖天地萬物本吾一體也以吾心之理窮
之則天地萬物之理如視諸掌矣豈待求
之於外哉請試陳之夫陽氣輕清而上浮
===
者天陰氣重濁而下凝者地天地覆載萬
物而天地則自相依附也陽之精爲日陰
之精爲月日月照臨下土而太極則爲之
主宰也日一日行不及天一度故一歲一
周天而遲月一日行不及天十三度有奇
故一月一周天而速曰春分曰秋分以陰
陽之中也曰夏至曰冬至以陰陽之極也
天左旋矣日月麗天亦左旋但天行速而
punctuated:
同考試官訓導黄批：「天地萬物之理，敷說無遺，盖嘗用心於格物之學者。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「辨析精詳，必刻意於理學者。」
考試官學正朱批：「善能窮理格物。」
欲知天地萬物之詳，當窮天地萬物之理。盖天地萬物本吾一體也，以吾心之理窮之，則天地萬物之理如視諸掌矣，豈待求之於外哉？請試陳之。夫陽氣輕清而上浮者，天；陰氣重濁而下凝者，地。天地覆載萬物，而天地則自相依附也。陽之精爲日，陰之精爲月。日月照臨下土，而太極則爲之主宰也。日一日行不及天一度，故一歲一周天而遲；月一日行不及天十三度有奇，故一月一周天而速。曰春分，曰秋分，以陰陽之中也；曰夏至，曰冬至，以陰陽之極也。天左旋矣，日月麗天亦左旋，但天行速而
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: “He expounds the principles of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things without omission. He has evidently devoted himself to the learning of investigating things.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “His distinctions and analyses are precise and thorough. He must have applied himself assiduously to the Learning of Principle.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, School Instructor: “He is adept at fathoming principles and investigating things.”
To understand Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things in detail, one must fathom their principles. Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things fundamentally form one body with me. If I investigate them through the principles in my own mind, their principles will be as clear as something viewed in the palm of my hand. Why should I need to seek them outside myself? Let me attempt to explain.
Yang qi, light and clear, floats upward and constitutes Heaven; yin qi, heavy and turbid, congeals below and constitutes Earth. Heaven covers and Earth supports the myriad things, while Heaven and Earth themselves depend upon one another. The essence of yang constitutes the sun; the essence of yin constitutes the moon. The sun and moon shine upon the earth below, while the Supreme Ultimate governs them. In its daily motion the sun falls one degree short of Heaven; thus it completes one circuit of Heaven in a year and is slow. In its daily motion the moon falls thirteen degrees and a fraction short of Heaven; thus it completes one circuit of Heaven in a month and is swift. The spring and autumn equinoxes are so called because yin and yang are in balance; the summer and winter solstices are so called because yin and yang reach their extremes. Heaven revolves to the left, and the sun and moon, attached to Heaven, also revolve to the left. Yet Heaven moves swiftly, while…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
日月遲故自天視之則見其退而右轉焉
日常盈矣月受日光亦常盈但與日近則
為所蔽故自下視之則見其偏而有虧焉
日為太陽月為太陰星為少陽辰為少陰
陰陽分太少者以此三年餘分之積得三
十二日有竒故三年一閏又積二年之後
通得五十四日有竒故五年再閏閏位之
置以近者以此或去極之度多或去極之
===
度少此所以有日長日短也光生於日之
所照魄生於日之所蔽此所以為生明生
魄也北極出地上三十六度故常見不隱
南極入地下三十六度故常隱不見月中
間有黑處山河之影掩映爾雷無形而有
聲陰陽之氣擊搏爾如風如雨乃火氣水
氣之化如霜如露乃金氣土氣之為如烟
雲如霾霧又何莫非水土之氣乎若夫四
punctuated: 日月遲，故自天視之，則見其退而右轉焉。日常盈矣，月受日光亦常盈，但與日近，則為所蔽，故自下視之，則見其偏而有虧焉。日為太陽，月為太陰，星為少陽，辰為少陰，陰陽分太少者以此。三年餘分之積，得三十二日有竒，故三年一閏；又積二年之後，通得五十四日有竒，故五年再閏。閏位之置以近者以此。或去極之度多，或去極之度少，此所以有日長日短也。光生於日之所照，魄生於日之所蔽，此所以為生明、生魄也。北極出地上三十六度，故常見不隱；南極入地下三十六度，故常隱不見。月中間有黑處，山河之影掩映爾。雷無形而有聲，陰陽之氣擊搏爾。如風如雨，乃火氣水氣之化；如霜如露，乃金氣土氣之為；如烟雲如霾霧，又何莫非水土之氣乎？若夫四
translation_en: …the sun and moon move slowly. Thus, viewed from heaven, they appear to fall back and turn to the right. The sun is always full, and the moon, receiving the sun’s light, is also always full. Yet when it is close to the sun, it is obscured by it; thus, viewed from below, it appears incomplete and diminished. The sun is greater yang; the moon is greater yin; the stars are lesser yang; and the celestial stations are lesser yin. This is how yin and yang are divided into greater and lesser. The surplus fractions accumulated over three years amount to thirty-two days and a fraction; hence there is one intercalary month every three years. After another two years’ accumulation, the total reaches fifty-four days and a fraction; hence there are two intercalary months in five years. This is why the placement of intercalary months follows what is near [?]. Sometimes the angular distance from the pole is greater, and sometimes it is smaller: this accounts for long and short days. Brightness arises where the sun illuminates, and the dark portion arises where the sun’s light is obscured: this accounts for the emergence of the moon’s bright and dark portions. The north celestial pole stands thirty-six degrees above the earth and is therefore always visible, never hidden. The south celestial pole lies thirty-six degrees below the earth and is therefore always hidden, never visible. The dark patches within the moon are merely the shadows of mountains and rivers showing upon it. Thunder has no form but has sound: it is merely the collision and clash of the qi of yin and yang. Wind and rain are transformations of the qi of fire and water; frost and dew are the workings of the qi of metal and earth. As for smoky clouds, haze, and fog, which of these is not also the qi of water and earth? As for the four…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
方水土一也陰氣盛於西北故多寒陽氣
盛於東南故多暖天下人品一也西北風
氣剛勁而人多強東南風氣柔弱而人多
弱禽蟲感氣候而鳴伏變化草木觸氣候
而榮悴開落龍之或潜或飛其神妙變化
不測也麟鳳無種而生鍾天地泰和之氣
也麟之角端有肉仁厚而止觸騶虞不食
生物仁心之自然地在水中而不沉一氣
===
運之爾水歸東海而不溢氣盡而散爾海
潮隨朔望之候乗陰盛也黃河自崑崙而
出有其源也以為憑子胥之怒自天上而
來非世俗之談乎是天地也萬物也一太
極為之根柢一陰陽為之樞紐執是而觀
則天地雖大萬物雖夥其所以然之理皆
在吾一心之内矣管見如斯未知是否惟
執事其與進焉
punctuated:
方水土一也，陰氣盛於西北，故多寒；陽氣盛於東南，故多暖。天下人品一也，西北風氣剛勁，而人多強；東南風氣柔弱，而人多弱。禽蟲感氣候而鳴伏變化，草木觸氣候而榮悴開落。龍之或潜或飛，其神妙變化不測也。麟鳳無種而生，鍾天地泰和之氣也。麟之角端有肉，仁厚而止觸；騶虞不食生物，仁心之自然。地在水中而不沉，一氣運之爾；水歸東海而不溢，氣盡而散爾。海潮隨朔望之候，乗陰盛也；黃河自崑崙而出，有其源也。以為憑子胥之怒、自天上而來，非世俗之談乎？

是天地也，萬物也，一太極為之根柢，一陰陽為之樞紐。執是而觀，則天地雖大，萬物雖夥，其所以然之理，皆在吾一心之内矣。管見如斯，未知是否，惟執事其與進焉。
translation_en:
…the waters and soils of the regions are alike. Yin qi predominates in the northwest, so it is generally cold; yang qi predominates in the southeast, so it is generally warm. Human nature is alike throughout the world, yet the winds and qi of the northwest are firm and forceful, and its people are mostly strong; those of the southeast are soft and yielding, and its people are mostly weak. Birds and insects respond to seasonal conditions by calling, becoming dormant, and undergoing transformations; plants and trees respond by flourishing and withering, blossoming and shedding their flowers. Dragons sometimes lurk beneath the waters and sometimes fly: their wondrous transformations are unfathomable. Qilin and phoenixes arise without breeding stock, embodying the concentrated qi of Heaven and Earth's supreme harmony. The qilin has flesh at the tip of its horn; benevolent and gentle, it refrains from goring. The zouyu does not eat living creatures: this is the spontaneous expression of its benevolent heart. Earth rests amid water without sinking simply because the single qi sustains its movement. Water flows into the eastern sea without overflowing simply because its qi is exhausted and disperses. Ocean tides follow the new and full moons because they take advantage of yin's predominance. The Yellow River issues from Kunlun because its source lies there. To suppose that the tides depend upon Zixu's wrath, or that the river comes down from heaven—is this not vulgar talk?

Heaven and Earth and the myriad things have the single Supreme Ultimate as their root and yin and yang as their pivot. Viewed in this light, although Heaven and Earth are vast and the myriad things numerous, the principles explaining why they are so all lie within my own single mind. Such is my limited understanding; I do not know whether it is correct. I ask you, honored examiner, to help me advance further.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第四問
余敬
同考試官教諭黄批此策剖析明白且推本
在於得人盖士之有才識者也
考試官教諭鄭批仁政一策議論平正必佳
士也
考試官學正朱批政待人而後行此策歸重於
此最是他日致用當不負斯言矣
===
欲治天下在脩爲治之法欲行治法在擇
天下之才省刑薄斂者治之法也任擇賢
才者治之原也有是法則治得其人則存
欲天下之治而此法不脩焉治不可致也
欲行爲治之法而國無人焉法不可行也
此天地之常經古今之通義也舍此則國
不可以爲國况天下乎昔孟軻有曰省刑
罰薄稅斂二者仁政之大目正當
punctuated:
第四問
余敬
同考試官教諭黄批：此策剖析明白，且推本在於得人，盖士之有才識者也。
考試官教諭鄭批：仁政一策，議論平正，必佳士也。
考試官學正朱批：政待人而後行，此策歸重於此，最是。他日致用，當不負斯言矣。
欲治天下，在脩爲治之法；欲行治法，在擇天下之才。省刑薄斂者，治之法也；任擇賢才者，治之原也。有是法則治，得其人則存。欲天下之治，而此法不脩焉，治不可致也；欲行爲治之法，而國無人焉，法不可行也。此天地之常經，古今之通義也。舍此，則國不可以爲國，况天下乎？昔孟軻有曰：「省刑罰，薄稅斂。」二者，仁政之大目，正當
translation_en:
Fourth Question
Yu Jing
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: This policy essay analyzes the matter clearly and, moreover, traces its foundation to securing the right people. Its author is indeed a scholar of talent and discernment.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: This policy essay on humane government presents balanced and sound arguments. Its author must be a worthy scholar.
Examiner Zhu, School Instructor, comments: Government depends upon the right people before it can be put into effect. This essay places its chief emphasis here, which is entirely correct. When the author puts his abilities to use in the future, he should live up to these words.
To bring order to all under Heaven, one must cultivate the methods of government; to implement those methods, one must select talented people from throughout the realm. Reducing punishments and lightening levies are methods of government; selecting and appointing worthy and talented people are its foundation. With these methods there is order; with the right people, they endure. If one desires order throughout the realm but does not cultivate these methods, order cannot be achieved. If one wishes to implement the methods of government but the state lacks the right people, those methods cannot be put into effect. This is the constant principle of Heaven and Earth, the universal truth of antiquity and the present. Abandon it, and a state cannot function as a state—how much less can all under Heaven be governed? Meng Ke once said: “Reduce punishments and lighten taxes and levies.” These two are the principal features of humane government, and are precisely …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今所急聞者刑罰天之所以齊民其倫要截然
也惡可苟耶舜典因天討而作五刑曰墨
劓剕宮大辟是也周官糾萬民而叙八刑
曰不孝不睦不姻不弟不任不恤造言亂
民是也此固刑之常矣而議獄緩死垂於
羲易赦過宥罪著於虞書陽舒陰慘取舍
於輕重之間仁漸義涵流行於常法之外
何莫而非以省刑為心哉賦稅上之所以
===
取下其法制秩如也惡可易耶禹貢則三
壤而成田賦非九州穀土品節上中下三
等者乎周官辨五物而制地征非山林川
澤丘陵墳衍原隰者乎此固賦之常矣而
散利薄征用於荒年弛力舍禁行於饑歲
取民之仁常存乎中正之法恤民之念每
寓於凶荒之政何莫而非以薄賦為意哉
刑制在虞周不能不用也董子乃謂天道
punctuated: 今所急聞者，刑罰，天之所以齊民，其倫要截然也，惡可苟耶？《舜典》因天討而作五刑，曰墨、劓、剕、宮、大辟是也。《周官》糾萬民而叙八刑，曰不孝、不睦、不姻、不弟、不任、不恤、造言、亂民是也。此固刑之常矣，而議獄緩死垂於《羲易》，赦過宥罪著於《虞書》。陽舒陰慘，取舍於輕重之間；仁漸義涵，流行於常法之外。何莫而非以省刑為心哉？賦稅，上之所以取下，其法制秩如也，惡可易耶？《禹貢》則三壤而成田賦，非九州穀土品節上中下三等者乎？《周官》辨五物而制地征，非山林、川澤、丘陵、墳衍、原隰者乎？此固賦之常矣，而散利薄征用於荒年，弛力舍禁行於饑歲。取民之仁常存乎中正之法，恤民之念每寓於凶荒之政。何莫而非以薄賦為意哉？刑制在虞周，不能不用也。董子乃謂天道
translation_en:
…what urgently needs to be heard today [?]. Punishments are Heaven’s means of bringing the people into order; their principles and essentials are sharply defined. How could they be applied carelessly? The Canon of Shun (Shun dian), following Heaven’s punitive justice, established the five punishments: tattooing, cutting off the nose, amputating the feet, castration, and death. The Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan), in correcting the myriad people, set out eight categories of punishment: for being unfilial, failing to maintain harmony among kinsmen, failing in relations with relatives by marriage, disrespecting elders, failing to discharge responsibilities, failing to aid those in need, fabricating rumors, and throwing the people into disorder. These are indeed the standing norms of punishment. Yet deliberating carefully over criminal cases and delaying executions are teachings handed down in Fuxi’s Book of Changes (Xi Yi), while pardoning errors and treating offenses leniently are recorded in the Book of Yu (Yu shu). Yang is gentle and yin severe: choices are made between lighter and heavier penalties. Benevolence permeates and righteousness suffuses, extending beyond the standing laws. Which of these does not take the reduction of punishments as its guiding concern?

Taxes are the means by which those above take from those below; their laws and institutions are orderly. How could they be altered lightly? The Tribute of Yu (Yu gong) based land taxation on three classes of soil: was this not the grading of grain-producing soils throughout the Nine Provinces into upper, middle, and lower classes? The Offices of Zhou distinguished five categories of land and their products in establishing land levies: were these not mountains and forests, rivers and marshes, hills and knolls, elevated riverbanks and level expanses, and uplands and lowlands? These are indeed the standing norms of taxation. Yet distributing resources and reducing levies were measures used in years of dearth, while easing labor service and lifting prohibitions were practiced in years of famine. Benevolence in taking from the people is always preserved within balanced and proper laws; concern for the people is continually embodied in policies for crop failure and famine. Which of these does not aim at lightening taxation?

Under Yu and Zhou, the system of punishments could not go unused. Yet Master Dong said that the Way of Heaven…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之大在陰陽陽爲德而陰爲刑故陽常居
大夏以長養生育爲事陰常居大冬積於
空虚無用之處王者承天意以從事任德
而不任刑盖不專於任刑耳是豈刑不可
任哉貢法在大禹未爲不善也龍子乃謂
貢者校數歳之中立常定之法豐年多取
不爲虐凶年舉貸以足盈在當時未爲不
善於後世不能無弊盖用法者之弊耳是
===
===
豈法之弊哉我
國朝統馭六合留心民事慮民之不知避也
創制律令以禁天下之奸慮民之或寃抑
也列職中外以司天下之刑其虞周省刑
之心乎然而奉法脩職者未必皆皐陶蘇
公也故刑益煩而民益玩始有不得其死
者矣恐取民之無制也均平賦税以理郡
國之財恐傷民之力也屢頒
punctuated:
之大在陰陽，陽爲德而陰爲刑。故陽常居大夏，以長養生育爲事；陰常居大冬，積於空虚無用之處。王者承天意以從事，任德而不任刑。盖不專於任刑耳，是豈刑不可任哉？貢法在大禹未爲不善也，龍子乃謂：「貢者，校數歳之中，立常定之法。豐年多取不爲虐，凶年舉貸以足。」盈在當時未爲不善，於後世不能無弊，盖用法者之弊耳，是豈法之弊哉？
我國朝統馭六合，留心民事。慮民之不知避也，創制律令以禁天下之奸；慮民之或寃抑也，列職中外以司天下之刑，其虞周省刑之心乎？然而奉法脩職者未必皆皐陶、蘇公也，故刑益煩而民益玩，始有不得其死者矣。恐取民之無制也，均平賦税以理郡國之財；恐傷民之力也，屢頒
translation_en:
…the great principles lie in yin and yang: yang represents virtue, while yin represents punishment. Thus yang constantly occupies high summer, taking growth, nourishment, generation, and nurture as its work; yin constantly occupies deep winter, accumulating in empty places where it serves no purpose. The true king undertakes his affairs in accordance with Heaven’s intention, relying on virtue rather than punishment. This merely means that he does not rely exclusively on punishment. How could it mean that punishment cannot be employed?
The tribute system under Yu the Great was by no means unsound. Yet Longzi said: “Under the tribute system, the average of several years is assessed to establish a fixed, standing rule. In a plentiful year, taking much would not be oppressive; in a famine year, people borrow to make up the required amount.” The surplus [?] was not unsatisfactory at the time, but in later ages abuses inevitably arose. These were merely abuses committed by those administering the system. How could they be defects in the system itself?
Our imperial dynasty governs all within the six directions and attends closely to the people’s affairs. Concerned that the people might not know what to avoid, it established statutes and ordinances to prohibit wrongdoing throughout the realm. Concerned that the people might suffer injustice or oppression, it instituted offices at court and in the provinces to administer the realm’s punishments. Does this not embody the intention of Yu and Zhou to reduce punishments? Yet those who uphold the laws and discharge their offices are not necessarily all men like Gao Yao and Duke Su. Thus punishments become ever more numerous, while the people become ever more heedless, and some consequently fail to meet a natural death. Fearing that exactions from the people might have no limits, the dynasty equalized taxes to regulate the finances of the prefectures and territories. Fearing that the people’s strength might be exhausted, it repeatedly promulgated…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
恩詔以蘇田野之困其夏周薄賦之仁乎然而
期會辦集者未必皆后稷君奭也故賦益
重而民益殘始有不遂其生者矣誠得温
良重厚之士如皐陶如蘇公之輩以司刑
政任廉潔有守之人如后稷如君奭之流
以領財賦處已誠廉矣則厚其禄榮其身
雖有過三宥再宥而後加以罪取於民誠
貪矣則收其禄役其身俾不齒於士則人
===
人力於事功群才効其職業刑措不用培
基本於萬年外户不閉跨四海而無斬治
法其有不舉者乎天下其有不治者乎管
見如斯不識執事以為何如
第五問
張紹齡
同考試官訓導左批塲中多為此策所窘惟
是卷條答詳明處置允當非平素究於兵法者不能也
punctuated:
恩詔，以蘇田野之困，其夏周薄賦之仁乎？然而期會辦集者，未必皆后稷、君奭也。故賦益重，而民益殘，始有不遂其生者矣。誠得温良重厚之士，如皐陶、如蘇公之輩，以司刑政；任廉潔有守之人，如后稷、如君奭之流，以領財賦。處已誠廉矣，則厚其禄，榮其身，雖有過，三宥再宥而後加以罪；取於民誠貪矣，則收其禄，役其身，俾不齒於士。則人人力於事功，群才効其職業，刑措不用，培基本於萬年；外户不閉，跨四海而無斬。治法其有不舉者乎？天下其有不治者乎？管見如斯，不識執事以為何如？

第五問
張紹齡

同考試官訓導左批：塲中多為此策所窘，惟是卷條答詳明，處置允當，非平素究於兵法者不能也。
translation_en:
…gracious edicts to relieve the hardships of the countryside: is this not the benevolence of the Xia and Zhou in keeping taxation light? Yet those responsible for meeting deadlines and completing collections are not necessarily all men like Hou Ji and Jun Shi. Thus taxes become ever heavier and the people ever more afflicted, until some can no longer sustain their lives. If truly gentle, upright, and substantial men, like Gao Yao and the Duke of Su, were obtained to administer penal affairs, and incorruptible men of firm principle, like Hou Ji and Jun Shi, were appointed to oversee revenue and taxation, then those truly honest in their conduct should receive generous stipends and personal honors. Even if they committed an offense, they should be pardoned three times and pardoned again before punishment was imposed. Those truly rapacious in extracting from the people should have their stipends withdrawn and be subjected to labor service, so that they would no longer be counted among the scholars. Then everyone would exert himself in public service, and all men of talent would perform the duties of their offices. Punishments would be set aside unused, and the foundations strengthened for ten thousand years. Outer doors would remain unbarred, and this order would extend throughout the Four Seas without interruption [?]. What measure of government would then remain unimplemented? How could the realm fail to be well governed? Such is my limited view; I do not know what you, honored examiners, will think of it.

Fifth Policy Question
Zhang Shaoling

Comment by Associate Examiner Zuo, an Assistant Instructor: Many in the examination hall were stymied by this policy question. This paper alone answers each point fully and clearly, proposing sound and appropriate measures. This could only have been accomplished by someone who had regularly studied military methods.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭批考拠詳而區處當足以觀其
所學矣
考試官學正朱批據古法而酌時宜必有用
之士也
論兵法於古人當考其實用兵法於今日
當適其宜夫不考其實則不知古法之善
不適其宜則不知變通之術又何能盡用
法之妙哉何則兵凶器戰危事聖人不得
===
已而用之非徒事乎詭道也蓋有仁義存
乎其間焉自吕望為師尚父則兵昉有法
自黄帝征討蚩尤則兵始有戰故六韜為
太公相周之法三畧為黄石佐漢之術不
可不知也八陣為孔明兵法之最一成為
司馬賦兵之原不可不識也若夫春秋之
時諸侯之兵有伐侵戰圍入遷之異然伐
則聲罪致討侵則無名興師戰則兩兵相
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭批：「考拠詳而區處當，足以觀其所學矣。」
考試官學正朱批：「據古法而酌時宜，必有用之士也。」
論兵法於古人，當考其實；用兵法於今日，當適其宜。夫不考其實，則不知古法之善；不適其宜，則不知變通之術，又何能盡用法之妙哉？何則？兵，凶器；戰，危事。聖人不得已而用之，非徒事乎詭道也，蓋有仁義存乎其間焉。自吕望為師尚父，則兵昉有法；自黄帝征討蚩尤，則兵始有戰。故《六韜》為太公相周之法，《三畧》為黄石佐漢之術，不可不知也。八陣為孔明兵法之最，一成為司馬賦兵之原，不可不識也。若夫春秋之時，諸侯之兵有伐、侵、戰、圍、入、遷之異。然伐則聲罪致討，侵則無名興師，戰則兩兵相
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor (jiaoyu): “His examination of the evidence is thorough, and his arrangements appropriate: these suffice to show what he has learned.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor (xuezheng): “He draws on ancient methods while weighing the needs of the times. He must surely be a man capable of useful service.”

When discussing the military methods of the ancients, one should investigate their actual practice; when applying military methods today, one should adapt them to present circumstances. Without investigating their actual practice, one cannot understand the merits of ancient methods; without adapting them to circumstances, one cannot understand the art of responding to change. How, then, could one fully realize the subtlety of employing these methods? Why is this so? Weapons are instruments of ill omen, and warfare is a perilous undertaking. The sages resorted to them only when compelled. They did not devote themselves merely to deception: benevolence and righteousness were present within their practice.

With Lü Wang’s appointment as Grand Preceptor, Father Shang, military affairs first acquired systematic methods; with the Yellow Emperor’s campaign against Chiyou, armed conflict first began. Thus the Six Secret Teachings contain the methods by which the Grand Duke assisted the Zhou, and the Three Strategies contain the arts by which Huangshi aided the Han. These must be known. The Eight Formations represent the finest of Kongming’s military methods, and the land unit of one cheng was the basis of the Minister of War’s military levies. These must be understood.

In the Spring and Autumn period, the military operations of the regional lords were distinguished as punitive expeditions, incursions, battles, sieges, entries, and relocations. A punitive expedition proclaimed the enemy’s crimes and exacted punishment; an incursion mobilized troops without a stated justification; a battle was when two armies mutually …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
接壤則繚其城邑入則造其國都遷則徙
其朝市則得失可議矣有敗取襲追戍以
之殊然敗則詭道而勝取則悉虜而俘襲
則輕行而揜追則已去而躡戍則聚兵而
守以則用弱假强則是非可别矣至於大
舜舞干羽於兩階七旬而格有苗文武應
天順人一怒而安天下斯皆聖人之德化
何兵法之有吳漢討公孫述而八戰八克
===
孔明征孟獲而七縱七擒斯皆良將之竒
畧何兵法之為夫兵法之善莫備於孫子
本義其曰道曰天曰地曰將曰法非經之
以五事者乎知可戰不可戰識衆寡之用
上下同欲以虞待不虞將能而君不御非
知勝有五者乎以至地生度度生量量生
數數生稱稱生勝此軍形之五法也與夫
五聲之變五色之變五味之變此兵勢之
punctuated: 接，壤則繚其城邑，入則造其國都，遷則徙其朝市，則得失可議矣。有敗、取、襲、追、戍、以之殊，然敗則詭道而勝，取則悉虜而俘，襲則輕行而揜，追則已去而躡，戍則聚兵而守，以則用弱假强，則是非可别矣。至於大舜舞干羽於兩階，七旬而格有苗；文武應天順人，一怒而安天下，斯皆聖人之德化，何兵法之有？吳漢討公孫述而八戰八克，孔明征孟獲而七縱七擒，斯皆良將之竒畧，何兵法之為？夫兵法之善，莫備於《孫子本義》。其曰道、曰天、曰地、曰將、曰法，非經之以五事者乎？知可戰不可戰，識衆寡之用，上下同欲，以虞待不虞，將能而君不御，非知勝有五者乎？以至地生度，度生量，量生數，數生稱，稱生勝，此軍形之五法也。與夫五聲之變、五色之變、五味之變，此兵勢之
translation_en: …engage one another; “encirclement” [?; transcribed as 壤] means surrounding their cities and towns; “entry” means reaching their capital; and “relocation” means moving their court and marketplace. The merits and failings of these actions can thus be discussed. There are also distinctions among “defeating,” “taking,” “raiding,” “pursuing,” “garrisoning,” and “employing.” “Defeating” means winning through deception; “taking” means capturing the enemy in their entirety; “raiding” means advancing lightly and taking the enemy by surprise; “pursuing” means following on the heels of an enemy who has departed; “garrisoning” means assembling troops for defense; and “employing” means using the weak and borrowing the strength of the strong. Right and wrong can thus be distinguished. As for the great Shun, he had dancers perform with shields and feathers between the two stairways, and within seventy days the Youmiao submitted. Kings Wen and Wu responded to Heaven and followed the wishes of the people; with one outburst of wrath, they brought peace to all under Heaven. These were all instances of the transforming virtue of sages: what need was there for military methods? Wu Han attacked Gongsun Shu and won eight victories in eight battles. Kongming campaigned against Meng Huo, releasing him seven times and capturing him seven times. These were all extraordinary strategies of fine generals: what part did military methods play? Now, nowhere are the excellences of military methods more fully set forth than in the Original Meaning of Master Sun (Sunzi benyi). Its enumeration of the Way, Heaven, Earth, the commander, and method—is this not the assessment of warfare through five factors? Knowing when one can and cannot fight; understanding how to employ large and small forces; having superiors and subordinates share the same purpose; awaiting the unprepared with preparedness; and having an able commander whose ruler does not constrain him—are these not the five means of knowing victory? Furthermore, terrain gives rise to measurement, measurement to estimation of quantity, quantity to numbers, numbers to weighing relative strengths, and weighing relative strengths to victory: these are the five methods of military dispositions. Together with the variations of the five notes, the five colors, and the five flavors, these are, in the strategic force of armies, …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
正之變也凡用兵之法有九變之利將能
通之則知用兵矣苟有五危焉用兵之災
非主將之過乎曰通曰掛曰支曰隘曰險
曰遠此六者乃地之道將能察之則利於
用兵矣曰走曰弛曰陷曰崩曰亂曰北此
六者非天地之災乃主將之過也吁兵法
原無得失而將之所行則有得失也用三
軍之衆若使一人則投之無所往使三軍
===
一心死鬭以取勝此無政之令亦法之善
也若敵來攻我順詳其意示弱而勿拒彼
必并力專向而無別謀我則設竒正之兵
先為歸路之伏故雖千里之外可殺敵國
之將此巧能成事非法之善而何若與敵
遇微與之期如處女之弱彼必驕怠而露
其隙我則乗隙用竒勢如脫兎敵不及拒
此巧能取勝亦法之善也然戰勝攻取雖
punctuated: 正之變也。凡用兵之法，有九變之利，將能通之，則知用兵矣。苟有五危焉，用兵之災，非主將之過乎？曰通、曰掛、曰支、曰隘、曰險、曰遠，此六者乃地之道，將能察之，則利於用兵矣。曰走、曰弛、曰陷、曰崩、曰亂、曰北，此六者非天地之災，乃主將之過也。吁！兵法原無得失，而將之所行則有得失也。用三軍之衆，若使一人，則投之無所往，使三軍一心死鬭以取勝，此無政之令，亦法之善也。若敵來攻我，順詳其意，示弱而勿拒，彼必并力專向而無別謀。我則設竒正之兵，先為歸路之伏，故雖千里之外，可殺敵國之將。此巧能成事，非法之善而何？若與敵遇，微與之期，如處女之弱，彼必驕怠而露其隙。我則乗隙用竒，勢如脫兎，敵不及拒。此巧能取勝，亦法之善也。然戰勝攻取，雖
translation_en:
…the transformations of orthodox deployment. In all methods of employing troops, there are advantages to be gained from the nine adaptations. If a commander can comprehend these, he understands how to employ troops. If, however, he has the five dangerous traits, are the resulting military disasters not the commanding general’s fault? Accessible, entangling, indecisive, narrow, precipitous, and distant: these six are the conditions of terrain. If a commander can examine them, they will aid his employment of troops. Flight, laxity, entrapment, collapse, disorder, and rout: these six are not calamities caused by Heaven and Earth, but faults of the commanding general. Ah! The methods of warfare inherently entail neither success nor failure; success and failure lie in how the commander puts them into practice.

To employ the multitude of the three armies as though directing a single person, cast them into a position where they have nowhere to go, so that all three armies fight to the death with one mind to gain victory. This is command without administrative measures, and is also an excellence of military method. If the enemy comes to attack us, we should follow and scrutinize his intentions [?], display weakness, and offer no resistance. He will surely concentrate his forces on a single objective and have no other plan. We then deploy unorthodox and orthodox forces, first setting an ambush on his route of return. Thus, even a thousand li away, we can kill the enemy state’s general. This is accomplishing the task through skill: what could it be but an excellence of military method? If we encounter the enemy, secretly setting a time to engage him [?], and appear as weak as a maiden, he will surely become arrogant and negligent and expose an opening. We then exploit that opening with unorthodox tactics, moving with the force of an escaping hare, so that the enemy has no time to resist. This is winning victory through skill, and is also an excellence of military method. Yet, in winning battles and taking objectives by assault, even though…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
用水火而必勝必取者乃人之功苟不脩
其功行其賞此致凶之道命曰費留非將
之罪而何吁兵法本無優劣而將之所用
則有優劣也曰火人火積火輺火庫火隊
此火攻有五非火人爲先乎曰因間内間
反間死間生間此用間有五非反間爲最
乎夫兵貴拙速不尚巧遲此用兵之大要
也今之欲用兵者豈可不以此通其變而
===
適其宜耶且廣之瀧水猺蠻其種類之生
非一時爲地方之患非一日邇者渠魁雖
殲餘孽尚多兹欲拙速也必將大振軍旅
長驅直擣一舉而滅之可也但恐山險路
﨑兵不得進馬不得馳遇敵無交戰之塲
退守無立營之地挑之不出攻之無間雖
竒謀深策亦無所施徒頓兵挫銳而已欲
巧遲也必將設竒示弱誘其出而擊之乗
punctuated:
用水火，而必勝必取者，乃人之功。苟不脩其功，行其賞，此致凶之道，命曰費留，非將之罪而何？吁！兵法本無優劣，而將之所用則有優劣也。曰火人、火積、火輺、火庫、火隊，此火攻有五，非火人爲先乎？曰因間、内間、反間、死間、生間，此用間有五，非反間爲最乎？夫兵貴拙速，不尚巧遲，此用兵之大要也。今之欲用兵者，豈可不以此通其變而適其宜耶？

且廣之瀧水猺蠻，其種類之生非一時，爲地方之患非一日。邇者渠魁雖殲，餘孽尚多。兹欲拙速也，必將大振軍旅，長驅直擣，一舉而滅之可也。但恐山險路﨑，兵不得進，馬不得馳，遇敵無交戰之塲，退守無立營之地，挑之不出，攻之無間，雖竒謀深策亦無所施，徒頓兵挫銳而已。欲巧遲也，必將設竒示弱，誘其出而擊之，乗
translation_en:
…use water and fire, yet assured victory and capture are achievements of men. If their achievements are not duly recognized and rewards bestowed, this is the road to disaster, termed “wasteful lingering.” Whose fault could it be but the general’s? Ah! The methods of warfare are not inherently superior or inferior; it is the general’s application of them that is superior or inferior. Burning personnel, burning stores, burning baggage wagons, burning arsenals, and burning supply columns: these are the five kinds of attack by fire. Is burning personnel not foremost? Local spies, inside spies, turned spies, doomed spies, and surviving spies: these are the five kinds of espionage. Are turned spies not the most important? In warfare, clumsy speed is prized, rather than clever delay. This is the essential principle of employing troops. How could those who wish to employ troops today fail to use this principle to respond to changing circumstances and act appropriately?

Moreover, the Yao people whom the text calls “barbarians” in Longshui, Guangdong, have been established there for more than a short time, and have troubled the locality for more than a single day. Recently, although their ringleaders have been annihilated, many remaining rebels survive. If we now seek clumsy speed, we must mobilize our forces in strength, drive straight ahead, and destroy them at a single stroke. Yet the fear is that the mountains are precipitous and the roads rugged: troops cannot advance, horses cannot gallop, there is no ground on which to engage the enemy when encountered, and no place to establish a camp when falling back to defend. Provocation will not draw them out, and there is no opening for an attack. Even ingenious schemes and profound plans would have no scope for application; we would merely exhaust our troops and blunt their fighting spirit. If we seek clever delay, we must devise stratagems and display weakness, lure them out and strike them, taking advantage of…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其虛而襲之可也但恐夷性狡譎熟知險
阻我雖匿兵設伏以伺彼則憑高瞭望先
知我東則彼西我南則彼北雖籌筭無遺
亦無所用徒屈力殫貨而已夫夷情之向
背由夷勢之盛衰也勢盛則肆惡而爲患
勢衰則畏威而向化一向一背自古爲然
爲今之計莫若選將益兵據其要險之處
斷其出入之途嚴號令明賞罰固守而勿
===
怠備禦而勿弛來則併力以奮擊去則堅
守而勿追如此者久則必困困則其勢自
衰衰則必畏威而自服矣或曰舉其眾而
可以盡滅之取其地而可以賦稅之遷吾
民而可以編戶之此貪功好利之說非爲
國保民之計亦非兵家萬全之良策也況
非今日之所宜乎敢以是爲終篇獻
punctuated: 其虛而襲之可也。但恐夷性狡譎，熟知險阻，我雖匿兵設伏以伺，彼則憑高瞭望先知。我東則彼西，我南則彼北，雖籌筭無遺，亦無所用，徒屈力殫貨而已。夫夷情之向背，由夷勢之盛衰也。勢盛則肆惡而爲患，勢衰則畏威而向化，一向一背，自古爲然。爲今之計，莫若選將益兵，據其要險之處，斷其出入之途，嚴號令，明賞罰，固守而勿怠，備禦而勿弛。來則併力以奮擊，去則堅守而勿追。如此者久，則必困；困則其勢自衰，衰則必畏威而自服矣。或曰：「舉其眾而可以盡滅之，取其地而可以賦稅之，遷吾民而可以編戶之。」此貪功好利之說，非爲國保民之計，亦非兵家萬全之良策也，況非今日之所宜乎？敢以是爲終篇獻。
translation_en:
…attack them when they are vulnerable: this would be feasible. Yet I fear that the Yi are cunning and deceitful, thoroughly familiar with the difficult terrain. Although we might conceal troops and lay ambushes to await them, they would watch from high ground and discover us beforehand. If we go east, they go west; if we go south, they go north. Even calculations that overlook nothing would be of no use: we would merely exhaust our strength and resources.

Whether the Yi submit or rebel depends on whether their power is strong or weak. When strong, they give free rein to wrongdoing and cause trouble; when weak, they fear our might and turn toward our civilizing influence. Such alternation between allegiance and rebellion has been so since antiquity. For the present, the best plan is to select commanders and reinforce the troops, occupy strategically important and defensible positions, and cut off their routes of entry and exit. Orders must be strict, rewards and punishments clearly established; we must hold our positions without negligence and maintain our defenses without slackening. When they come, we should combine our forces and strike vigorously; when they withdraw, we should hold firm and not pursue. If this continues long enough, they will inevitably be hard pressed. Once hard pressed, their power will naturally decline; once it declines, they will surely fear our might and submit of their own accord.

Some say: “We could wipe out their entire population, seize their land and levy taxes on it, and move our own people there and register them as households.” This is the talk of those greedy for merit and profit, not a plan to serve the state and protect the people, nor a sound military strategy ensuring complete success. How much less is it appropriate to present circumstances! I venture to offer this as my concluding submission.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
國家三載一試士周制也乃成
化丙午秋廣東藩服大萃十
郡之士圍棘而三試之遵
成憲也于時監察御史徐同愛以
爲重典不可易易規畫之周
防範之密視往歲有加凡內
===
外百執事咸出慎選罔不殫
乃力畢乃智惟公惟勤冀是
科之得人皆真才也撤棘之
日得其才之通經術博古訓
者七十五人故事有錄而焯
當序其後竊惟天生賢才所
以爲世用也用之則天經以
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

國家三載一試士，周制也。乃成化丙午秋，廣東藩服大萃十郡之士，圍棘而三試之，遵成憲也。于時，監察御史徐同愛以爲重典不可易易，規畫之周，防範之密，視往歲有加。凡內外百執事，咸出慎選，罔不殫乃力、畢乃智，惟公惟勤，冀是科之得人皆真才也。撤棘之日，得其才之通經術、博古訓者七十五人。故事有錄，而焯當序其後。竊惟天生賢才，所以爲世用也。用之，則天經以
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

The state examines scholars once every three years, following the system of the Zhou dynasty. In the autumn of the bingwu year of Chenghua [1486], Guangdong, a provincial domain, assembled scholars from its ten prefectures within the thorn enclosure and examined them in three sessions, in accordance with established regulations. At that time, Investigating Censor Xu Tong’ai considered this important institution something that must not be treated lightly. The thoroughness of the planning and the strictness of the safeguards surpassed those of previous years. All personnel serving inside and outside the examination compound were carefully selected. Every one exhausted his strength and applied his wisdom to the fullest, acting with impartiality and diligence, in the hope that all those selected in this examination would possess genuine talent.

When the thorn enclosure was dismantled, seventy-five men had been selected whose talents encompassed mastery of classical learning and broad knowledge of ancient teachings. Established practice calls for a record, and it falls to me, Chuo, to write its postface. I humbly reflect that Heaven brings forth worthy and talented men so that they may serve the world. When they are employed, Heaven’s enduring norms, through them …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之而扶人紀以之而立社稷
黎元以之而安養無所往而
非用賢之效矣賢之關乎世
計其大矣哉顧惟今日所以
取之之道何如夫文乃賢士
之一藝耳彼其平居所涵蓄
所進脩不止於是而今之高
===
下去取一於文而決者盖文
乃言之精而成章發乎心而
貫乎道者也賢而心醇乎道
文之發也純而正暢而不詭
原於性而根於理否則詖淫
邪遁梏於聞見而性理其背
馳矣觀其文之醇駁而人之
punctuated: 之而扶，人紀以之而立，社稷黎元以之而安養，無所往而非用賢之效矣。賢之關乎世界，其大矣哉！顧惟今日所以取之之道何如？夫文乃賢士之一藝耳，彼其平居所涵蓄、所進脩，不止於是。而今之高下去取，一於文而決者，盖文乃言之精而成章，發乎心而貫乎道者也。賢而心醇乎道，文之發也純而正，暢而不詭，原於性而根於理；否則詖淫邪遁，梏於聞見，而性理其背馳矣。觀其文之醇駁，而人之
translation_en: …through them the constant principles of Heaven are upheld, the bonds of human society established, and the altars of state secured and the common people nurtured. Wherever one turns, these are the effects of employing the worthy. How great is the importance of worthy men to the ordering of the world! Yet consider the means by which they are selected today: what are these like? Literary composition is but one accomplishment of a worthy scholar. What he cultivates within himself and advances in through daily study extends beyond this alone. Yet today, ranking candidates and deciding whom to reject or accept depend entirely upon their writing. This is because writing is the refined essence of speech, formed into coherent composition, issuing from the heart and permeated by the Way. When a man is worthy and his heart accords purely with the Way, the writing that issues from him is pure and correct, fluent without being deceptive, originating in human nature and rooted in principle. Otherwise, it is biased, extravagant, perverse, and evasive, confined by what one has heard and seen, and runs counter to human nature and principle. By observing the purity or impurity of a man's writing, his…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
高下瞭然可見
朝廷取士之科决於文者職此
故也嗚呼士之登名兹錄者
以其賢而文之醇也由是而
進嚮用有日其可自負於賢
之名哉必於天經思所以扶
之於人紀思所以立之於社
===
稷黎元思所以安固而康寧
之隨所任而始終不異其趣
以弼我
皇明億萬載無疆之盛治使用賢
之效大著於斯世可矣苟徒
竊賢名以自欺冒賢行以文
奸豈但自戕而已而於
punctuated: 高下瞭然可見。朝廷取士之科决於文者，職此故也。嗚呼！士之登名兹錄者，以其賢而文之醇也。由是而進，嚮用有日，其可自負於賢之名哉？必於天經思所以扶之，於人紀思所以立之，於社稷黎元思所以安固而康寧之，隨所任而始終不異其趣，以弼我皇明億萬載無疆之盛治，使用賢之效大著於斯世，可矣。苟徒竊賢名以自欺，冒賢行以文奸，豈但自戕而已，而於
translation_en: …their relative worth can clearly be seen. This is precisely why the court’s examinations for selecting scholars are decided on the basis of their writing. Ah! Those scholars whose names appear in this record have earned their place through their worthiness and the purity of their writing. Advancing from here, they will in time be entrusted with office. How could they rest content with their reputation for worthiness? They must consider how to uphold Heaven’s enduring principles, how to establish the bonds of human relationships, and how to secure the altars of soil and grain and bring peace and well-being to the common people. Whatever their appointments, they must remain constant in their purpose from beginning to end, thereby assisting our august Ming dynasty in its flourishing rule, boundless for countless ages. If they thus make the benefits of employing worthy men abundantly manifest in this age, that will suffice. But if they merely steal a reputation for worthiness to deceive themselves and assume the guise of worthy conduct to cloak their wickedness, would they merely be ruining themselves? And with regard to…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖天子設科求賢之意負之亦殆
甚歟
湖廣岳州府華容縣儒學教
諭鄭焯謹序
punctuated:
聖天子設科求賢之意，負之亦殆甚歟！
湖廣岳州府華容縣儒學教諭鄭焯謹序。
translation_en:
…the sage Son of Heaven’s intention in establishing examinations to seek worthy men—would not betraying it be grave indeed!
Zheng Chao, Instructor at the Confucian School of Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, respectfully composed this preface.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試小錄序
聖天子君臨
大寶于兹二十有二載天下以鄉
舉選士凡七科矣成化丙午
復當大比之期廣東藩臬重
臣恪遵
成憲預期禮聘儒紳以司文衡
===
瑭等濫竽而至于時都察院
右都御史宋旻受
命宣撫作興士類太監劉倜韋眷
總兵安遠侯柳景皆飭武備
衛文教而敦崇儒雅巡按監
察御史徐同愛以登庸髦俊
國家首事凡百規畫靡不究心
punctuated:
廣東鄉試小錄序

聖天子君臨大寶，于兹二十有二載，天下以鄉舉選士凡七科矣。成化丙午，復當大比之期，廣東藩臬重臣恪遵成憲，預期禮聘儒紳，以司文衡。瑭等濫竽而至。于時，都察院右都御史宋旻受命宣撫，作興士類；太監劉倜、韋眷、總兵安遠侯柳景，皆飭武備，衛文教，而敦崇儒雅。巡按監察御史徐同愛以登庸髦俊，國家首事，凡百規畫，靡不究心。
translation_en:
Preface to the Brief Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

The sagely Son of Heaven has occupied the imperial throne for twenty-two years. Throughout the realm, men have now been selected through provincial examinations on seven occasions. In the bingwu year of Chenghua [1486], the time for the triennial examination came around once more. The senior officials of Guangdong’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions scrupulously followed established regulations and, ahead of the appointed time, courteously invited learned gentlemen to serve as judges of literary merit. We, Tang 瑭 and the others, arrived to fill these posts, unworthily counted among the qualified.

At this time, Song Min 宋旻, Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, had received an imperial commission to bring peace and reassurance and to encourage the scholars. The Grand Eunuchs Liu Ti 劉倜 and Wei Juan 韋眷, together with the Regional Commander Liu Jing 柳景, Marquis of Anyuan, all put military preparations in order, safeguarded civil education, and accorded high honor to Confucian learning and refinement. Xu Tong’ai 徐同愛, the Regional Inspecting Censor, regarded the advancement and appointment of outstanding talent as the foremost business of the state; in every aspect of planning, he devoted the utmost care.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乃合諸郡邑士之可舉者重
加精選得預試者千四百有
竒鎖院而三試之内而提調
監試則右叅政周瑛左叅議
姜英僉事翁晏周啓外而綜
理彌範則右布政使熊懷按
察使馮俊陶魯左叅政李芳
===
謝瑀副使俞俊李瑢僉事張
榖彭頎陳英李元鎮若後先匡
賛則提學僉事張習躬親任
之與凡執事者皆懋簡以充
而御史徐同愛實監臨焉比撤
棘得中式者七十有五人遵
定額也爰第其姓名及文之純
punctuated: 乃合諸郡邑士之可舉者，重加精選，得預試者千四百有竒。鎖院而三試之。内而提調監試，則右叅政周瑛、左叅議姜英、僉事翁晏、周啓；外而綜理彌範，則右布政使熊懷、按察使馮俊、陶魯、左叅政李芳、謝瑀、副使俞俊、李瑢、僉事張榖、彭頎、陳英、李元鎮。若後先匡賛，則提學僉事張習躬親任之。與凡執事者，皆懋簡以充，而御史徐同愛實監臨焉。比撤棘，得中式者七十有五人，遵定額也。爰第其姓名及文之純
translation_en:
They then assembled the eligible scholars from the various prefectures and counties and subjected them to further careful selection. More than fourteen hundred qualified to take the examination. The examination compound was sealed, and they were examined in three sessions. Within the compound, proctoring and examination oversight were handled by Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhou Ying, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Jiang Ying, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Weng Yan and Zhou Qi. Outside, overall management and coordination [?] were handled by Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Xiong Huai; Surveillance Commissioners Feng Jun and Tao Lu; Left Administration Vice Commissioners Li Fang and Xie Yu; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yu Jun and Li Rong; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Zhang Gu, Peng Qi, Chen Ying, and Li Yuanzhen. Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Zhang Xi, serving as Education Intendant, personally undertook the work of assistance and support throughout. These men, together with all the functionaries, were carefully selected to fill their posts, while Censor Xu Tong’ai served as Supervising Official.

When the thorn barriers were removed, seventy-five candidates had passed, in accordance with the prescribed quota. Their names were then arranged in order, together with those of their compositions that were pure …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
粹者具錄以
進謂瑭宜序諸首竊惟
國家求賢雖非一途恒以科目
爲重賢才入官之階雖非一
致率以科目爲榮我
太祖高皇帝受
天景命奄有萬方惓惓欲以人文
===
化成天下
詔有司三年一開科取士重之以
選舉榮之以賓興期得賢才
以爲化理之本
列聖相承率由舊典
皇上繼承大統克篤前烈而於興
賢之典益加慎重惟欲上當
punctuated: 粹者，具錄以進，謂瑭宜序諸首。竊惟國家求賢，雖非一途，恒以科目爲重；賢才入官之階，雖非一致，率以科目爲榮。我太祖高皇帝受天景命，奄有萬方，惓惓欲以人文化成天下，詔有司三年一開科取士，重之以選舉，榮之以賓興，期得賢才以爲化理之本。列聖相承，率由舊典。皇上繼承大統，克篤前烈，而於興賢之典益加慎重，惟欲上當
translation_en:
…those of purest excellence were fully recorded for submission to the throne, and I, Tang, was told that I should place a preface at the beginning. I humbly reflect that, although the state seeks worthy men through more than one avenue, it has always attached particular importance to the examinations. Although talented and worthy men enter official service by different routes, they generally regard advancement through the examinations as an honor.

Our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s great mandate and possessed all the realm. Earnestly desiring to transform the world through cultural cultivation, he commanded the responsible authorities to hold examinations every three years to select men for service. He accorded them distinction through selection for office and honored them through the ceremonial reception and recommendation of worthy men, hoping to obtain worthy talent as the foundation of moral transformation and good government. Successive sage emperors followed one another, all adhering to these established institutions. His Majesty has succeeded to the imperial sovereignty and faithfully carried forward the achievements of his predecessors, exercising still greater care in the institutions for advancing worthy men, desiring only, above, to accord with…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天心下安黎元爲
宗社億萬年靈長之計也猗歟盛
哉廣東嶺南大藩海嶽靈淑
之氣鍾爲俊英百餘年來士
由科目以進昭崇勳揚休烈
卓然爲世名臣者不可稱數
先正有云豪傑之士繇科目
===
而進斯言信矣夫
國家以科目取士以賢才之士
待之也士君子荷
國家之造出而致用求無愧於
科名盍以賢才之士自待乎
爾多士登名薦書行將試禮
闈奉
punctuated:
天心，下安黎元，爲宗社億萬年靈長之計也。猗歟，盛哉！廣東，嶺南大藩，海嶽靈淑之氣鍾爲俊英。百餘年來，士由科目以進，昭崇勳，揚休烈，卓然爲世名臣者，不可稱數。先正有云：「豪傑之士繇科目而進。」斯言信矣！
夫國家以科目取士，以賢才之士待之也。士君子荷國家之造，出而致用，求無愧於科名，盍以賢才之士自待乎？爾多士登名薦書，行將試禮闈，奉
translation_en:
…accord with Heaven’s will above and bring peace to the common people below, thereby securing the enduring prosperity of the ancestral temples and altars of state for countless ages. Ah, how magnificent! Guangdong is a great province south of the mountain ranges, where the potent and auspicious influences of sea and mountains gather to produce outstanding men. Over the past hundred years and more, innumerable scholars have advanced through the examinations, displayed great merit, and made their splendid achievements renowned, distinguishing themselves as celebrated ministers of their age. A worthy predecessor once said, “Men of exceptional ability advance through the examinations.” These words are indeed true!
The state selects scholars through the examinations and treats them as men of virtue and ability. Having benefited from the state’s nurturing, gentlemen come forth to put their abilities to use and seek to prove worthy of their examination distinction. Should they not hold themselves to the standard of men of virtue and ability? You assembled scholars, whose names have been entered on the roll of recommendation, will soon sit the examination in the Ministry of Rites examination compound and respectfully…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廷對而荐陟華要其所以自待
者必賢足以正君而善俗才
足以脩政而立事宏文碩學
足以賛
謀謨而黼黻乎治道爲
上爲德爲下爲民躋斯世於唐虞
三代之盛庶無愧賢才之稱
===
而亦無負
朝廷期待之德意矣其或靜言
而庸違枉已以徇人計而利
禄謀而身家賢才之實漠乎
其無聞則科目之榮且重者
適足以取辱而致輕非士君
子之所自待也非
punctuated: 廷對，而荐陟華要。其所以自待者，必賢足以正君而善俗，才足以脩政而立事，宏文碩學足以賛謀謨而黼黻乎治道，爲上爲德，爲下爲民，躋斯世於唐虞三代之盛，庶無愧賢才之稱，而亦無負朝廷期待之德意矣。其或靜言而庸違，枉已以徇人，計而利禄，謀而身家，賢才之實漠乎其無聞，則科目之榮且重者，適足以取辱而致輕，非士君子之所自待也，非
translation_en:
…respond at court and rise successively to distinguished and important offices. The standards you set for yourselves must be such that your virtue suffices to rectify the ruler and improve customs, your ability suffices to put government in order and accomplish affairs, and your expansive literary accomplishment and profound learning suffice to assist in deliberations and lend lustre to the way of governance. For those above, work for virtue; for those below, work for the people [?]. Raise this age to the flourishing condition of the reigns of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties. Only then may you be worthy of the designation “men of virtue and talent” and not disappoint the benevolent intentions with which the court places its hopes in you.

If, however, you speak fine words but act contrary to them, compromise yourselves to accommodate others, scheme for profit and official emoluments, and plan for yourselves and your families [?], while nothing is heard of any actual virtue or talent, then the honour and distinction conferred by examination success will serve only to bring disgrace and contempt upon you. This is not the standard that gentlemen should set for themselves, nor is it…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
朝廷設科取士之初意也亦非
瑭等今日之所頥望也庸序
諸卷首以爲多士勗
河南開封府許州儒學學正
朱瑭謹序
punctuated:
朝廷設科取士之初意也，亦非瑭等今日之所頥望也。庸序諸卷首，以爲多士勗。
河南開封府許州儒學學正朱瑭謹序。
translation_en:
…the court’s original intention in establishing examinations to recruit officials, nor is it what I, Tang, and my colleagues now earnestly hope for [?]. I therefore set this preface at the beginning of the volume to encourage the assembled scholars.
Respectfully prefaced by Zhu Tang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
主忠信徙義崇德也
中也者天下之大本也和也者天下之達
道也致中和天地位焉萬物育焉
夫義路也禮門也惟君子能由是路出入
是門也
易
===
應乎天而時行
進得位往有功也進以正可以正邦也其
位剛得中也止而巽動不窮也
以言乎遠則不禦以言乎邇則靜而正
有事而後可大故受之以臨臨者大也物
大然後可觀故受之以觀可觀而後
有所合故受之以噬嗑嗑者合也物
不可以苟合而已故受之以賁
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

主忠信，徙義，崇德也。

中也者，天下之大本也；和也者，天下之達道也。致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉。

夫義，路也；禮，門也。惟君子能由是路，出入是門也。

易

應乎天而時行。

進得位，往有功也。進以正，可以正邦也。其位，剛得中也。止而巽，動不窮也。

以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正。

有事而後可大，故受之以臨。臨者，大也。物大然後可觀，故受之以觀。可觀而後有所合，故受之以噬嗑。嗑者，合也。物不可以苟合而已，故受之以賁。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

To make loyalty and trustworthiness one's guiding principles and to move toward righteousness is to exalt virtue.

Equilibrium is the great foundation of all under Heaven; harmony is the universally followed Way of all under Heaven. When equilibrium and harmony are fully realized, Heaven and Earth take their proper places, and the myriad things flourish.

Righteousness is the road; ritual propriety is the gate. Only the gentleman can follow this road and pass in and out through this gate.

Book of Changes

Responding to Heaven and acting when the time is right.

Advancing and obtaining a position, one achieves success in going forward. Advancing with correctness, one can set the state right. In its position, the firm occupies the center. Keeping still and being yielding, one acts without exhaustion.

Speaking of what is distant, it meets no resistance; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct.

Only after there are undertakings can there be greatness; therefore it is followed by Lin (Approach). Lin means greatness. Only when things are great can they be viewed; therefore it is followed by Guan (Contemplation). Only after things can be viewed can there be a joining together; therefore it is followed by Shihe (Biting Through). He means joining together. Things cannot merely join together in a haphazard fashion; therefore it is followed by Bi (Adornment).

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書
日宣三德夙夜浚明有家日嚴祗敬六德
亮采有邦翕受敷施九德咸事俊乂
在官百僚師師百工惟時撫于五辰
庶績其凝
若虞機張往省括于度則釋
予惟徃求朕攸濟敷賁敷前人受命
乃命重黎絶地天通罔有降格羣后之逮
===
在下明明棐常鰥寡無盖皇帝清問
下民鰥寡有辭于苗德威惟畏德明
惟明乃命三后恤功于民伯夷降典
折民惟刑禹平水土主名山川稷降
播種農殖嘉穀三后成功惟殷于民
士制百姓于刑之中以教祗德
詩
天保定爾以莫不興如山如阜如岡如陵
punctuated:
書
日宣三德，夙夜浚明有家；日嚴祗敬六德，亮采有邦。翕受敷施，九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師，百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績其凝。
若虞機張，往省括于度，則釋。
予惟徃求朕攸濟，敷賁敷前人受命。
乃命重黎，絶地天通，罔有降格。羣后之逮在下，明明棐常，鰥寡無盖。皇帝清問下民，鰥寡有辭于苗。德威惟畏，德明惟明。乃命三后，恤功于民。伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以教祗德。
詩
天保定爾，以莫不興。如山如阜，如岡如陵。
translation_en:
Book of Documents

Those who daily manifest three virtues, profoundly understanding and practicing them morning and night, may govern a noble house; those who daily attend reverently and respectfully to six virtues, faithfully conducting affairs, may govern a state. When such men are welcomed together and employed widely, all nine virtues enter into service, and men of outstanding ability hold office. The hundred officials learn from one another, and all officers perform their duties at the proper times. In harmony with the five seasonal cycles, their many achievements become firmly established.

As a huntsman, with his crossbow cocked, first checks that the arrow is properly aligned with his aim and then releases it.

I shall seek what will aid me in accomplishing my task, and gloriously adorn my predecessors’ reception of the Mandate [the repeated 敷 is doubtful].

He then commanded Chong and Li to sever communication between earth and heaven, so that there would be no descending and coming down. The various lords serving below clearly upheld the constant norms, and the plight of widowers and widows was not concealed. The august emperor carefully questioned the common people below, and widowers and widows brought accusations against the Miao. The authority of virtue alone was to be feared; the illumination of virtue alone was to enlighten. He then commanded three lords to labor solicitously for the people. Bo Yi promulgated the statutes, bringing the people into order through laws. Yu regulated the waters and the land, taking charge of the renowned mountains and rivers. Ji taught sowing and planting, cultivating fine grain. The three lords completed their work, richly benefiting the people. The Director of Justice regulated the people through punishments that struck the proper mean, teaching them to revere virtue.

Book of Odes

Heaven protects and establishes you, causing all things to flourish. Like mountains and hills, like ridges and high mounds…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
如川之方至以莫不增
鎬京辟廱自西自東自南自北無思不服
皇王烝哉考卜維王宅是鎬京維龜
正之武王成之武王烝哉豐水有芑
武王豈不仕詒厥孫謀以燕翼子武
王烝哉
即有邰家室誕降嘉種維秬維秠維穈維
芑恒之秬秠是穫是畝恒之穈芑是
===
任是負以歸肇祀誕我祀如何或舂
或揄或簸或蹂釋之叟叟烝之浮浮
載謀載惟取蕭祭脂取羝以軷載燔
載烈以興嗣歲卬盛于豆于豆于登
其香始升上帝居歆胡臭亶時后稷
肇祀庶無罪悔以迄于今
我將我享維羊維牛維天其右之
春秋
punctuated:
如川之方至，以莫不增。
鎬京辟廱，自西自東，自南自北，無思不服。皇王烝哉！考卜維王，宅是鎬京。維龜正之，武王成之。武王烝哉！豐水有芑，武王豈不仕？詒厥孫謀，以燕翼子。武王烝哉！
即有邰家室，誕降嘉種，維秬維秠，維穈維芑。恒之秬秠，是穫是畝；恒之穈芑，是任是負，以歸肇祀。誕我祀如何？或舂或揄，或簸或蹂。釋之叟叟，烝之浮浮。載謀載惟，取蕭祭脂，取羝以軷。載燔載烈，以興嗣歲。卬盛于豆，于豆于登。其香始升，上帝居歆。胡臭亶時！后稷肇祀，庶無罪悔，以迄于今。
我將我享，維羊維牛，維天其右之。
春秋
translation_en:
…Like a river newly swelling, may there be nothing that does not increase.

At the Biyong ceremonial school in Haojing, from west and east, from south and north, none failed to submit. How great the august king! It was the king who examined the divination and settled here in Haojing. The tortoise determined the site; King Wu brought the work to completion. How great King Wu! White millet grows beside the Feng River. Did King Wu not attend to his duties? He bequeathed plans to his descendants, to bring peace to and protect his children. How great King Wu!

He settled in Tai and established his household. Then he bestowed fine seeds: black millet, double-grained black millet, red millet, and white millet. He planted black millet and double-grained millet throughout; these were harvested and gathered in the fields [?]. He planted red and white millet throughout; these were carried in arms and borne on backs, brought home to begin the sacrifices. And how were our sacrifices performed? Some pounded the grain, some scooped it out; some winnowed it, some rubbed off the husks. They washed it with a rustling sound and steamed it until the vapour rose. They consulted and considered; they took southernwood to offer with fat, and took a ram for the sacrifice to the road spirit. They roasted and broiled, to usher in the coming year. We filled the offering vessels, the wooden dou and the earthen deng. As the fragrance began to rise, the Lord on High accepted it with pleasure. How truly fitting was the fragrance! Hou Ji began these sacrifices; may we remain free of fault and cause for regret, down to the present day.

We bring forward our offerings: sheep and oxen. May Heaven favour them.

Spring and Autumn Annals

They jointly concluded a covenant at Keling. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Cheng〕 The duke met with the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin…

The highest-ranking minister of a medium-sized state holds a position equivalent to that of a middle-ranking minister of a large state; its middle-ranking minister corresponds to the latter’s lowest-ranking minister, and its lowest-ranking minister to the latter’s senior grand officer. title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夫其有中士下士者數各居其上之
三分
德盛而教尊五穀時熟然後賞之以樂
三代之王也必先其令聞
率法而强之資仁者也
第貳塲
論
帝王之治一本於道
===

擬漢高帝定元功十八人位次詔〔漢高帝六年〕

上言大臣德政
入戶以籍爲定
punctuated:

率法而强之，資仁者也。
第貳塲
論
帝王之治，一本於道。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢高帝定元功十八人位次詔〔漢高帝六年〕。

判語五條
上言大臣德政。
入戶以籍爲定。
translation_en:
…grand masters. Where there are middle-ranking and lower-ranking servicemen, the number in each rank is one-third that of the rank immediately above it.
When their virtue is abundant, their teaching honored, and the five grains ripen in season, only then are they rewarded with music.
Those who became kings of the Three Dynasties invariably first established a good reputation.
Those who follow the rules and exert themselves draw upon benevolence.
Second Session
Discourse
The government of emperors and kings is rooted entirely in the Way.
Edicts, Pronouncements, and Memorials 〔One question from these categories [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of Emperor Gao of Han establishing the order of precedence of the eighteen foremost meritorious officials. 〔Sixth year of Emperor Gao of Han〕
Compose a Tang pronouncement appointing Zhang Jiuling Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Participant in Determining Governmental Matters. 〔Twenty-first year of Kaiyuan〕
Compose a Song memorial of thanks for Tang Jie’s appointment as Participant in Determining Governmental Matters. 〔First year of Xining〕
Five Legal Judgments
Submitting a report to the throne praising a high minister’s virtue and governance.
Determining household membership on the basis of the registers.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禁止師巫邪術
縱放軍人歇役
詐欺官私取財
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問有善無惡天之命也自古帝王之興體
天致治其勸善懲惡莫不有典法以
詔諭臣民篤尚倫理弼成治化之隆
===
姑舉一二言之若成湯之誕告萬方
成王之訓迪百官其所懲勸攷之於
經槩可見矣洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝大誥三編
太宗文皇帝為善陰隲孝順事實
宣宗章皇帝五倫一書嘉惠臣民至精至悉盖
與商周之君異世而同心也
punctuated:
禁止師巫邪術。
縱放軍人歇役。
詐欺官私取財。

第叁場
策〔五道〕

問：有善無惡，天之命也。自古帝王之興，體天致治，其勸善懲惡，莫不有典法，以詔諭臣民，篤尚倫理，弼成治化之隆。姑舉一二言之：若成湯之誕告萬方，成王之訓迪百官，其所懲勸，攷之於經，槩可見矣。洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》，宣宗章皇帝《五倫》一書，嘉惠臣民，至精至悉，盖與商周之君異世而同心也。
translation_en:
Prohibiting the heterodox arts of spirit mediums.
Allowing soldiers to cease performing their duties.
Fraudulently obtaining public or private property.

Third Session
Policy Questions〔Five questions〕

Question: That there is goodness and no evil is Heaven’s endowment. From antiquity, when emperors and kings arose, they modeled themselves on Heaven to establish good government. In encouraging good and punishing evil, all had established statutes and rules through which they instructed their officials and people, earnestly upheld ethical relationships, and helped bring government and moral transformation to flourishing fulfillment. Let us cite one or two examples: Cheng Tang’s proclamation to the myriad regions and King Cheng’s instruction and guidance of the hundred officials. What they punished and encouraged can be seen in broad outline by examining the Classics. We reverently consider our dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao’s Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), in three compilations; Emperor Taizong Wen’s Doing Good and Hidden Virtue (Wei Shan Yin Zhi) and True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi); and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang’s book, The Five Human Relationships (Wulun). These bestowed beneficent instruction upon officials and people with the utmost refinement and thoroughness. Though they lived in different ages from the rulers of Shang and Zhou, they shared the same purpose.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
三聖之書其間懲勸之條凡幾見而其旨之同
於湯之誕告成王之訓迪果安在哉
方今
聖天子在上治教休明普天率土相安於皞皞
之天善有勸而惡有懲述其所自皆
聖學緝熈率由舊典之明驗也斯世斯民何其
幸歟諸士子博古通今願詳著于篇
以觀膺
===
聖訓之功
問諸史浩瀚固難以一二議也今姑舉司
馬遷班固二家言之或謂固優於遷
或謂遷優於固然不能無可疑者嘗
即其書觀之遷曰天官固曰天文遷
曰河渠固曰溝洫遷之封禪而固以
郊祀易之遷之食貨而固以平準更
之遷爲十表八書固志五行地里而
punctuated:
三聖之書，其間懲勸之條凡幾見，而其旨之同於湯之誕告、成王之訓迪，果安在哉？方今聖天子在上，治教休明，普天率土，相安於皞皞之天。善有勸而惡有懲，述其所自，皆聖學緝熈、率由舊典之明驗也。斯世斯民何其幸歟！諸士子博古通今，願詳著于篇，以觀膺聖訓之功。

問：諸史浩瀚，固難以一二議也。今姑舉司馬遷、班固二家言之。或謂固優於遷，或謂遷優於固，然不能無可疑者。嘗即其書觀之，遷曰天官，固曰天文；遷曰河渠，固曰溝洫；遷之封禪，而固以郊祀易之；遷之食貨，而固以平準更之；遷爲十表八書，固志五行地里，而
translation_en:
In the books of these three sage emperors, how many provisions for admonition and encouragement are to be found? Where precisely do their purport and that of Tang’s proclamation to the myriad regions and King Cheng’s instruction of the officials coincide? Now the sage Son of Heaven reigns above, and governance and moral instruction are splendid and enlightened. Throughout the realm, all live together in peace beneath a heaven of harmonious contentment. Goodness is encouraged and evil punished. Tracing the source of these achievements, all are clear evidence of his ever-brightening sagely learning and his adherence to established precedents. How fortunate are this age and its people! You candidates are widely versed in antiquity and conversant with the present. We ask you to set these matters forth in detail in your essays, so that we may see the fruits of your receiving the imperial teachings.

Question: The histories are vast; it is certainly difficult to discuss them in just a few remarks. For now, let us consider the two historians Sima Qian and Ban Gu. Some say that Gu surpasses Qian; others say that Qian surpasses Gu. Yet these judgments cannot be free of points open to doubt. Looking at their books, Qian calls one treatise “Celestial Offices,” while Gu calls his “Astronomy”; Qian calls another “Rivers and Canals,” while Gu calls his “Ditches and Watercourses.” For Qian’s “Feng and Shan Sacrifices,” Gu substitutes “Suburban Sacrifices”; for Qian’s “Food and Money,” Gu substitutes “The Equalization of Prices” [?—the titles attributed to the two historians here are reversed]. Qian composed ten tables and eight treatises, while Gu wrote monographs on the Five Phases and geography, and…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其書之同異若此豈無優劣之可議
歟遷序三千年事僅五十萬言固叙
二百年事已餘八十萬言遷傳循吏
止五人固傳循吏六人而其書之繁
簡若此亦豈無優劣之可言歟或又
謂遷有二失固有二得又謂遷固易
地而處本無優劣是果至當之評歟
諸生博學待問久矣其於二史優劣
===
必有定論願以語我
問格物窮理學者事也試舉天地萬物而
質之可乎夫天覆地載天地何依附
歟日照月臨日月何主宰歟日月運
行何周天有遲速之異四時錯行何
四仲有分至之殊天左旋矣日月麗
天何為乎右行日常盈矣月受日光
何為乎有虧同一陰陽也何以分水
punctuated:
其書之同異若此，豈無優劣之可議歟？遷序三千年事，僅五十萬言；固叙二百年事，已餘八十萬言。遷傳循吏止五人，固傳循吏六人，而其書之繁簡若此，亦豈無優劣之可言歟？或又謂遷有二失，固有二得；又謂遷固易地而處，本無優劣。是果至當之評歟？諸生博學待問久矣，其於二史優劣，必有定論，願以語我。

問：格物窮理，學者事也。試舉天地萬物而質之，可乎？夫天覆地載，天地何依附歟？日照月臨，日月何主宰歟？日月運行，何周天有遲速之異？四時錯行，何四仲有分至之殊？天左旋矣，日月麗天，何為乎右行？日常盈矣，月受日光，何為乎有虧？同一陰陽也，何以分水
translation_en:
…Such are the similarities and differences between their works: surely their relative merits admit of discussion? Sima Qian narrates three thousand years of events in only five hundred thousand words; Ban Gu recounts two hundred years of events in over eight hundred thousand words. Sima Qian includes biographies of only five exemplary officials, while Ban Gu includes six. Given these differences in the fullness and brevity of their works, surely their relative merits also admit of discussion? Some further maintain that Sima Qian had two failings and Ban Gu two strengths; others maintain that, had Sima Qian and Ban Gu exchanged circumstances, there would have been no difference in their merits. Are these truly the most fitting judgments? You students have long pursued broad learning in readiness for questioning. You must have reached settled conclusions about the relative merits of these two histories; I hope you will tell me.

Question: Investigating things and fathoming principles are the tasks of scholars. May we take Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as subjects for inquiry? Heaven covers and Earth bears: upon what do Heaven and Earth depend? The sun shines and the moon looks down: what governs the sun and moon? As the sun and moon move, why do they differ in the speed with which they complete their circuits of the heavens? As the four seasons succeed one another, why do their middle months differ in having equinoxes or solstices? Heaven revolves to the left; since the sun and moon are attached to Heaven, why do they move to the right? The sun is always full; since the moon receives sunlight, why does it wane? It is the same yin and yang throughout: how, then, is water differentiated [?]…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
少勻一閏位也何以置夊近日長日
短何稽生明生魄何主南極何常隱
而不見北極何常見而不隱月受日
光似矣中間黑者何物歟雷無形像
信矣聲之震霆何物歟風雨霜露自
何成歟烟雲霾霧自何起歟風土一
也西北多寒東南多暖何歟人品一
也西□多强東南多弱何歟禽蟲之
===
鳴伏變化何為有時草木之榮悴開
落何為有節潛者不能飛何神龍或
潛而或飛生者皆有種何麟鳳無種
而亦生有角皆能觸麒麟何以角端
有肉獸皆食生物騶虞何以不食生
物石入水則沉地在水中何不沉歟
器載滿則溢水歸滄海何不溢歟海
潮乘子胥之怒然歟黄河自天上而
punctuated: 少勻一閏位也，何以置夊近？日長日短，何稽？生明生魄，何主？南極何常隱而不見，北極何常見而不隱？月受日光，似矣，中間黑者何物歟？雷無形像，信矣，聲之震霆何物歟？風雨霜露自何成歟？烟雲霾霧自何起歟？風土一也，西北多寒，東南多暖，何歟？人品一也，西□多强，東南多弱，何歟？禽蟲之鳴伏變化，何為有時？草木之榮悴開落，何為有節？潛者不能飛，何神龍或潛而或飛？生者皆有種，何麟鳳無種而亦生？有角皆能觸，麒麟何以角端有肉？獸皆食生物，騶虞何以不食生物？石入水則沉，地在水中何不沉歟？器載滿則溢，水歸滄海何不溢歟？海潮乘子胥之怒，然歟？黄河自天上而
translation_en: …[The opening text, 少勻一閏位也何以置夊近, is garbled; it appears to include a question about intercalation][?]. By what are the lengthening and shortening of the days determined? What governs the moon’s developing brightness and darkness? Why is the south celestial pole always concealed from view, while the north celestial pole is always visible and never concealed? It seems plausible that the moon receives sunlight; what, then, are the dark areas within it? Granted that thunder has no visible form, what produces its resounding crashes? From what are wind, rain, frost, and dew formed? From what do smoke, clouds, haze, and mist arise? The natural environment is one: why is the northwest generally cold and the southeast generally warm? Human nature is one: why are people in the west [illegible character] generally strong, while those in the southeast are generally weak? Why do the calls, dormancy, and transformations of birds and insects occur at particular times? Why do the flourishing and withering, flowering and falling of plants have their appointed seasons? Creatures that live beneath the water cannot fly; why, then, can the divine dragon both dwell beneath the water and fly? All living creatures come from their own kind; why, then, do qilin and phoenixes appear even without breeding stock? All horned creatures can butt with their horns; why does the qilin have flesh at the tip of its horn? Beasts all eat living things; why does the zouyu not eat living things? A stone sinks when put into water; why does the earth, situated amid water, not sink? A vessel overflows when filled; why does the vast sea not overflow when the waters flow into it? Is it true that the ocean tides are driven by the wrath of Zixu? That the Yellow River comes from Heaven above and…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
來信歟此皆諸生耳目所見聞必講
究之有素矣請吐胸中之蘊以觀格
物之學
問民惟邦本本固邦寧古聖王之治天下
非有異常絕特之事其所謂仁政者
不過省刑罰薄稅斂二者而已以固
邦國之本以結天下之心此其要歟
仁政之化民大豈微哉因天討而作
===
五刑糾邦國以叙八刑明一成而不
變也又有赦過肆眚議獄緩死於義
何在辨五物而制地征則三壤而成
田賦明一定不可輕重也又有散利
薄征弛力舍禁其要奚從虞周之制
刑無容議矣或謂王者任德不任刑
刑其可偏廢歟禹貢之為法無間然
矣或謂治地莫不善於貢弊若是其
punctuated:
來，信歟？此皆諸生耳目所見聞，必講究之有素矣。請吐胸中之蘊，以觀格物之學。

問：民惟邦本，本固邦寧。古聖王之治天下，非有異常絕特之事，其所謂仁政者，不過省刑罰、薄稅斂二者而已。以固邦國之本，以結天下之心，此其要歟？仁政之化民大，豈微哉？因天討而作五刑，糾邦國以叙八刑，明一成而不變也。又有赦過肆眚、議獄緩死，於義何在？辨五物而制地征，則三壤而成田賦，明一定不可輕重也。又有散利薄征、弛力舍禁，其要奚從？虞周之制刑，無容議矣。或謂王者任德不任刑，刑其可偏廢歟？禹貢之為法，無間然矣。或謂治地莫不善於貢，弊若是其
translation_en:
…comes from heaven—is this true? These are all things that you students have seen or heard, and surely you have long studied them closely. Please disclose the knowledge stored within your minds, so that we may see your learning in the investigation of things.

Question: The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is at peace. In governing the realm, the sage kings of antiquity did nothing extraordinary or exceptional. What they called benevolent government amounted simply to two things: reducing punishments and lightening taxation. Was this not the essential means of securing the foundation of the state and winning the hearts of all under heaven? The influence of benevolent government in transforming the people is great—how could it be slight?

The five punishments were established in accordance with Heaven’s chastisement, and the eight punishments were arranged to regulate the states: clearly, once a penal judgment was settled, it was not to be changed. Yet there were also provisions for pardoning faults and forgiving inadvertent offenses, deliberating on criminal cases and delaying executions. What principle underlies these practices? The five categories of land and their produce were distinguished to establish land levies, and the three grades of soil were taken as the standard for assessing field taxes: clearly, once fixed, these assessments were not to be made lighter or heavier. Yet there were also provisions for distributing resources, reducing levies, relaxing labor obligations, and lifting prohibitions. What essential principle should be followed?

The penal institutions of Yu and Zhou surely admit of no criticism. Yet some say that a true king relies on virtue rather than punishment. Can punishment then be wholly set aside? The Tribute of Yu surely offers a system beyond reproach. Yet some say that, among systems of taxing cultivated land, none is worse than the tribute system. Could its defects be so…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
甚歟今律令非不明也有司按四方
之罪非少怠也宜天下無不化之民
矣然刑罰未盡清而民心未盡服者
抑何故耶貢賦非無常制也
朝廷寬恤之典非不屢下也宜海內無不獲
之夫矣然賦斂未盡平而民心未盡
安者豈無自耶伊欲獄孚於下而民
不寃賦供於上而民不擾行何道而
===
可願聞所以折衷
問兵戎有國之大事學者所當講也夫用
兵有法而法昉於何時禦敵有戰而
戰始於何人若太公之六韜黃石公
之三畧所宜知也若孔明之八陣司
馬之一成所當識也有曰伐曰侵曰
戰曰圍曰入曰遷可詳其事議得失
歟有曰敗曰取曰襲曰追曰戍曰以
punctuated:
甚歟？今律令非不明也，有司按四方之罪非少怠也，宜天下無不化之民矣。然刑罰未盡清而民心未盡服者，抑何故耶？貢賦非無常制也，朝廷寬恤之典非不屢下也，宜海內無不獲之夫矣。然賦斂未盡平而民心未盡安者，豈無自耶？伊欲獄孚於下而民不寃，賦供於上而民不擾，行何道而可？願聞所以折衷。

問：兵戎，有國之大事，學者所當講也。夫用兵有法，而法昉於何時？禦敵有戰，而戰始於何人？若太公之《六韜》、黃石公之《三畧》，所宜知也；若孔明之八陣、司馬之一成，所當識也。有曰伐、曰侵、曰戰、曰圍、曰入、曰遷，可詳其事、議得失歟？有曰敗、曰取、曰襲、曰追、曰戍、曰以
translation_en:
…so severe? Today the statutes and ordinances are certainly clear, and the responsible officials are by no means lax in investigating crimes throughout the land. There should therefore be no one in the realm who remains untransformed. Yet punishments have not become entirely just, and the people's hearts are not entirely won over. Why is this? Tribute and taxation certainly have established regulations, and the court has repeatedly issued measures of leniency and relief. There should therefore be no one within the seas who fails to obtain his due. Yet tax levies are not entirely equitable, and the people's hearts are not entirely at peace. Surely there are reasons for this? If we wish judicial decisions to command trust among those below, so that the people suffer no injustice, and taxes to be supplied to those above, so that the people suffer no disturbance, what course should we follow? We wish to hear how these matters may be judiciously resolved.

Question: Military affairs are a matter of great importance to a state and ought to be studied by scholars. There are methods for employing troops: when did these methods originate? There is battle for resisting enemies: with whom did battle begin? Such works as Taigong's Six Secret Teachings and Huangshi Gong's Three Strategies ought to be known; such arrangements as Kongming's Eight Formations and Sima's single cheng formation [?] ought to be understood. There are actions termed punitive expedition, invasion, battle, encirclement, entry, and forced relocation. Can you explain their particulars and discuss their merits and shortcomings? There are also actions termed defeating, capturing, surprise attack, pursuit, garrisoning, and leading troops [?]…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
可悉其目别是非歟古之帝王有七
旬而苗來格者有一怒而安天下者
用何兵法而然昔之將帥有八戰八
克者有七擒七縱者以何兵法而能
夫兵法之善莫備於孫武子本義始
計有曰經之以五事其事可指陳歟
謀攻有曰知勝有五其勝可歴言歟
軍形有曰度量數稱勝其意安在兵
===
勢有曰五聲五色五味其事何居將
通九變之利者知用兵與將有五危
者孰得地形六者地之道將不可不
察與六者非天地之災將之過孰失
犯三軍之衆若使一人與并敵一向
千里殺將者孰優始如處女敵人開
戸與戰勝攻取不脩其功者孰劣火
攻有五以何爲先用間有五以何爲
punctuated: 可悉其目，别是非歟？古之帝王，有七旬而苗來格者，有一怒而安天下者，用何兵法而然？昔之將帥，有八戰八克者，有七擒七縱者，以何兵法而能？夫兵法之善，莫備於《孫武子本義》。《始計》有曰：「經之以五事。」其事可指陳歟？《謀攻》有曰：「知勝有五。」其勝可歴言歟？《軍形》有曰：「度、量、數、稱、勝。」其意安在？《兵勢》有曰：「五聲、五色、五味。」其事何居？「將通九變之利者，知用兵」與「將有五危」者，孰得？「地形六者，地之道，將不可不察」與「六者非天地之災，將之過」，孰失？「犯三軍之衆，若使一人」與「并敵一向，千里殺將」者，孰優？「始如處女，敵人開戸」與「戰勝攻取，不脩其功」者，孰劣？火攻有五，以何爲先？用間有五，以何爲
translation_en:
…Can you fully enumerate these categories and distinguish right from wrong? Among the emperors and kings of antiquity, one brought the Miao to submit after seventy days, and another, in a single outburst of anger, brought peace to all under Heaven. By what military methods did they achieve this? Among the commanders of former times, one fought eight battles and won all eight; another captured and released his opponent seven times. By what military methods were they able to do so?

Nowhere is excellence in military method more fully presented than in The Essential Meaning of Master Sun Wu (Sun Wuzi benyi) [?]. “Initial Calculations” says, “Assess it by five matters.” Can you identify and explain these matters? “Planning Attacks” says, “There are five ways to know victory.” Can you recount these ways in turn? “Military Dispositions” speaks of “measurement, estimation of quantity, calculation of numbers, weighing relative strengths, and victory.” What does this mean? “Military Momentum” speaks of “the five sounds, five colors, and five flavors.” What is the significance of these things?

Compare “The commander who understands the advantages of the nine variations knows how to employ troops” with “There are five dangers for a commander”: which represents sound practice? Compare “The six types of terrain constitute the principles of the ground, which a commander must examine” with “These six are not calamities caused by Heaven and Earth, but faults of the commander”: which represents error? Compare “Directing the multitude of the Three Armies as though employing a single man” [?] with “Concentrating against the enemy in one direction and killing his commander a thousand li away”: which is superior? Compare “Begin like a maiden, and the enemy will open his door” with “Winning battles and taking objectives, yet failing to cultivate the achievement”: which is inferior?

There are five kinds of attack by fire: which should take precedence? There are five kinds of employment of spies: which should be considered…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
最夫兵貴速不貴久興師十萬日費
千金是尚拙速不尚巧遲也且如廣
之瀧水猺蠻為患久矣渠魁近已授
首餘孽尚多潜遁今欲拙速耶則彼
巢穴險阻急莫能進將欲巧遲耶則
彼剽掠不息事不可緩欲以古人兵
法治之不知何法為善諸士子生長
是鄉必有定見明以告我毋曰軍旅
===
之事未之學也
punctuated: 最？夫兵貴速，不貴久，興師十萬，日費千金，是尚拙速，不尚巧遲也。且如廣之瀧水猺蠻為患久矣，渠魁近已授首，餘孽尚多潜遁。今欲拙速耶，則彼巢穴險阻，急莫能進；將欲巧遲耶，則彼剽掠不息，事不可緩。欲以古人兵法治之，不知何法為善？諸士子生長是鄉，必有定見，明以告我，毋曰：「軍旅之事，未之學也。」
translation_en: …is foremost? In warfare, speed is prized, not protracted operations. Raising an army of a hundred thousand costs a thousand pieces of gold each day; thus clumsy speed is preferred to skillful delay. Consider the Yao tribespeople of Longshui in Guangdong, who have long caused trouble. Their ringleaders have recently been beheaded, but many remaining followers are still in hiding. If we now seek clumsy speed, their lairs lie in rugged, inaccessible terrain, and a hurried advance cannot succeed. If we instead seek skillful delay, their plundering continues unabated, and action cannot be postponed. We wish to deal with them using the military methods of the ancients, but which method would be best? You candidates were born and raised in this region and must have settled views. Explain them clearly to me; do not say, “I have not studied military affairs.”
