title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
四書
主忠信徙義崇德也
張紹齡
同考試官訓導左批德不外於仁義禮知作
者多不知此惟此篇得之是用錄出
考試官敎諭鄭批發揮明白足見作手
考試官學正朱批非得身心體驗之真者不
能到此錄之
===
實其心而宜其事此所以崇德也蓋主忠信則
存於心者無不實徙義則見於事者無不宜德
之崇也夫豈外於此哉聖人因子張問崇德而
告之以此蓋謂忠信所以進德也人不忠信則
事皆無實德無自而進矣是故曰仁曰義必實
心以體之使仁義之存於心者無一息之虛假
焉曰禮曰智必實心以存之俾禮智之具乎內
者無一毫之僞妄焉然心之實也固爲進德之
punctuated:
四書

主忠信，徙義，崇德也。
張紹齡

同考試官訓導左批：德不外於仁義禮知，作者多不知此，惟此篇得之，是用錄出。
考試官敎諭鄭批：發揮明白，足見作手。
考試官學正朱批：非得身心體驗之真者，不能到此，錄之。

實其心而宜其事，此所以崇德也。蓋主忠信，則存於心者無不實；徙義，則見於事者無不宜。德之崇也，夫豈外於此哉？聖人因子張問崇德而告之以此，蓋謂忠信所以進德也。人不忠信，則事皆無實，德無自而進矣。是故曰仁曰義，必實心以體之，使仁義之存於心者無一息之虛假焉；曰禮曰智，必實心以存之，俾禮智之具乎內者無一毫之僞妄焉。然心之實也，固爲進德之
translation_en:
Four Books

“Make loyalty and trustworthiness your guiding principles, and move toward righteousness: this is how to exalt virtue.”
Zhang Shaoling

Comment by Associate Examiner Zuo, Assistant Instructor: Virtue does not extend beyond benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom. Most writers do not understand this; this essay alone grasps it, and for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: The exposition is clear and lucid, amply demonstrating the writer’s skill.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Anyone who had not attained genuine understanding through personal experience in body and mind could not reach this level. Include it.

To make one’s heart sincere and one’s actions fitting: this is how to exalt virtue. For when loyalty and trustworthiness are one’s guiding principles, everything residing in the heart is sincere; when one moves toward righteousness, everything manifested in action is fitting. How could the exaltation of virtue lie outside this? When Zizhang asked about exalting virtue, the Sage answered him with these words. His meaning was that loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue. If a person lacks loyalty and trustworthiness, nothing he does has substance, and virtue has no means of advancing. Thus, as regards benevolence and righteousness, one must embody them with a sincere heart, so that benevolence and righteousness residing in the heart are never false, even for a single moment. As regards propriety and wisdom, one must preserve them with a sincere heart, so that propriety and wisdom possessed within contain not the slightest trace of pretense or deception. Yet sincerity of heart is assuredly, for the advancement of virtue, …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
本而不徙義則專於內而遺乎外進德之功不
有病乎故日用之間發於心而見於事者或有
未仁未義也必勇以遷之使事事合乎仁而當
乎義焉云為之際由乎中而應乎外者一有未
禮未智也必速以改之俾事事循乎禮而周乎
智焉夫內主忠信則心無不誠而本立矣外徙
於義則事無不善而日新矣內外之功交致進
脩之道兩全則仁義之得於己者日脩而罔覺
===
禮智之萃於身者日進而無疆孰謂崇德不本
於主忠信徙義也哉大抵子張才高意廣務外
少誠聖人於此既告之以主忠信徙義矣他日
問行則又以忠信篤敬告之皆所以因其失而
教之使之誠善補過以成其德也然忠信徙義
雖所以為子張告實所以示君子造道之門入
德之要也此又非特為子張也此所以為聖人
之言也
punctuated: 本，而不徙義，則專於內而遺乎外，進德之功不有病乎？故日用之間，發於心而見於事者，或有未仁未義也，必勇以遷之，使事事合乎仁而當乎義焉。云為之際，由乎中而應乎外者，一有未禮未智也，必速以改之，俾事事循乎禮而周乎智焉。夫內主忠信，則心無不誠而本立矣；外徙於義，則事無不善而日新矣。內外之功交致，進脩之道兩全，則仁義之得於己者日脩而罔覺，禮智之萃於身者日進而無疆。孰謂崇德不本於主忠信徙義也哉？大抵子張才高意廣，務外少誠。聖人於此既告之以主忠信徙義矣，他日問行，則又以忠信篤敬告之，皆所以因其失而教之，使之誠善補過，以成其德也。然忠信徙義，雖所以為子張告，實所以示君子造道之門、入德之要也。此又非特為子張也，此所以為聖人之言也。
translation_en:
…the foundation for advancing in virtue; yet if one does not turn toward righteousness, one concentrates on the inward and neglects the outward. Would this not impair the work of advancing in virtue? Thus, in daily life, whenever what arises in the heart and appears in affairs falls short of benevolence or righteousness, one must courageously change it, so that every affair accords with benevolence and conforms to righteousness. In speech and action, whenever what proceeds from within and responds to things outside falls short of ritual propriety or wisdom, one must promptly correct it, so that every affair follows ritual propriety and fully accords with wisdom. If inwardly one makes loyalty and trustworthiness one's guiding principles, the heart will be wholly sincere and the foundation established. If outwardly one turns toward righteousness, one's affairs will all be good, and one will renew oneself daily. When inward and outward efforts are both fully exerted, and both aspects of the way of moral advancement and cultivation are fulfilled, the benevolence and righteousness attained within oneself will develop daily without one's noticing, while the ritual propriety and wisdom gathered in one's person will advance daily without limit. Who could say that exalting virtue is not grounded in making loyalty and trustworthiness one's guiding principles and turning toward righteousness?

Generally speaking, Zizhang possessed great talent and broad ambitions, but devoted himself to outward matters and lacked sincerity. On this occasion, the sage had already instructed him to make loyalty and trustworthiness his guiding principles and to turn toward righteousness. When, on another day, he asked about conduct, the sage again instructed him in loyalty, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence. All this was teaching directed at his failings, enabling him to make his goodness sincere and remedy his errors, thereby perfecting his virtue. Yet although the teaching on loyalty, trustworthiness, and turning toward righteousness was addressed to Zizhang, it truly shows the gentleman the gateway to approaching the Way and the essentials of entering into virtue. It is therefore not solely for Zizhang. This is what makes it the utterance of a sage.

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
中也者天下之大本也和也者天下之達
道也致中和天地位焉萬物育焉
何應潮
同考試官訓導王批此作始終以心立說最是且
辭簡理明故錄之
考試官敎諭鄭批體認眞切
考試官學正朱批辭足以發理
中庸論心該乎道之體用推而極之則其效大
===
矣夫道之體用不外乎中和而一心有以該之
也苟能加夫推極之功則位育之效不其大歟
昔子思推本天命之性以明由敎而入者謂夫
人之一心性情具焉彼性之渾然在中而無所
偏倚謂之中也中而曰天下之大本于以見中
即天命之性而天下之理皆由是出乃道之體
而心之所該者焉情之發皆中節而無所乖戾
謂之和也和而曰天下之達道于以見和即循
punctuated:
「中也者，天下之大本也；和也者，天下之達道也。致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉。」
何應潮
同考試官訓導王批：此作始終以心立說，最是。且辭簡理明，故錄之。
考試官敎諭鄭批：體認眞切。
考試官學正朱批：辭足以發理。
中庸論心，該乎道之體用，推而極之，則其效大矣。夫道之體用不外乎中和，而一心有以該之也。苟能加夫推極之功，則位育之效不其大歟？昔子思推本天命之性，以明由敎而入者，謂夫人之一心，性情具焉。彼性之渾然在中而無所偏倚，謂之中也。中而曰天下之大本，于以見中即天命之性，而天下之理皆由是出，乃道之體，而心之所該者焉。情之發皆中節而無所乖戾，謂之和也。和而曰天下之達道，于以見和即循
translation_en:
“Equilibrium is the great foundation of all under Heaven; harmony is the universally followed Way of all under Heaven. Bring equilibrium and harmony to their utmost, and Heaven and Earth take their proper places, and the myriad things flourish.”
He Yingchao
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: This composition bases its argument throughout on the mind, which is entirely right. Moreover, its language is concise and its principles clear; hence its inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Its understanding is genuine and exact.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Its language adequately elucidates the principles.
The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the mind as encompassing the substance and functioning of the Way. Extend this to its utmost, and its effects are great indeed. The substance and functioning of the Way do not go beyond equilibrium and harmony, and the single mind encompasses them. If one can undertake the work of extending these to their utmost, will not the effects—Heaven and Earth taking their proper places and all things flourishing—be great?
Long ago, Zisi traced matters back to the nature conferred by Heaven to illuminate how one enters the Way through instruction. His meaning was that within each person’s single mind, both nature and feelings are fully present. Nature, undivided within and inclining to neither side, is called equilibrium. Calling equilibrium “the great foundation of all under Heaven” shows that equilibrium is precisely the nature conferred by Heaven, and that all the principles of the world issue from it. It is the substance of the Way and is encompassed by the mind. When the feelings arise, all attaining their proper measure without discord, this is called harmony. Calling harmony “the universally followed Way of all under Heaven” shows that harmony is precisely following…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
性之謂而天下古今之所共由乃道之用而心
之所統者焉夫道之具於人心者其體用之全
本皆如此然靜而不知所以存之則天理昧而
大本有所不立苟能自戒懼而約之以至於至
靜之中無所偏倚而其守不失則有以極其中
而大本之立益以固矣動而不知所以節之則
人欲肆而達道有所不行苟能自謹獨而精之
以至於應物之處無少差謬而無適不然則有
===
以極其和而達道之行益以廣矣夫靜而無一
息之不中則吾心正而天地之心亦正故陰陽
動靜各止其所天地不於此而位乎動而無一
事之不和則吾氣順而天地之氣亦順故充塞
無間驩欣交通萬物不於此而育乎吁始之所
發端終之所至極其皆不外於吾心也如是彼
由敎而入者惡可外心以求道乎抑觀中庸此
章首明道之本原出於天而不可易其實體備
punctuated: 性之謂，而天下古今之所共由，乃道之用，而心之所統者焉。夫道之具於人心者，其體用之全，本皆如此。然靜而不知所以存之，則天理昧而大本有所不立。苟能自戒懼而約之，以至於至靜之中無所偏倚，而其守不失，則有以極其中，而大本之立益以固矣。動而不知所以節之，則人欲肆而達道有所不行。苟能自謹獨而精之，以至於應物之處無少差謬，而無適不然，則有以極其和，而達道之行益以廣矣。夫靜而無一息之不中，則吾心正而天地之心亦正，故陰陽動靜各止其所，天地不於此而位乎？動而無一事之不和，則吾氣順而天地之氣亦順，故充塞無間，驩欣交通，萬物不於此而育乎？吁！始之所發端，終之所至極，其皆不外於吾心也如是。彼由敎而入者，惡可外心以求道乎？抑觀《中庸》此章，首明道之本原出於天而不可易，其實體備
translation_en:
…what is meant by following one’s nature: it is the path shared by all under Heaven, past and present, the functioning of the Way, and that which the heart governs. The Way as endowed in the human heart is originally complete in both its substance and its functioning in precisely this manner. Yet if, in stillness, one does not know how to preserve it, Heaven’s principle becomes obscured, and the great foundation is not fully established. If one can begin with vigilance and apprehension and thereby gather oneself inward, reaching a state in which, amid the utmost stillness, there is no deviation or leaning and one never fails to maintain it, then one can bring equilibrium to its fullest extent, and the great foundation will stand ever more firmly. If, in activity, one does not know how to regulate it, human desires run unchecked, and the universally followed Way is not fully put into practice. If one can begin with watchfulness when alone and thereby refine oneself, reaching a state in which one responds to things without the slightest error, and does so in every circumstance, then one can bring harmony to its fullest extent, and the practice of the universally followed Way will extend ever more broadly.

When in stillness there is not a single breath in which equilibrium is absent, my heart is upright, and the heart of Heaven and Earth is likewise upright. Thus yin and yang, activity and stillness, each abide in their proper place. Is it not through this that Heaven and Earth take their proper positions? When in activity there is not a single affair lacking harmony, my vital energy flows smoothly, and the vital energy of Heaven and Earth likewise flows smoothly. Thus it fills all space without interruption, joyfully circulating and communicating. Is it not through this that the myriad things are nourished? Ah! From the initial starting point to the ultimate attainment, nothing lies outside our own hearts—such is the case. How could those who enter through instruction seek the Way outside the heart? Furthermore, consider this chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean: it first makes clear that the Way’s fundamental source proceeds from Heaven and cannot be altered, and that its substantive reality is fully present…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於己而不可離次言存養省察之要終言聖神
功化之極然聖神功化之極固有非始學所當
議者而射者之的行者之歸亦學者立志之初
所當知也吁旨哉
夫義路也禮門也惟君子能由是路出入
是門也
謝慶
同考試官教諭黃批順題說理文氣自充無
===
如此篇
考試官教諭鄭批詞達不冗
考試官學正宋批得孟子立言之旨
道之在人為甚切人之賢者為能踐夫義為路
而禮為門道之切於人也尚矣求其能踐之者
其惟君子乎且夫事之合於宜者義也人之出
處去就必惟義是從而不可離義非在人共由
之路乎理之中乎節者禮也人之進退行藏必
punctuated:
於己而不可離。次言存養省察之要，終言聖神功化之極。然聖神功化之極，固有非始學所當議者，而射者之的、行者之歸，亦學者立志之初所當知也。吁，旨哉！
夫義，路也；禮，門也。惟君子能由是路，出入是門也。
謝慶
同考試官教諭黃批：順題說理，文氣自充，無如此篇。
考試官教諭鄭批：詞達不冗。
考試官學正宋批：得孟子立言之旨。
道之在人為甚切，人之賢者為能踐。夫義為路，而禮為門，道之切於人也尚矣。求其能踐之者，其惟君子乎？且夫事之合於宜者，義也。人之出處去就，必惟義是從，而不可離，義非在人共由之路乎？理之中乎節者，禮也。人之進退行藏，必
translation_en:
…is fully present within oneself and cannot be departed from. Next, it explains the essentials of nurturing and preserving one’s moral nature and examining oneself; finally, it speaks of the utmost achievements and transforming influence of the sage and the spiritually perfected person. Although these ultimate achievements and transforming influence include matters that beginners ought not yet to discuss, the target toward which the archer shoots and the destination toward which the traveler proceeds are nevertheless things that learners should know when first setting their aspirations. Ah, how profound!
“Righteousness is the road; ritual propriety is the gate. Only the gentleman can follow this road and go in and out through this gate.”
Xie Qing.
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Following the topic, it expounds the principles, and the writing’s vigor naturally fills it. No piece equals this one.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The wording conveys the meaning without verbosity.”
Comment by Examiner Song, School Instructor: “It grasps Mencius’s intent in making this statement.”
The Way is intimately connected with human life, and it is the worthy among men who can put it into practice. Righteousness is the road, and ritual propriety is the gate: how profound is the Way’s connection with human life! If we seek those capable of putting it into practice, are they not the gentlemen alone? Now, righteousness means that an affair accords with what is fitting. In entering office or remaining in retirement, in leaving or accepting a position, people must follow righteousness alone and never depart from it. Is righteousness not the road that all people alike must follow? Ritual propriety is principle conforming to its proper measure. In advancing or withdrawing, in serving or remaining out of public life, people must…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
惟禮是循而不可舎禮非在人出入之門乎夫
義路禮門乃道之切於人者如此苟非君子之
人則不能由是路而出入是門矣彼若庶人召
之役則往役者非徇人也義之宜然也君子知
乎此而守身以義故往役而不往見其所以由
是路也豈衆人所可能哉不傳贄爲臣則不見
諸侯非傲上也禮之當然也君子明乎此而律
身以禮故不爲臣則不敢往見其所以出入是
===
門也豈常人所能及哉吁義路禮門固君子之
所以自處者亦人君之所以處乎賢者也苟見
賢而不以是道是欲其入而閉其門塞其路矣
賢豈爲吾用哉嗟夫戰國之士朝叩秦關暮遊
燕璧不待人君之召而衒玉求售者比比皆然
禮義漠然也孟子以命世亞聖之才因萬章不
見諸侯之問旣反覆告之至此又以禮義之切
於人者曉之其垂世立教之意有在矣他章有
punctuated:
惟禮是循而不可舎，禮非在人出入之門乎？夫義路禮門，乃道之切於人者如此。苟非君子之人，則不能由是路而出入是門矣。彼若庶人，召之役則往役者，非徇人也，義之宜然也。君子知乎此而守身以義，故往役而不往見，其所以由是路也，豈衆人所可能哉？不傳贄爲臣，則不見諸侯，非傲上也，禮之當然也。君子明乎此而律身以禮，故不爲臣則不敢往見，其所以出入是門也，豈常人所能及哉？
吁！義路禮門，固君子之所以自處者，亦人君之所以處乎賢者也。苟見賢而不以是道，是欲其入而閉其門、塞其路矣，賢豈爲吾用哉？嗟夫！戰國之士，朝叩秦關，暮遊燕璧，不待人君之召而衒玉求售者，比比皆然，禮義漠然也。孟子以命世亞聖之才，因萬章不見諸侯之問，旣反覆告之至此，又以禮義之切於人者曉之，其垂世立教之意有在矣。他章有
translation_en:
…must follow ritual alone and never abandon it: is ritual not the gate through which people enter and leave? Righteousness as the road and ritual as the gate: such is the Way’s intimate importance to human life. Unless one is a gentleman, one cannot follow this road and pass through this gate. Take the commoner who, when summoned for labor service, goes to perform it: this is not compliance with another person’s wishes, but what righteousness requires. The gentleman understands this and maintains his integrity through righteousness. Thus he goes to perform labor service but does not go merely to attend an audience. This is how he follows that road. How could ordinary people manage this? If one has not presented an introductory gift and become a subject, one does not attend an audience with a feudal lord. This is not arrogance toward a superior, but what ritual requires. The gentleman understands this and regulates his conduct through ritual. Thus, unless he has become a subject, he does not presume to go for an audience. This is how he passes through that gate. How could an ordinary person attain this?
Ah! Righteousness as the road and ritual as the gate are indeed the means by which the gentleman conducts himself, but they are also the means by which a ruler should treat worthy men. If a ruler seeks an audience with a worthy man without following this Way, he wishes the man to enter while closing his gate and blocking his road. How could such a worthy man serve me? Alas! Among the scholars of the Warring States, those who knocked at Qin’s passes in the morning and roamed Yan’s ramparts [?] in the evening, displaying their jade in search of a buyer without waiting for a ruler’s summons, were everywhere. They were indifferent to ritual and righteousness. Mencius, possessing the talents of an age-defining figure and Second Sage, had already explained the matter repeatedly and at length in response to Wan Zhang’s question about not attending audiences with feudal lords. Here he further enlightened him by explaining the intimate importance of ritual and righteousness to human life. Therein lay his intention to establish teachings for later generations. In another chapter there is…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
曰居天下之廣居立天下之正位行天下之大
道孟軻氏其以斯言爲已任也歟
易
應乎天而時行
張紹齡
同考試官訓導王批題本平易場中作者多
專指九二爲應乾殊失本義之旨此篇體認切而詞
不繁故錄之以冠本房
===
考試官敎諭鄭批辭理兼優於衆作故錄之
考試官學正朱批得本義之旨
順乎天而隨時有爲大有之君爲然也蓋君道
莫大乎體天而致治也六五之君應天而時行
此其治之所以元亨也歟昔夫子傳彖釋大有
元亨之辭舉卦體而言謂夫下乾爲天而六五
應之時有可爲而六五乗之六五之君其治有
也應天而時行蓋必心焉同乎天心之至公德
punctuated:
曰：「居天下之廣居，立天下之正位，行天下之大道。」孟軻氏其以斯言爲已任也歟？

易
應乎天而時行
張紹齡

同考試官訓導王批：題本平易，場中作者多專指九二爲應乾，殊失本義之旨。此篇體認切而詞不繁，故錄之以冠本房。

考試官敎諭鄭批：辭理兼優於衆作，故錄之。

考試官學正朱批：得本義之旨。

順乎天而隨時有爲，大有之君爲然也。蓋君道莫大乎體天而致治也。六五之君應天而時行，此其治之所以元亨也歟？昔夫子傳彖，釋大有元亨之辭，舉卦體而言，謂夫下乾爲天而六五應之，時有可爲而六五乗之。六五之君其治有也，應天而時行，蓋必心焉同乎天心之至公，德
translation_en:
…says: “Dwell in the broad dwelling of all under Heaven, stand in the correct position of all under Heaven, and walk the great Way of all under Heaven.” Did Meng Ke not take these words as his own responsibility?

Book of Changes
“Responding to Heaven and acting in accordance with the time”
Zhang Shaoling

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: The topic is straightforward, yet many candidates in the examination hall identify responding to Qian exclusively with the nine in the second place, seriously missing the purport of the Original Meaning. This essay shows precise understanding without excessive verbiage; therefore it is recorded here at the head of the essays from this examination room.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Its language and reasoning are both superior to those of the other compositions; therefore it is recorded here.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: It grasps the purport of the Original Meaning.

To follow Heaven and undertake action as the time requires—such is the ruler represented by Great Possession. For nothing in the ruler’s Way is greater than embodying Heaven and bringing about good government. The ruler represented by the six in the fifth place responds to Heaven and acts in accordance with the time: is this not why his government enjoys supreme success? Formerly, when the Master composed the Commentary on the Judgments and explained the words “supreme success” in Great Possession, he spoke in terms of the hexagram’s structure. He meant that the lower trigram, Qian, represents Heaven, and the six in the fifth place responds to it; when the time offers an opportunity for action, the six in the fifth place seizes it. In governing what he possesses, the ruler represented by the six in the fifth place responds to Heaven and acts in accordance with the time. title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
焉合乎天德之至健天命有善我則命有德而
善必揚之焉天命無惡我則討有罪而惡必遏
之焉一舉措也與天黙契而不違一設施也與
天脗合而不悖夫既無往而不應乎天尤必無
適而不以其時時可行也於焉乗之以有行時
可為也於焉隨之以有為善必揚之而揚善以
時不先而不後焉惡必遏之而遏惡以時無過
而無不及焉凡設施也必當其時之可凡舉措
===
也必適乎時之宜五之應天而時行如此則治
有之大善而亨也豈不宜哉粤稽諸古堯舜之
承天道而通變宜民湯武之奉天命而志在救
民此皆應天而時行者也故堯舜之世黎民於
變而四方風動湯武之時兆民允殖而萬姓悅
服是皆有元亨之治也然則堯舜湯武其大有
之六五也歟
以言乎遠則不禦以言乎邇則靜而正
punctuated:
焉合乎天德之至健。天命有善，我則命有德而善必揚之焉；天命無惡，我則討有罪而惡必遏之焉。一舉措也，與天黙契而不違；一設施也，與天脗合而不悖。夫既無往而不應乎天，尤必無適而不以其時。時可行也，於焉乗之以有行；時可為也，於焉隨之以有為。善必揚之，而揚善以時，不先而不後焉；惡必遏之，而遏惡以時，無過而無不及焉。凡設施也，必當其時之可；凡舉措也，必適乎時之宜。五之應天而時行如此，則治有之大善而亨也，豈不宜哉？粤稽諸古，堯舜之承天道而通變宜民，湯武之奉天命而志在救民，此皆應天而時行者也。故堯舜之世，黎民於變而四方風動；湯武之時，兆民允殖而萬姓悅服。是皆有元亨之治也。然則堯舜湯武，其大有之六五也歟？

以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正。
translation_en:
…and in virtue accords with the utmost vigor of Heaven’s virtue. Heaven’s mandate favors goodness; I therefore appoint the virtuous and ensure that goodness is promoted. Heaven’s mandate excludes evil; I therefore punish the guilty and ensure that evil is checked. Every action tacitly accords with Heaven without deviation; every measure agrees with Heaven without contradiction. Since nowhere does he fail to respond to Heaven, still more must he act everywhere in accordance with the proper time. When the time permits action, he seizes it and acts; when the time permits an undertaking, he follows it and undertakes it. Goodness must be promoted, and he promotes it at the proper time, neither too early nor too late. Evil must be checked, and he checks it at the proper time, neither going too far nor falling short. Every measure must suit what the time permits; every action must accord with what the time requires. Such is the way the fifth-line ruler responds to Heaven and acts according to the time. Is it not fitting, then, that his government of what he possesses should attain supreme goodness and success?

Examining antiquity, we find that Yao and Shun upheld the Way of Heaven, adapting to change to benefit the people, while Tang and Wu honored Heaven’s mandate, setting their hearts on rescuing the people. All these rulers responded to Heaven and acted according to the time. Thus, in the age of Yao and Shun, the common people were transformed, and the four quarters were stirred as if by the wind. In the time of Tang and Wu, the myriad people truly prospered, and all the families submitted gladly. These were all instances of government attaining supreme success. Were Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, then, embodiments of the six in the fifth place of Great Possession?

“Speaking of what is distant, it encounters no obstruction; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct.”

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
張紹齡
同考試官訓導王批此題作者多泛講不同能以
陰陽之理貫於事物立說者僅見此篇
考試官教諭鄭批辭理俱到可取
考試官學正朱批說出易理之所以廣大者甚
明
隨所在而各足者易理之廣大也夫易理無間
於遠近則隨在而各足矣謂之廣大不亦宜乎
===
昔大傳聖人論易之廣大而言及此謂夫易之
爲易陰陽之理而已是理也語遠而有所盡則
周乎近而窮於遠矣非廣大也語近而有不存
則該乎遠而忽於近矣非廣大也今焉以至遠
言之吾知其際天極地事物之充塞乎兩間者
陰陽之理皆有以體之而無遺不以地之至遠
而有限量之可言焉往古來今事物之散殊於
古今者陰陽之理皆有以貫之而無間不以時
punctuated:
張紹齡

同考試官訓導王批：此題作者多泛講，不同能以陰陽之理貫於事物立說者，僅見此篇。

考試官教諭鄭批：辭理俱到，可取。

考試官學正朱批：說出易理之所以廣大者甚明。

隨所在而各足者，易理之廣大也。夫易理無間於遠近，則隨在而各足矣。謂之廣大，不亦宜乎？

昔大傳聖人論易之廣大而言及此，謂夫易之爲易，陰陽之理而已。是理也，語遠而有所盡，則周乎近而窮於遠矣，非廣大也；語近而有不存，則該乎遠而忽於近矣，非廣大也。今焉以至遠言之，吾知其際天極地，事物之充塞乎兩間者，陰陽之理皆有以體之而無遺，不以地之至遠而有限量之可言焉。往古來今，事物之散殊於古今者，陰陽之理皆有以貫之而無間，不以時
translation_en:
Zhang Shaoling

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: Most writers on this topic discuss it in general terms. This essay alone [?] develops its argument by showing how the principles of yin and yang run through affairs and things.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor (jiaoyu): Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished; worthy of selection.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor (xuezheng): It explains very clearly why the principles of the Changes are broad and great.

That they are complete wherever they are found constitutes the breadth and greatness of the principles of the Changes. Since these principles admit no gap between far and near, they are complete wherever they are found. Is it not fitting to call them broad and great?

Formerly, in the Great Commentary, the sage discussed the breadth and greatness of the Changes and spoke these words. What makes the Changes the Changes, he meant, is simply the principles of yin and yang. If, speaking of what is distant, these principles reached some limit, they would encompass what is near but be exhausted in what is far: this would not be breadth and greatness. If, speaking of what is near, there were somewhere they did not exist, they would embrace what is far but overlook what is near: this would not be breadth and greatness. Now, speaking of the utmost distance, I know that, to the bounds of heaven and the ends of earth, the principles of yin and yang constitute the substance of all the affairs and things filling the space between them, leaving nothing out. However distant a place may be, no limit to these principles can be asserted. From antiquity through the present, the principles of yin and yang run without interruption through all the diverse affairs and things of past and present; nor, on account of time …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之至遠而有涯涘之可擬焉其遠之無有盡也
為何如以至近言之吾知其几席之下事物之
觸乎目者雖至微也不待涉於動作而陰陽之
實理以具初不以地之近而有所違焉瞬息之
際事物之接乎前者雖至小也不待形於施為
而陰陽之正理以存亦不以時之近而有所外
焉其近之無不存也又何如吁言乎遠則不以
遠而窮言乎近則不以近而偏易理之廣大非
===
此而何歟抑嘗觀之中庸所謂語大天下莫能
載即此之遠則不禦也所謂語小天下莫能破
即此之近則靜而正也所謂洋洋乎發育萬物
峻極于天即下文言乎天地之間則備者焉蓋
易之道即中庸之道子思之於夫子得傳道之
心法不然何其言之不異若符節之相合也歟
書
日宣三德夙夜浚明有家日嚴祗敬六德
punctuated:
之至遠而有涯涘之可擬焉。其遠之無有盡也，為何如？以至近言之，吾知其几席之下，事物之觸乎目者，雖至微也，不待涉於動作，而陰陽之實理以具，初不以地之近而有所違焉；瞬息之際，事物之接乎前者，雖至小也，不待形於施為，而陰陽之正理以存，亦不以時之近而有所外焉。其近之無不存也，又何如？吁！言乎遠，則不以遠而窮；言乎近，則不以近而偏。易理之廣大，非此而何歟？抑嘗觀之，《中庸》所謂「語大，天下莫能載」，即此之「遠則不禦」也；所謂「語小，天下莫能破」，即此之「近則靜而正」也；所謂「洋洋乎發育萬物，峻極于天」，即下文「言乎天地之間則備」者焉。蓋《易》之道，即《中庸》之道。子思之於夫子，得傳道之心法，不然何其言之不異，若符節之相合也歟？

書

日宣三德，夙夜浚明有家；日嚴祗敬六德，
translation_en:
…nor does the utmost remoteness of time impose any conceivable boundary upon it. How boundless, then, is its reach into the distant! Speaking of what is nearest, I know that around our very tables and mats, the things that meet our eyes, however minute, already embody the substantial principles of yin and yang before any movement or action occurs. Spatial proximity never causes anything to depart from these principles. In the span of an instant, the things that come before us, however slight, already contain the correct principles of yin and yang before these take form in practical activity. Temporal proximity likewise leaves nothing outside them. How all-pervading, then, is its presence in what is near! Ah! Speaking of the distant, it is not exhausted by distance; speaking of the near, it is not confined by proximity. What else could the breadth and greatness of the principles of the Changes mean?

I have also considered this: what the Doctrine of the Mean calls “Speaking of its greatness, nothing under Heaven can contain it” is precisely what is meant here by “In its remoteness, it encounters no impediment.” What it calls “Speaking of its smallness, nothing under Heaven can divide it” is precisely what is meant here by “In its nearness, it is still and correct.” What it calls “Vastly flowing, it brings forth and nourishes the myriad things, reaching in its loftiness to Heaven” is precisely what the following passage means by “Speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it encompasses everything.” For the Way of the Changes is the Way of the Doctrine of the Mean. Zisi received from the Master the essential teaching through which the Way is transmitted. Otherwise, how could their words agree so completely, like the matching halves of a tally?

text:
亮采有邦翕受敷施九德咸事俊乂
在官百僚師師百工惟時撫于五辰
庶績其凝
余敬

陳言令人厭觀求其詞氣春容理致自見此作得之
考試官教諭鄭批發明臯陶知人之㫖精切未有
如此篇者
===
考試官學正朱批說書明盡此卷特優
賢才脩德不同各有以宜其職人君用賢盡道
斯有以成其功蓋德有多寡宜職有大小也人
君誠能用賢而盡其道又豈不致治功之成哉
昔臯陶陳知人之謨於舜及此謂夫官人之道
不求其德之備而取其德之常彼人於九德之
中有其三必日宣而充廣之而使之益以著是
三德爲有常矣是人也而爲大夫必能夙夜匪
punctuated:
亮采有邦。翕受敷施，九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師，百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績其凝。

考試官教諭鄭批：發明臯陶知人之㫖，精切未有如此篇者。
考試官學正朱批：說書明盡，此卷特優。
賢才脩德不同，各有以宜其職；人君用賢盡道，斯有以成其功。蓋德有多寡，宜職有大小也。人君誠能用賢而盡其道，又豈不致治功之成哉？昔臯陶陳知人之謨於舜，及此謂夫官人之道，不求其德之備，而取其德之常。彼人於九德之中有其三，必日宣而充廣之，而使之益以著，是三德爲有常矣。是人也而爲大夫，必能夙夜匪
translation_en:
…faithfully discharge the duties of governing a state. Receive them all together and distribute them in service: let those possessing the nine virtues all serve, and let talented and accomplished men hold office. Let the many officials learn from one another, and all officers attend to their proper duties, acting in accordance with the five seasonal periods; then the various achievements of government will be firmly established.
Yu Jing.
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: Most candidates who addressed this topic in the examination repeated stale expressions, making their work tiresome to read. If one seeks an expansive ease of expression and reasoning whose import emerges naturally, this composition achieves it.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: In elucidating Gao Yao’s purport concerning the discernment of men, no essay has matched this one’s precision and pertinence.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, School Instructor: Its exposition of the Book of Documents is clear and thorough. This paper is exceptionally fine.
Worthy and talented men differ in their cultivation of virtue, and each has qualities suited to his office. When the ruler fully follows the proper way of employing worthy men, he can thereby bring his work to fruition. For men possess more or fewer virtues, and the offices to which they are suited are greater or lesser. If the ruler can truly employ worthy men in complete accordance with the proper way, how could he fail to achieve successful government?
Long ago, when Gao Yao presented to Shun his counsel on discerning men, he reached this point and explained that the way to appoint men to office was not to demand completeness in their virtues, but to value constancy in them. If a man possesses three of the nine virtues, he must manifest and extend them daily, making them increasingly evident; these three virtues will then be constant in him. If such a man becomes a grand master, he will surely be able, day and night, without …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
懈明治夫有家之事焉人於九德之中有其六
尢必日嚴而祗敬之而使之益以謹是六德爲
有常矣若人也而爲諸侯必能克勤無怠亮采
夫有邦之政焉夫德之多寡雖不同人君惟能
合而受之寸善片長無或遺布而用之量德隨
才無不當如此則九德之賢或浚明或亮采咸
事其事而野無遺賢矣俊乂之人或有邦或有
家皆在官使而下無遺才矣百僚皆以德而相
===
師善與人同無媚嫉也百工皆及時以趨事順
于五辰無玩愒也由是禮樂明備而庶政有惟
和之休刑政脩舉而庶績有咸熈之美治功之
成爲何如哉抑嘗考之人君御世不患治功之
不成惟患賢才之不用不患賢才之不用惟患
任使之無方苟徒求其德之備而不求其德之
常幾何不虚譽隆而實德病哉故臯陶陳知人
之謨拳拳及此無非欲以天下之才任天下之
punctuated:
懈，明治夫有家之事焉。人於九德之中有其六，尢必日嚴而祗敬之，而使之益以謹，是六德爲有常矣。若人也而爲諸侯，必能克勤無怠，亮采夫有邦之政焉。夫德之多寡雖不同，人君惟能合而受之，寸善片長無或遺；布而用之，量德隨才無不當。如此，則九德之賢，或浚明，或亮采，咸事其事，而野無遺賢矣；俊乂之人，或有邦，或有家，皆在官使，而下無遺才矣。百僚皆以德而相師，善與人同，無媚嫉也；百工皆及時以趨事，順于五辰，無玩愒也。由是禮樂明備，而庶政有惟和之休；刑政脩舉，而庶績有咸熈之美。治功之成爲何如哉！

抑嘗考之，人君御世，不患治功之不成，惟患賢才之不用；不患賢才之不用，惟患任使之無方。苟徒求其德之備，而不求其德之常，幾何不虚譽隆而實德病哉？故臯陶陳知人之謨，拳拳及此，無非欲以天下之才任天下之
translation_en:
…without slackening, and administer clearly the affairs of a noble house. If a person possesses six of the nine virtues, he must all the more maintain daily vigilance and reverently attend to them, making his conduct increasingly circumspect. These six virtues will then be constant. If such a person becomes a feudal lord, he will surely work diligently without indolence and faithfully discharge the duties of governing a state. Although people differ in the number of virtues they possess, the ruler need only gather and accept them, overlooking no small goodness or particular strength, and deploy them in service, assessing their virtue and assigning them according to their abilities, so that every appointment is fitting. Thus, worthy men possessing the nine virtues will each attend to their duties, some governing with profound discernment and others faithfully discharging their responsibilities; no worthy man will remain neglected in the countryside. Men of outstanding ability, whether governing states or noble houses, will all hold office and serve; no talent will remain neglected among those below. The many officials will take one another as models of virtue, joining others in goodness without flattery or jealousy. All officers will attend to their duties at the proper times, following the seasons governed by the five celestial bodies, without idling or wasting their days. Consequently, rites and music will be clearly established and fully provided for, and the various affairs of government will enjoy the blessing of harmony. Punishments and administration will be put in good order, and every undertaking will flourish. How great, then, will be the achievement of good government!

Yet I have considered this: in ruling the world, a sovereign should worry not that good government will fail to be achieved, but that worthy and talented men will not be employed; not that they will not be employed, but that their appointment and deployment will lack proper method. If he merely demands completeness of virtue without seeking constancy of virtue, how can inflated reputations fail to flourish while actual virtue suffers? Thus, when Gao Yao set forth his counsel on discerning men, he earnestly addressed this matter, desiring only to entrust the talents of the realm with the realm’s…

折民惟刑禹平水土主名山川稷降
播種農殖嘉穀三后成功惟殷于民
士制百姓于刑之中以教祗德
===

所窘能摹寫穆王訓刑之意殆盡僅見此篇

此賢王舉之以訓刑也夫為治之本在德而刑

punctuated:
治也。吁！有虞雍熈泰和之盛，良有以夫！

乃命重黎絕地天通，罔有降格。羣后之逮在下，明明棐常，鰥寡無蓋。皇帝清問下民，鰥寡有辭于苗。德威惟畏，德明惟明。乃命三后恤功于民：伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以教祗德。

吳言

同考試官教諭黃批：題頭緒頗多，作者甚為所窘。能摹寫穆王訓刑之意殆盡，僅見此篇。

考試官教諭鄭批：文足以發理，此作為最。

考試官學正朱批：辭詳整而理縝密。

聖世君臣盡心以圖治，尤資大臣明刑以輔治。此賢王舉之以訓刑也。夫為治之本在德，而刑特以輔其所不及耳。賢王歷叙聖世之事以命
translation_en:
…to govern the realm. Ah! The flourishing harmony and supreme peace of the age of Youyu truly had their foundation in this!

“He then commanded Chong and Li to sever communication between earth and heaven, so that there would be no descending spirits. The various lords and those below them clearly upheld the constant principles, and the plight of widowers and widows was not concealed. The august emperor carefully inquired among the common people, and widowers and widows brought complaints against the Miao. The awe of his virtue alone inspired fear; the illumination of his virtue alone brought enlightenment. He then commanded three lords to undertake work for the people's welfare: Boyi promulgated the statutes, restraining the people through punishments; Yu brought the waters and lands into order and took charge of the renowned mountains and rivers; Ji taught sowing and planting, cultivating fine grain. The three lords accomplished their tasks, bringing abundance to the people. The Minister of Crime regulated the common people through punishments that struck the proper mean, teaching them to revere virtue.”

Wu Yan

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The topic has many threads, which placed considerable constraints on the writers. This is the only essay I have seen that conveys almost fully King Mu's intent in his instructions concerning punishments.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “For writing that adequately elucidates principle, this essay is the best.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Director of Studies: “The wording is detailed and orderly, and the reasoning meticulous.”

In the age of the sages, rulers and ministers devoted their whole hearts to achieving good government. They relied especially on great ministers to clarify punishments as an aid to governing. These were the precedents that the worthy king cited in giving instructions concerning punishments. For the foundation of government lies in virtue; punishments merely supplement it where its influence does not reach. The worthy king recounted in sequence the affairs of the age of the sages in order to instruct…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
呂侯其知本歟昔穆王之意若謂昔在有虞三
苗昏虐人心蓋泯泯棼棼矣帝舜以爲治莫先
於正人心也首命重黎脩明祀典絕地天之通
嚴幽明之分焄蒿妖誕之說舉屏息而不作當
時大小之臣皆精白一心輔助常道雖鰥寡無
告之微亦得以自伸焉尤恐無以盡達下情也
於是虛心而問下民鰥寡得以聲苗之過苗以
虐爲威過也帝則以德威而天下無不畏苗以
===
察爲明過也帝則以德明而天下無不明焉民
漸吏化如此不命官分任其責治能有成乎乃
命三后致憂民之功伯夷降典折民邪妄以正
人心禹平水土主名山川以定民居稷降播種
農殖嘉穀以厚民生三后成功而致民之殷盛
富庶也治化之盛如此不制刑以輔不及治能
永保乎於是命皐陶爲士師之官彼民之漸涵
吾治化固無事於刑其頑慢弗率者則制之于
punctuated: 呂侯，其知本歟！昔穆王之意若謂：昔在有虞，三苗昏虐，人心蓋泯泯棼棼矣。帝舜以爲治莫先於正人心也，首命重黎脩明祀典，絕地天之通，嚴幽明之分，焄蒿妖誕之說舉屏息而不作。當時大小之臣皆精白一心，輔助常道，雖鰥寡無告之微，亦得以自伸焉。尤恐無以盡達下情也，於是虛心而問下民，鰥寡得以聲苗之過。苗以虐爲威，過也；帝則以德威，而天下無不畏。苗以察爲明，過也；帝則以德明，而天下無不明焉。民漸吏化如此，不命官分任其責，治能有成乎？乃命三后致憂民之功：伯夷降典，折民邪妄，以正人心；禹平水土，主名山川，以定民居；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀，以厚民生。三后成功，而致民之殷盛富庶也。治化之盛如此，不制刑以輔不及，治能永保乎？於是命皐陶爲士師之官。彼民之漸涵吾治化，固無事於刑；其頑慢弗率者，則制之于
translation_en:
…the Marquis of Lü—did he not understand the foundation of government? King Mu’s meaning was as though he were saying: In the days of Youyu, the Three Miao were benighted and cruel, and people’s hearts had fallen into darkness and confusion. Emperor Shun held that nothing took precedence in government over rectifying people’s hearts. He first ordered Chong and Li to restore and clarify the sacrificial ordinances, sever communication between earth and heaven, and enforce the distinction between the unseen and visible realms. All strange and fantastic talk of spirit vapors was thereby silenced and ceased to arise. The ministers of that time, great and small, were pure and single-minded in supporting the constant Way. Even widowers and widows, humble people with no one to whom they could appeal, were able to make their cases heard.

Still fearing that the circumstances of those below might not be fully communicated, he opened his mind and questioned the common people. Widowers and widows could thus voice the wrongs of the Miao. The Miao used cruelty to inspire awe: this was their fault. The emperor instead inspired awe through virtue, and none under Heaven failed to revere him. The Miao took intrusive scrutiny for discernment: this was their fault. The emperor instead exercised discernment through virtue, and none under Heaven remained unenlightened.

With the people thus imbued and the officials transformed [?], could government achieve success without appointing officers to share its responsibilities? He therefore charged the three lords with carrying out the work of caring for the people. Bo Yi promulgated the ordinances, checking the people’s depravity and delusion so as to rectify their hearts. Yu brought the waters and land into order and took charge of the renowned mountains and rivers, so as to secure the people’s dwellings. Ji imparted the methods of sowing and planting, cultivating fine grains so as to enrich the people’s livelihood. The three lords accomplished their work, bringing the people prosperity, wealth, and abundance.

With government and moral transformation flourishing in this way, could good order be preserved forever without establishing punishments to supplement what they could not reach? He therefore appointed Gao Yao to the office of Chief Judge. Those people gradually steeped in our governance and moral influence would assuredly have no need of punishment; but those who were obstinate, negligent, and unwilling to follow would be restrained within…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
刑辟之中民之範圍吾治理亦無待於法其泯
棼未信者則制之以刑罰之當非徒繩之以法
也正以檢制其心而教祗德使民心之未正者
悉歸於正焉非直示之以威也所以檢束其心
而教敬德使人心之未善者皆化於善焉吁德
以化之於先君臣圖治為甚詳刑以維之於後
一臣保治為有要此有虞之治所以盡善也歟
雖然德化乃聖人之本心刑罰亦聖人之不得
===
已二者固不可偏廢也穆王訓刑首及乎此其
亦知所尚矣惜乎專訓贖刑雖罪大辟之科而
亦有金贖之例曾謂有虞之制有是哉夫子錄
之蓋以示戒云
詩
即有邰家室誕降嘉種維秬維秠維穈維
芑恒之秬秠是穫是畝恒之穈芑是
任是負以歸肇祀誕我祀如何或春
punctuated:
刑辟之中。民之範圍吾治理，亦無待於法；其泯棼未信者，則制之以刑罰之當。非徒繩之以法也，正以檢制其心而教祗德，使民心之未正者悉歸於正焉；非直示之以威也，所以檢束其心而教敬德，使人心之未善者皆化於善焉。吁！德以化之於先，君臣圖治為甚詳；刑以維之於後，一臣保治為有要。此有虞之治所以盡善也歟！雖然，德化乃聖人之本心，刑罰亦聖人之不得已，二者固不可偏廢也。穆王訓刑，首及乎此，其亦知所尚矣。惜乎專訓贖刑，雖罪大辟之科，而亦有金贖之例，曾謂有虞之制有是哉！夫子錄之，蓋以示戒云。

詩

即有邰家室，誕降嘉種：維秬維秠，維穈維芑。恒之秬秠，是穫是畝；恒之穈芑，是任是負，以歸肇祀。誕我祀如何？或春
translation_en:
…within the bounds of penal law. The people encompassed by our good government likewise have no need of laws; those who remain confused and disorderly and have not become trustworthy [?] are restrained through appropriate punishments. This is not merely to hold them to the law: it is precisely to restrain their hearts and teach them to revere virtue, so that all those whose hearts are not yet upright return to uprightness. Nor is it merely to display awe-inspiring authority: it is to discipline their hearts and teach them to respect virtue, so that all those whose hearts are not yet good are transformed toward goodness. Ah! With virtue first transforming the people, ruler and ministers planned good government in the utmost detail; with punishments subsequently sustaining it, a single minister grasped the essentials of preserving good government. Was this not how the government of Youyu attained complete excellence?

Nevertheless, transformation through virtue was the sage’s fundamental intention, while punishment was something to which the sage resorted only when compelled. Neither could properly be neglected. King Mu addressed this first in his instructions on punishments, so he too understood what should be esteemed. Regrettably, he concentrated his instructions on the redemption of punishments: even offenses classified as capital crimes could be redeemed by payments of metal. Could anyone really suppose that the institutions of Youyu contained such a provision? The Master recorded this, presumably to offer a warning.

The Book of Odes

He settled at Tai and established his household; abundantly he bestowed fine seeds: black millet and double-grained black millet, red millet and white millet. Everywhere the black millet and double-grained black millet were reaped and stacked in the fields; everywhere the red millet and white millet were carried in loads on shoulders and backs. Returning with them, he inaugurated the sacrifices. And how do we perform our sacrifices? Some pound the grain [?]…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或揄或簸或蹂釋之叟叟烝之浮浮
載謀載惟取蕭祭脂取羝以軷載燔
載烈以興嗣歲卬盛于豆于豆于登
其香始升上帝居歆胡臭亶時后稷
肇祀庶無罪悔以迄于今
陳鍾
同考試官訓導黃批后稷以農功封邰而肇
祀後人郊祀而天格之速由后稷有農功也此作
===
深得本旨錄之
考試官教諭鄭批始終歸重后稷之農功有
定見者
考試官學正朱批說后稷之功明白
詩人原始祖受封主祭而詳奉祭之事述後王
尊祖配天而推天饗之由蓋后稷以農功受封
而肇祀天心眷之久矣後王尊以配天之祭而
天饗之速者豈不由于此耶昔周公制禮尊后
punctuated:
或揄，或簸，或蹂，釋之叟叟，烝之浮浮。載謀載惟，取蕭祭脂，取羝以軷，載燔載烈，以興嗣歲。卬盛于豆，于豆于登，其香始升，上帝居歆。胡臭亶時？后稷肇祀，庶無罪悔，以迄于今。
陳鍾
同考試官訓導黃批：「后稷以農功封邰而肇祀，後人郊祀而天格之速，由后稷有農功也。此作深得本旨，錄之。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「始終歸重后稷之農功，有定見者。」
考試官學正朱批：「說后稷之功明白。」
詩人原始祖受封主祭，而詳奉祭之事；述後王尊祖配天，而推天饗之由。蓋后稷以農功受封而肇祀，天心眷之久矣。後王尊以配天之祭，而天饗之速者，豈不由于此耶？昔周公制禮，尊后
translation_en:
…Some scoop, some winnow, some rub the grain; they rinse it with a swishing sound and steam it until the vapor rises thickly. They deliberate and consider, take southernwood to offer with fat, and take a ram for the roadside sacrifice. They roast and broil, thereby inaugurating the coming year. I fill the offering vessels—the dou vessels and the deng vessels. As their fragrance begins to rise, the Lord on High accepts the offering. Why is the fragrance truly fitting? Hou Ji began these sacrifices; may there have been no fault or cause for regret, down to this day.

Chen Zhong

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: “Hou Ji was enfeoffed at Tai for his agricultural achievements and there inaugurated sacrifices. When his descendants offered the suburban sacrifice, Heaven came swiftly because of Hou Ji’s agricultural achievements. This composition grasps the fundamental meaning deeply. Let it be recorded.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “From beginning to end, the emphasis rests on Hou Ji’s agricultural achievements. The writer has a settled understanding.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, School Instructor: “The explanation of Hou Ji’s achievements is clear.”

The poet traces how the founding ancestor received his fief and presided over sacrifices, detailing the conduct of the offerings; he recounts how later kings honored their ancestor by associating him with Heaven in sacrifice, and investigates why Heaven accepted the offerings. Hou Ji received his fief for his agricultural achievements and inaugurated sacrifices; Heaven had long cherished him. When later kings honored him with sacrifices associating him with Heaven, was this not the reason Heaven accepted them so swiftly? In former times, when the Duke of Zhou established the rites, he honored Hou…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
稷以配天故作此詩謂夫后稷務兹稼穡有功
乎民故堯封之有邰之地使主姜嫄之祀斯時
也后稷以嘉種而降之其種伊何不惟有黑黍
之秠而又有一稃二米之秠不惟有赤粱粟之
縻而又有白粱粟之芑徧種之而旣成也則穫
而棲之于畝徧播之而巳熟也則任而負之以
歸所以然者將以肇宗廟之祭始羣神之祀也
然是祀也后稷之所奉也其事何如或以嘉穀
===
而春揄之或以嘉穀而簸蹂之釋之聲叟叟也
蒸之氣浮浮也謀焉而卜日擇士惟焉而齊戒
具脩祀宗廟之主而蕭脂以爇祀行道之神而
牡羊以將燔焉而尸羞無不具也烈焉而尸羞
無不供也所以然者將以興來歲之祀于無窮
繼往歲之祀于不替也后稷以農功而肇祀如
此後人寧不尊之以配天之祭乎于是我以菹
醢而盛之于豆也我以太羹而薦之于登也馨
punctuated:
稷以配天，故作此詩。謂夫后稷務兹稼穡，有功乎民，故堯封之有邰之地，使主姜嫄之祀。斯時也，后稷以嘉種而降之。其種伊何？不惟有黑黍之秠，而又有一稃二米之秠；不惟有赤粱粟之縻，而又有白粱粟之芑。徧種之而旣成也，則穫而棲之于畝；徧播之而巳熟也，則任而負之以歸。所以然者，將以肇宗廟之祭，始羣神之祀也。
然是祀也，后稷之所奉也，其事何如？或以嘉穀而春揄之，或以嘉穀而簸蹂之。釋之聲叟叟也，蒸之氣浮浮也。謀焉而卜日擇士，惟焉而齊戒具脩。祀宗廟之主，而蕭脂以爇；祀行道之神，而牡羊以將。燔焉而尸羞無不具也，烈焉而尸羞無不供也。所以然者，將以興來歲之祀于無窮，繼往歲之祀于不替也。后稷以農功而肇祀如此，後人寧不尊之以配天之祭乎？
于是我以菹醢而盛之于豆也，我以太羹而薦之于登也。馨
translation_en:
…Ji as the associate of Heaven in sacrifice, and therefore composed this poem. It says that Hou Ji devoted himself to sowing and reaping and rendered meritorious service to the people. Yao therefore enfeoffed him in the land of Youtai and charged him with presiding over sacrifices to Jiang Yuan. At that time, Hou Ji bestowed fine seeds upon the people. What seeds were these? There was not only black millet, called pi [?], but also pi with two kernels in a single husk; not only red liang millet, called mi [?], but also white liang millet, called qi. When these had been planted everywhere and had grown, the people harvested them and stacked them in the fields. When these had been sown everywhere and had ripened, the people shouldered them and carried them home. The purpose was to inaugurate the sacrifices in the ancestral temple and begin the offerings to the various spirits.
These were the sacrifices that Hou Ji performed. What did their observances entail? Some pounded and scooped out the fine grain [?]; others winnowed and rubbed it. As it was washed, it made a rustling sound; as it was steamed, vapor rose in billows. They consulted together, divined the day, and selected the officers [?]; they reflected upon the rites, purified themselves through abstinence, and made all preparations. To sacrifice to the ancestral tablets in the temple, they burned southernwood with fat; to sacrifice to the spirit of the road, they presented a ram. They roasted the meat, and every delicacy for the personator of the dead was made ready; they broiled it, and every delicacy for the personator was supplied. The purpose was to carry forward the sacrifices of coming years without end and continue those of past years without interruption. Since Hou Ji thus inaugurated the sacrifices through his achievements in agriculture, could his descendants fail to honor him with sacrifice as the associate of Heaven?
Thus we fill the stemmed dishes with pickled vegetables and meat paste, and present the unseasoned broth in the offering bowls. The fragrance…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
香之氣始芬然而升上帝之神已居然而饗此
何但芳臭之薦信得其時哉蓋自后稷以農功
而受封因稼穡而肇祀則庶無罪悔以至于今
矣然則天應之疾者有由然也豈徒以其物哉
抑觀此詩與思文均爲尊稷配天作也而詳畧
不同何耶蓋此爲序事宜詳不詳無以見其始
終彼爲獻詞宜簡不簡無以見其嚴肅讀詩者
不可不知
===
我將我享維羊維牛維天其右之
田宏
同考試官訓導黃批此題朱傳本明白作者
多蹈襲陳言令人厭觀一主朱傳措詞而說理著
僅見此篇
考試官教諭鄭批周王敬天之意發揮殆盡
考試官學正朱批善發周人祭祀明堂之意
奉物以祀天而冀天之降監此周王之大享於
punctuated:
香之氣始芬然而升，上帝之神已居然而饗。此何但芳臭之薦信得其時哉！蓋自后稷以農功而受封，因稼穡而肇祀，則庶無罪悔，以至于今矣。然則天應之疾者有由然也，豈徒以其物哉！抑觀此詩與《思文》均爲尊稷配天作也，而詳畧不同，何耶？蓋此爲序事宜詳，不詳無以見其始終；彼爲獻詞宜簡，不簡無以見其嚴肅。讀詩者不可不知。

「我將我享，維羊維牛，維天其右之。」
田宏

同考試官訓導黃批：「此題朱傳本明白，作者多蹈襲陳言，令人厭觀。一主朱傳，措詞而說理著，僅見此篇。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「周王敬天之意，發揮殆盡。」
考試官學正朱批：「善發周人祭祀明堂之意。」

奉物以祀天，而冀天之降監，此周王之大享於
translation_en:
…the fragrant aroma has only just begun to rise, yet the spirit of the Lord on High already serenely receives the offering. How could this mean merely that the fragrant offering was indeed presented at the proper time? Since Hou Ji received his fief for his achievements in agriculture and instituted sacrifices on the basis of his cultivation and harvesting, there has been, one may hope, neither fault nor cause for regret, down to the present. Thus Heaven has reason to respond so swiftly. Surely it is not merely because of the things offered!
Furthermore, this poem and “Solemn” (Si Wen) were both composed to honor Hou Ji by associating him with Heaven in sacrifice. Why, then, do they differ in fullness and brevity? This poem recounts events and should therefore be detailed: without detail, it could not reveal their beginning and end. The other presents words of offering and should therefore be concise: without concision, it could not convey its solemnity. Readers of the Poetry must understand this.

“I bring forward my offerings: sheep and oxen. May Heaven aid us.”
Tian Hong

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: “Zhu Xi’s commentary on this passage is clear enough, but most writers repeat stale expressions, making them tiresome to read. This is the only essay I have seen that takes Zhu Xi’s commentary as its sole guide while expressing its meaning in language that makes the underlying principles clear.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The Zhou king’s intention to revere Heaven is expounded almost exhaustively.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “It skillfully elucidates the intention behind the Zhou people’s sacrifices in the Hall of Enlightenment.”

To present offerings in sacrifice to Heaven, hoping that Heaven will descend to look upon them: this was the Zhou king’s great sacrifice at…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
明堂也蓋有其誠則有其神也周王奉祭而冀
天之降監其大享之誠何如哉此宗祀文王於
明堂以配上帝之樂歌吾想周王於季秋之月
行大享之禮而以父配帝意豈不曰我所奉於
明堂之上以享上帝者果何物耶少牢之羊可
以為俎實也則維羊之是奉于以盡宗祀之誠
焉我所薦於明堂之間以享上帝者又何物耶
大牢之牛可以為犧牲也則維牛之是薦于以
===
行大享之禮焉然維羊之奉特以將吾誠爾彼
皇皇后帝巍巍在上也庶其有感而在此羊之
右乎維牛之薦特以行吾禮爾彼浩浩昊天高
高在上也庶其俯降而在此牛之右乎曰其右
之者蓋不敢必也周人明堂之祭尊尊之意有
如是夫載觀思文之頌旣尊后稷以配天矣此
又尊文王以配帝何耶蓋萬物本乎天人本乎
祖故冬至祭天而以祖配之所以尊尊也萬物
punctuated: 明堂也。蓋有其誠，則有其神也。周王奉祭而冀天之降監，其大享之誠何如哉！此宗祀文王於明堂以配上帝之樂歌。吾想周王於季秋之月，行大享之禮，而以父配帝，意豈不曰：「我所奉於明堂之上以享上帝者，果何物耶？少牢之羊，可以為俎實也，則維羊之是奉，于以盡宗祀之誠焉。我所薦於明堂之間以享上帝者，又何物耶？大牢之牛，可以為犧牲也，則維牛之是薦，于以行大享之禮焉。然維羊之奉，特以將吾誠爾。彼皇皇后帝，巍巍在上也，庶其有感而在此羊之右乎！維牛之薦，特以行吾禮爾。彼浩浩昊天，高高在上也，庶其俯降而在此牛之右乎！」曰「其右之」者，蓋不敢必也。周人明堂之祭，尊尊之意有如是夫！載觀《思文》之頌，旣尊后稷以配天矣，此又尊文王以配帝，何耶？蓋萬物本乎天，人本乎祖，故冬至祭天而以祖配之，所以尊尊也。萬物
translation_en:
…in the Hall of Light. For where there is such sincerity, there is the presence of the spirit. The king of Zhou presents his sacrifice and hopes that Heaven will descend to look upon it: how profound is his sincerity in this great offering! This is the song for the ancestral sacrifice to King Wen in the Hall of Light, associating him with the Lord on High. I imagine that, in the last month of autumn, when the king of Zhou performed the rite of the great offering and associated his father with the Lord on High, his thought must have been: “What, indeed, do I present in the Hall of Light as an offering to the Lord on High? The sheep of the lesser animal offering can furnish the sacrificial stand; thus it is a sheep that I present, thereby fully expressing the sincerity of the ancestral sacrifice. And what else do I offer within the Hall of Light to the Lord on High? The ox of the greater animal offering can serve as a sacrificial victim; thus it is an ox that I offer, thereby performing the rite of the great offering. Yet presenting the sheep serves only to convey my sincerity. The august Sovereign Lord is majestically above: may he respond and be here at the right of this sheep! Offering the ox serves only to carry out my ritual observance. Vast Heaven is high above: may it descend and be here at the right of this ox!” The words “may he be at their right” show that the king does not dare presume upon this. Such was the intention to honor the exalted in the Zhou people's sacrifice in the Hall of Light!

Looking also at the hymn “The Cultured One” (Si wen), we see that Hou Ji was already honored by being associated with Heaven. Why, here, was King Wen also honored by being associated with the Lord on High? All things have their origin in Heaven, and human beings have their origin in their ancestors. Thus, at the winter solstice, sacrifice was offered to Heaven with the ancestor associated in the offering: this was the means of honoring the exalted. All things…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭鄭批措詞簡當
考試官學正朱批發明重民力之意可嘉
役民而非時害義者春秋固著其罪役民而雖
時且義者春秋亦重其事此可見民力不可以
輕而用之也何則爲民立君所以養之也養民
之道在愛其力今我魯隱當國七年夏也而有
中丘之城九年夏也又有郎邑之築是二城也
正農事之方殷勞民力於興作是使民非時矣
===
桓公懼齊鄭之襲紀而有祝丘之城莊公恐納
糾之見討亦有洙水之浚是二役也弗脩德以
禦患惟恃險以自防是使民害義矣夫使民不
時害義則民力不足生養不遂豈君國子民之
道哉故春秋必歷書以著其罪也若夫莊公城
諸防也乃龍見戒事之時宣公城平陽也於火
見致用之日之三城也當三務之始畢正百穀
之告成是使民得其時矣仲孫從晉定有成周
punctuated:
考試官敎諭鄭批：措詞簡當。

考試官學正朱批：發明重民力之意，可嘉。

役民而非時害義者，春秋固著其罪；役民而雖時且義者，春秋亦重其事。此可見民力不可以輕而用之也。何則？爲民立君，所以養之也；養民之道，在愛其力。今我魯隱當國七年夏也，而有中丘之城；九年夏也，又有郎邑之築。是二城也，正農事之方殷，勞民力於興作，是使民非時矣。桓公懼齊鄭之襲紀，而有祝丘之城；莊公恐納糾之見討，亦有洙水之浚。是二役也，弗脩德以禦患，惟恃險以自防，是使民害義矣。夫使民不時害義，則民力不足，生養不遂，豈君國子民之道哉？故春秋必歷書以著其罪也。若夫莊公城諸防也，乃龍見戒事之時；宣公城平陽也，於火見致用之日。之三城也，當三務之始畢，正百穀之告成，是使民得其時矣。仲孫從晉定有成周
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: The wording is concise and apt.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Its elucidation of the importance of conserving the people’s strength is commendable.

When rulers employ the people in labor at the wrong season and in violation of righteousness, the Spring and Autumn Annals certainly exposes their wrongdoing. Yet even when they employ the people at the proper season and in accordance with righteousness, the Annals still treats the undertaking as a weighty matter. This shows that the people’s strength must not be employed lightly. Why is this? A ruler is established for the people in order to sustain them; the way to sustain them lies in cherishing their strength. Now, in the summer of the seventh year of Duke Yin’s rule over our state of Lu, there was the walling of Zhongqiu; in the summer of his ninth year, there was again construction at the town of Lang. Both these wall-building projects took place precisely when agricultural work was at its busiest. To exhaust the people’s strength on construction was to employ them at the wrong season.

Duke Huan feared that Qi and Zheng would attack Ji, and so had Zhuqiu walled. Duke Zhuang feared a punitive attack for attempting to install Jiu, and likewise had the Zhu River dredged. In these two undertakings, they failed to cultivate virtue to ward off calamity, relying solely on defensive terrain to protect themselves. This was to employ the people in violation of righteousness. When the people are employed at the wrong season and in violation of righteousness, their strength is depleted and they cannot adequately sustain their lives. How could this be the proper way to rule a state and nurture its people as one’s children? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals invariably records these undertakings individually to expose the wrongdoing.

As for Duke Zhuang’s walling of Zhu and Fang, this occurred when the Dragon constellation appeared and preparations for work were ordered; Duke Xuan’s walling of Pingyang occurred when the Fire star appeared and implements were brought into use. These three wall-building projects [?] came just as the work of the three agricultural seasons was completed and the various grains had reached maturity. This was to employ the people at the proper season. Zhongsun followed Jin in settling the undertaking at Chengzhou [?] …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之城魯定命叔季有郈費之墮之三役也供臣
職以藩王室張公室以弱私家是使民合乎義
矣夫使民雖時且義豈能免營築力役之勞哉
故春秋亦備書以重其事也吁不時害義固爲
罪雖時且義而亦書非以見勞民爲重事矣乎
大抵民惟邦本本固邦寧故固國以保民爲本
人君能愛民力而民力足則生養遂敎化行風
俗美而邦本固矣使不能愛民而輕用民力於
===
守國之末務則邦本一搖雖有城池之固誰與
之守此春秋於用民力必書以爲重也噫人君
而知此義則知慎重於用民力矣
公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男曹
伯于葵丘諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕宋
公曹人邾人盟于曹南〔僖公十九年〕晉侯齊
師宋師秦師及楚人戰于城濮〔僖公二
十八年〕秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕楚子陳侯鄭
punctuated:
之城。魯定命叔季，有郈費之墮。之三役也，供臣職以藩王室，張公室以弱私家，是使民合乎義矣。夫使民雖時且義，豈能免營築力役之勞哉？故《春秋》亦備書以重其事也。吁！不時害義，固爲罪；雖時且義而亦書，非以見勞民爲重事矣乎？大抵民惟邦本，本固邦寧，故固國以保民爲本。人君能愛民力，而民力足，則生養遂，敎化行，風俗美，而邦本固矣。使不能愛民，而輕用民力於守國之末務，則邦本一搖，雖有城池之固，誰與之守？此《春秋》於用民力必書以爲重也。噫！人君而知此義，則知慎重於用民力矣。
公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。諸侯盟于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕宋公、曹人、邾人盟于曹南。〔僖公十九年〕晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮。〔僖公二十八年〕秦人伐晉。〔文公三年〕楚子、陳侯、鄭
translation_en:
…the construction of the walls. Duke Ding of Lu commanded the Shu and Ji clans, and the walls of Hou and Fei were demolished. These three undertakings fulfilled a subject’s duty by defending the royal house, and strengthened the ducal house by weakening the private clans: this was employing the people in accordance with righteousness. Yet even when the people are employed at the proper season and for a righteous purpose, how can they escape the toil of construction and labor service? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals also records these undertakings fully, treating them as weighty matters. Ah! Employing the people out of season and in violation of righteousness is certainly culpable; but even undertakings that are timely and righteous are recorded. Does this not show that imposing toil upon the people is a grave matter?
Broadly speaking, the people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is at peace. Thus securing the state must rest upon protecting the people. If a ruler can cherish the people’s strength, and their strength is sufficient, they can sustain their livelihoods and raise their families, moral instruction will take effect, customs will improve, and the state’s foundation will be firm. If he cannot cherish the people but heedlessly expends their strength on the secondary tasks of defending the state, then, once its foundation is shaken, who will join him in its defense, however strong its walls and moats? This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals invariably records the employment of the people’s strength, treating it as a weighty matter. Ah! A ruler who understands this principle will know to exercise care in employing the people’s strength.
The duke met with the chief minister, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the heir of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu.
