title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諸臣無以及其賢此可見五伯莫盛於齊桓而
諸臣皆有愧於宰孔也慨自黍離旣降雅頌不
作王室之不尊久矣咺賵仲子糾聘桓公王臣
之不賢甚矣所幸齊桓創伯廼心王室合諸侯
爲葵丘之會適宰孔有賜胙之行于時孔也嚴
恭寅畏宣加勞賜級之命桓也俯伏下拜盡天
威咫尺之恭已而宰孔言旋盟禮斯講申五命
之詞示一王之法束牲載書而不歃血桓公之
===
信義以著唯與之會而不與盟宰臣之名分以
尊桓之伯業於斯爲盛孔之奬伯亦與有功厥
後宋晉秦楚接踵而主伯於當時尹單劉子相
繼而下臨於伯國使能蹈芳躅而繼休績則桓
與孔豈得專美於前哉夫何曹南有盟而宋襄
之作舍無成城濮戰楚而晉文則陰謀取勝秦
穆之伐晉也濟河焚舟未免有逞忿之失楚莊
之盟辰陵也假義討罪不過濟貪利之私之數
punctuated: 諸臣無以及其賢。此可見五伯莫盛於齊桓，而諸臣皆有愧於宰孔也。慨自黍離旣降，雅頌不作，王室之不尊久矣。咺賵仲子，糾聘桓公，王臣之不賢甚矣。所幸齊桓創伯，廼心王室，合諸侯爲葵丘之會，適宰孔有賜胙之行。于時孔也嚴恭寅畏，宣加勞賜級之命；桓也俯伏下拜，盡天威咫尺之恭。已而宰孔言旋，盟禮斯講，申五命之詞，示一王之法，束牲載書而不歃血，桓公之信義以著。唯與之會而不與盟，宰臣之名分以尊。桓之伯業於斯爲盛，孔之奬伯亦與有功。厥後宋晉秦楚接踵而主伯於當時，尹單劉子相繼而下臨於伯國。使能蹈芳躅而繼休績，則桓與孔豈得專美於前哉？夫何曹南有盟，而宋襄之作舍無成；城濮戰楚，而晉文則陰謀取勝；秦穆之伐晉也，濟河焚舟，未免有逞忿之失；楚莊之盟辰陵也，假義討罪，不過濟貪利之私。之數
translation_en:
…the other ministers could not match his worth. This shows that none of the Five Hegemons surpassed Duke Huan of Qi in greatness, and that the other ministers all fell short of Zai Kong. Alas, ever since “The Millet Hangs Low” (Shu li) was relegated to a lower category and the Elegantiae and Hymns ceased to be composed, the royal house had long gone without due honor. Xuan presented funeral gifts for Zhongzi, and Jiu paid a diplomatic visit to Duke Huan: how grievously the royal ministers lacked virtue!

Fortunately, Duke Huan of Qi established his hegemony with his heart set upon the royal house. He assembled the feudal lords at Kuiqiu, just as Zai Kong arrived on a mission to bestow sacrificial meat. Kong, solemnly respectful and reverently cautious, proclaimed the king’s command conveying special commendation and granting a privilege of rank. Huan prostrated himself and bowed below the steps, showing the utmost reverence as though the royal majesty were close at hand. After Zai Kong set off homeward, the covenant ceremony proceeded. The five injunctions were reiterated, displaying the laws of the one true king. The sacrificial victim was bound and the covenant recorded, but no blood was smeared upon the lips. Thus Duke Huan’s trustworthiness and righteousness became manifest. By participating in the meeting but not in the covenant, the royal minister upheld the dignity proper to his status. Huan’s hegemonic achievement reached its height here, and Kong also earned merit through his support of the hegemon.

Thereafter, the rulers of Song, Jin, Qin, and Chu successively held the hegemony in their respective times, while the lords of Yin, Shan, and Liu came down in succession to the hegemonic states. Had they followed those worthy footsteps and continued those splendid achievements, how could Huan and Kong alone have enjoyed such distinction among their predecessors? Yet why was it that, when a covenant was concluded south of Cao, Duke Xiang of Song’s undertaking came to nothing [?]; that, in fighting Chu at Chengpu, Duke Wen of Jin secured victory through secret stratagems; that Duke Mu of Qin, when attacking Jin, crossed the river and burned his boats, thereby falling into the fault of indulging his anger; and that Duke Zhuang of Chu, in concluding the covenant at Chenling, invoked righteousness to punish wrongdoing merely to satisfy his private greed for advantage? These several [?]…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君者雖雄長於一時其於世道何補回視齊桓
之尊王室明五禁以一匡天下豈可同日語哉
伐鄭盟柯陵也而晉厲則瀆尹武單襄以講信
鷄澤謀外楚也而晉悼復扳單頃公以要言晉
昭因懼楚為平丘之會盟劉獻亦屈己以同事
於牲歃之數三者瀆尊卑之大分則於君命有
辱回視宰孔之獎伯主謹名分以表正天下豈
可一例觀哉故春秋備書則其優劣賢否自見
===
矣雖然齊桓固為五伯之盛然自葵丘之後伯
業漸衰何有王者不息之誠宰孔固為諸臣之
賢然前此阿順王命撫鄭從楚何有大臣格君
之道合而觀之則桓孔之功過得失不可掩矣
禮記
德盛而教尊五穀時熟然後賞之以樂
陸中行
同考試官訓導左批勤於治民則德盛應氏
punctuated:
君者，雖雄長於一時，其於世道何補？回視齊桓之尊王室，明五禁，以一匡天下，豈可同日語哉？伐鄭盟柯陵也，而晉厲則瀆尹武、單襄以講信；鷄澤謀外楚也，而晉悼復扳單頃公以要言；晉昭因懼楚，為平丘之會盟，劉獻亦屈己以同事於牲歃之數。三者瀆尊卑之大分，則於君命有辱。回視宰孔之獎伯主，謹名分以表正天下，豈可一例觀哉？故春秋備書，則其優劣賢否自見矣。雖然，齊桓固為五伯之盛，然自葵丘之後，伯業漸衰，何有王者不息之誠？宰孔固為諸臣之賢，然前此阿順王命，撫鄭從楚，何有大臣格君之道？合而觀之，則桓、孔之功過得失不可掩矣。
禮記
德盛而教尊，五穀時熟，然後賞之以樂。
陸中行
同考試官訓導左批：勤於治民，則德盛。應氏
translation_en:
…these rulers, though dominant in their own times, contributed what to the moral order of the world? Looking back at Duke Huan of Qi, who honored the royal house and made clear the five prohibitions, thereby setting all under Heaven right, how could they be spoken of in the same breath?
When Zheng was attacked and a covenant concluded at Keling, Duke Li of Jin affronted Duke Wu of Yin and Duke Xiang of Shan by involving them in pledges of good faith. When plans were made at Jize to exclude Chu, Duke Dao of Jin again drew Duke Qing of Shan into sworn undertakings. Duke Zhao of Jin, fearing Chu, convened the meeting and covenant at Pingqiu, and Duke Xian of Liu likewise abased himself by joining those who participated in the animal sacrifice and blood oath. These three rulers violated the fundamental distinction between superior and inferior, thereby dishonoring the king’s commission. Looking back at Minister Kong (Zai Kong), who supported the hegemon and scrupulously upheld distinctions of status to set a correct example for all under Heaven, how could they be judged alike? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals records these matters fully, and their relative merits and failings, worthiness and unworthiness, become apparent of themselves.
Nevertheless, although Duke Huan of Qi was indeed the most illustrious of the Five Hegemons, his hegemonic enterprise gradually declined after Kuiqiu. Where was the unceasing sincerity of a true king? Although Minister Kong was indeed a worthy man among the ministers, he had previously complied obsequiously with the king’s commands, pacifying Zheng and following Chu. Where was the great minister’s way of correcting his ruler? Considered together, the achievements and faults, successes and failures, of Huan and Kong cannot be concealed.
Book of Rites
“When virtue flourishes and moral instruction is honored, and the five grains ripen in season, only then are they rewarded with music.”
Lu Zhongxing
Comment by Associate Examiner Zuo, Assistant Instructor: “Diligence in governing the people brings flourishing virtue. Master Ying…”

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之註作者昧此臆說紛紛惟此篇認理詳明措詞典
雅其禮經之翹楚者乎
考試官教諭鄭批說出天子以樂賞諸侯之意
宛然在目
考試官學正朱批詞簡意足禮經無出其右者
人臣德懋而有其驗人君必錫以章德之具也
夫樂所以章德也人臣德懋而有其驗如此人
君得不賞之以樂哉記樂記者謂夫昔天子之
===
為樂將以賞諸侯之有德者也彼為之諸侯者
勤於教民而勞來匡直之匪懈勤於養民而勸
課巡行之不怠非有德而勤於為治者不能也
然勤於教民而教道未尊未見其德之盛也必
若父子有親君臣有義與夫夫婦長幼朋友之
教民皆承聽而無敢慢易則德之盛於此乎可
驗勤於養民而五穀未熟亦未見其德之盛也
必若麥熟於夏稻熟於秋與夫若黍若稷若菽
punctuated:
之註，作者昧此，臆說紛紛。惟此篇認理詳明，措詞典雅，其禮經之翹楚者乎！

考試官教諭鄭批：說出天子以樂賞諸侯之意，宛然在目。

考試官學正朱批：詞簡意足，禮經無出其右者。

人臣德懋而有其驗，人君必錫以章德之具也。

夫樂所以章德也。人臣德懋而有其驗如此，人君得不賞之以樂哉？記《樂記》者謂：夫昔天子之為樂，將以賞諸侯之有德者也。彼為之諸侯者，勤於教民，而勞來匡直之匪懈；勤於養民，而勸課巡行之不怠，非有德而勤於為治者不能也。然勤於教民而教道未尊，未見其德之盛也。必若父子有親，君臣有義，與夫夫婦、長幼、朋友之教，民皆承聽而無敢慢易，則德之盛於此乎可驗。勤於養民而五穀未熟，亦未見其德之盛也。必若麥熟於夏，稻熟於秋，與夫若黍、若稷、若菽
translation_en:
…in Master Ying’s commentary. Writers fail to understand this, and speculative explanations abound. This essay alone explains the principles clearly and thoroughly, with refined and elegant diction. Is it not an outstanding essay on the Classic of Rites!

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: The meaning of the Son of Heaven’s rewarding the feudal lords with music is expressed so vividly that it seems present before our eyes.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, School Instructor: Concise in wording and complete in meaning; no essay on the Classic of Rites surpasses it.

When a minister’s virtue is abundant and has demonstrable effects, his ruler will assuredly bestow upon him the means to display that virtue.

Music is the means by which virtue is displayed. When a minister’s virtue is abundant and has such demonstrable effects, how could his ruler fail to reward him with music? The author of the Record of Music says: In ancient times, the Son of Heaven instituted music in order to reward virtuous feudal lords. Those who served as feudal lords diligently taught the people, tirelessly encouraging, attracting, correcting, and guiding them. They diligently provided for the people’s livelihood, untiringly encouraging and supervising their work and making tours of inspection. Only those possessed of virtue and diligent in governing could accomplish this. Yet if they diligently taught the people but the way of instruction was not yet honored, the fullness of their virtue would not yet be manifest. There must be affection between fathers and sons and righteousness between rulers and ministers; and these teachings, together with those governing husbands and wives, elders and juniors, and friends, must all be accepted and obeyed by the people, with none daring to treat them lightly. Then the fullness of their virtue can be verified in this. If they diligently provided for the people’s livelihood but the five grains had not ripened, the fullness of their virtue would likewise not yet be manifest. There must be wheat ripening in summer and rice ripening in autumn, together with such crops as glutinous millet, non-glutinous millet, and beans…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之類各以時熟而無或愆期則德之盛於此乎
可徵天子於此得不賞樂以章其德哉盖樂有
羽旄夔所制也于焉錫之以羽旄以為文舞之
用樂有干戚夔所制也于焉錫之以干戚以充
武舞之列是則樂舞一舉而侯德以著綴兆一
陳而侯德以章先王賞樂於諸侯豈苟焉而已
哉抑稽昔者舜作五絃之琴以歌南風夔始制
樂以賞諸侯其賞之也一惟視其德之厚薄未
===
嘗至於濫賞下文所謂其治民勞者其舞行綴
遠其治民逸者其舞行綴短槩可見矣噫制樂
不以已而賞樂因其德此先王之世所以樂必
盡善盡美而觀樂則可以知其德也後世燕奏
肆夏庭舞八佾殆不知此
三代之王也必先其令聞
陸中行
同考試官訓導左批塲中作此題者多不知
punctuated:
之類，各以時熟而無或愆期，則德之盛於此乎可徵。天子於此得不賞樂以章其德哉？盖樂有羽旄，夔所制也，于焉錫之以羽旄，以為文舞之用；樂有干戚，夔所制也，于焉錫之以干戚，以充武舞之列。是則樂舞一舉，而侯德以著；綴兆一陳，而侯德以章。先王賞樂於諸侯，豈苟焉而已哉？抑稽昔者，舜作五絃之琴以歌南風，夔始制樂以賞諸侯。其賞之也，一惟視其德之厚薄，未嘗至於濫賞。下文所謂「其治民勞者，其舞行綴遠；其治民逸者，其舞行綴短」，槩可見矣。噫！制樂不以已，而賞樂因其德，此先王之世所以樂必盡善盡美，而觀樂則可以知其德也。後世燕奏肆夏，庭舞八佾，殆不知此。
三代之王也，必先其令聞。
陸中行
同考試官訓導左批：塲中作此題者，多不知
translation_en:
…and other such crops all ripen in their proper seasons, none failing to mature on time: in this the fullness of their virtue can be verified. Could the Son of Heaven then fail to reward them with music to make their virtue manifest? Music has its feather and yak-tail standards, instituted by Kui; these are bestowed upon them for use in civil dances. Music has its shields and axes, instituted by Kui; these are bestowed upon them to furnish the ranks of martial dances. Thus, once the music and dance are performed, the feudal lord’s virtue is revealed; once the positions of the dancers are laid out, his virtue is made manifest. Surely the former kings did not bestow music upon the feudal lords casually!
Furthermore, consider antiquity: Shun made a five-stringed zither to sing “South Wind,” and Kui first instituted music to reward the feudal lords. In conferring these rewards, they considered solely the degree of the recipients’ virtue and never bestowed them indiscriminately. This can broadly be seen in the passage below: “For those who labored in governing the people, the rows of dancers were spaced far apart; for those who governed the people with ease, the rows of dancers were spaced close together.” Ah! Music was instituted without regard to oneself, and bestowed according to the recipient’s virtue. This is why, in the age of the former kings, music was necessarily perfect in goodness and beauty, and by observing the music one could know the recipient’s virtue. In later ages, those who performed “Si Xia” at banquets and staged dances in eight rows in their courtyards seem not to have understood this.
“When the founders of the Three Dynasties became kings, their fine reputation necessarily preceded them.”
Lu Zhongxing
Comment by Associate Examiner Zuo, Assistant Instructor: “Among those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic, many did not understand…”

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
旨此篇說出三王無私之德明白簡切非熟於禮不能
也寘諸上第允愜輿情
考試官教諭鄭批文從理順
考試官學正朱批禮經義無有能如此作者
論歷代受命而興由先世著無私之譽也夫三
代之王同一無私而已今聖人又原其先世之
令聞豈無意哉昔聖人因子夏問三王之德參
於天地而告之及此意豈不謂塗山啓會萬國
===
歸心此大禹之王於夏也帝命下臨九圍是式
此成湯之王於商也文王以文治而三分有二
武王以武功而四海永清非文武之王於周乎
三代之王如此夫豈無自而然哉誠以大禹受
命而興非但禹之一身有是無私之德而天遂
命之也盖未王之先有顓頊為之祖頊嘗法施
於民其積德之深已有無私之令聞慰服於當
時之人心矣夏之有天下實基於此成湯受命
punctuated:
旨。此篇說出三王無私之德，明白簡切，非熟於禮不能也。寘諸上第，允愜輿情。

考試官教諭鄭批：文從理順。

考試官學正朱批：禮經義無有能如此作者。

論歷代受命而興，由先世著無私之譽也。夫三代之王，同一無私而已。今聖人又原其先世之令聞，豈無意哉？昔聖人因子夏問三王之德參於天地，而告之及此，意豈不謂塗山啓會，萬國歸心，此大禹之王於夏也；帝命下臨，九圍是式，此成湯之王於商也；文王以文治而三分有二，武王以武功而四海永清，非文武之王於周乎？三代之王如此，夫豈無自而然哉？誠以大禹受命而興，非但禹之一身有是無私之德，而天遂命之也。盖未王之先，有顓頊為之祖，頊嘗法施於民，其積德之深，已有無私之令聞，慰服於當時之人心矣。夏之有天下，實基於此。成湯受命
translation_en:
…the purport. This essay explains the selfless virtue of the kings of the Three Dynasties clearly, concisely, and aptly. Only someone thoroughly versed in the rites could accomplish this. Placing it among the highest-ranked essays truly accords with the general judgment.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: The writing flows naturally, and the reasoning is coherent.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, School Instructor: Among essays interpreting the Classic of Rites, none can match this.

I submit that the rulers of successive dynasties received the Mandate and rose to power because their forebears had established a reputation for selflessness. The kings of the Three Dynasties shared one quality: selflessness, and nothing more. Now the Sage further traces this back to the good reputation of their forebears. Surely he had a purpose in doing so? Formerly, when Zixia asked how the virtue of the kings of the Three Dynasties ranked alongside Heaven and Earth, the Sage's reply extended to this point. Did he not mean that when an assembly was convened at Tushan and the myriad states gave their allegiance, this was how Yu the Great became king of Xia; that when the Lord on High's Mandate descended and the nine regions took him as their model, this was how Cheng Tang became king of Shang; and that when King Wen, through civil governance, possessed two-thirds of the realm, and King Wu, through martial achievement, brought lasting peace within the Four Seas, this was how Wen and Wu became kings of Zhou? Such was the kingship of the Three Dynasties. Could it have come about without a source?

Indeed, Yu the Great received the Mandate and rose to power not merely because Yu himself possessed this selfless virtue and Heaven therefore bestowed its Mandate upon him. Before he became king, he had Zhuanxu as his ancestor. Zhuanxu had bestowed exemplary institutions upon the people. Through his profound accumulation of virtue, he had already earned a fine reputation for selflessness, reassuring and winning over the hearts of the people of his time. Xia's possession of All under Heaven was truly founded upon this. Cheng Tang received the Mandate…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而興非徒湯之一身有是無私之德而帝遂命
之也盖未王之先有契爲之始祖契嘗敬敷五
敎其積德之厚已有無私之令聞固結於當時
之人心矣商之有天下實肇于茲若夫文武之
興王於周人皆知其有無私之德故天眷之也
殊不知周之先世有后稷敎民稼穡有王季其
勤王家其積功累仁有素矣周之有天下不先
有無私之令聞著于未王之先乎聖人論三代
===
之王而必原其祖宗積德之所自此可見王業
之興其積累非一日矣孰敢以私議之哉抑考
閒居一篇皆聖人荅子夏之問始論爲民父母
之道則在於致五至而行三無終論參於天地
之德則在於奉三無私而先令聞盖有爲民父
母之道然後可以行三王之德洪範曰天子作
民父母以爲天下王其序有如是夫
論
punctuated:
而興，非徒湯之一身有是無私之德，而帝遂命之也。盖未王之先，有契爲之始祖，契嘗敬敷五敎，其積德之厚，已有無私之令聞固結於當時之人心矣。商之有天下，實肇于茲。若夫文武之興王於周，人皆知其有無私之德，故天眷之也。殊不知周之先世，有后稷敎民稼穡，有王季其勤王家，其積功累仁有素矣。周之有天下，不先有無私之令聞著于未王之先乎？聖人論三代之王，而必原其祖宗積德之所自，此可見王業之興，其積累非一日矣，孰敢以私議之哉？抑考《閒居》一篇，皆聖人荅子夏之問。始論爲民父母之道，則在於致五至而行三無；終論參於天地之德，則在於奉三無私而先令聞。盖有爲民父母之道，然後可以行三王之德。《洪範》曰：「天子作民父母，以爲天下王。」其序有如是夫！

論
translation_en:
…and rose to power. It was not simply that Tang himself possessed this virtue of impartiality and the Lord on High therefore bestowed the mandate upon him. Before his accession to kingship, there had been Xie 契, the founding ancestor of his line. Xie had reverently disseminated the five teachings, and through his abundant accumulation of virtue, his fine reputation for impartiality had already become firmly rooted in the hearts of the people of his time. Shang’s possession of all under Heaven truly began here. As for Wen and Wu rising to kingship in Zhou, everyone knows that Heaven favored them because they possessed the virtue of impartiality. Yet people fail to recognize that among Zhou’s forebears were Hou Ji, who taught the people to sow and reap, and Wang Ji, who labored diligently for the royal house. Their accumulation of meritorious deeds and benevolence was long established. Before Zhou possessed all under Heaven, had not a fine reputation for impartiality already become manifest, even before its rulers became kings? When the Sage discusses the kingship of the Three Dynasties, he invariably traces it to the virtue accumulated by their ancestors. From this we can see that the rise of royal dominion rests on an accumulation extending beyond a single day. Who would dare attribute it to partiality?

Moreover, if we examine the chapter “Living at Leisure” (Xianju), it consists entirely of the Sage’s answers to Zixia’s questions. At the outset, it discusses the way to become father and mother to the people: this lies in bringing the five attainments to fulfillment and practicing the three things without outward form. At the end, it discusses matching the virtue of Heaven and Earth: this lies in honoring the three forms of impartiality and first establishing a fine reputation. Only after possessing the way to become father and mother to the people can one practice the virtue of the Three Kings. The “Great Plan” (Hongfan) says: “The Son of Heaven becomes father and mother to the people, thereby becoming king of all under Heaven.” Such indeed is the sequence!

Discourse

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝王之治一本於道
謝慶
同考試官訓導湯批有發揮有指歸論之優者
考試官教諭鄭批舂容大篇能闡明帝王之道
者此作見之
考試官學正朱批詞富而理明當是作家用魁多
士何忝
論曰帝王之致治也豈有他哉亦曰道而
===
已蓋道乃為治之本也治而本於道則近
而一家家以之而齊遠而一國國以之而
治極其遠而天下天下以之而平矣苟為
不然則徒操為治之柄而失為治之本欲
家國天下之治平也不其難乎愚嘗伏讀
太宗文皇帝御製性理大全序文有曰帝王之
治一本於道大哉
皇言乎一哉
punctuated:
帝王之治一本於道
謝慶
同考試官訓導湯批：有發揮，有指歸，論之優者。
考試官教諭鄭批：舂容大篇，能闡明帝王之道者，此作見之。
考試官學正朱批：詞富而理明，當是作家，用魁多士，何忝？
論曰：帝王之致治也，豈有他哉？亦曰道而已。蓋道乃為治之本也。治而本於道，則近而一家，家以之而齊；遠而一國，國以之而治；極其遠而天下，天下以之而平矣。苟為不然，則徒操為治之柄，而失為治之本，欲家國天下之治平也，不其難乎？愚嘗伏讀太宗文皇帝御製《性理大全》序文，有曰：「帝王之治，一本於道。」大哉，皇言乎！一哉
translation_en:
The Government of Emperors and Kings Is Rooted Entirely in the Way
Xie Qing

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Assistant Instructor: There is elaboration, and there is a clear point toward which the argument leads. This is an excellent discourse.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: An expansive [?] composition of considerable scope. Here is a work that elucidates the Way of emperors and kings.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, School Instructor: Rich in expression and clear in principle: this must be an accomplished writer. What cause for embarrassment could there be in placing him first among the candidates?

The discourse states: In bringing about good government, do emperors and kings rely on anything else? It is simply the Way. The Way is the foundation of government. When government is rooted in the Way, at the nearest level, that of a household, the household is brought into order through it; farther afield, at the level of a state, the state is well governed through it; and at the farthest extent, encompassing all under Heaven, all under Heaven is brought to peace through it. If this is not so, one merely holds the reins of government while losing its foundation. Would it not then be difficult to bring order and peace to the household, the state, and all under Heaven?

I have humbly and reverently read Emperor Taizong Wen’s imperially composed preface to the Complete Compendium of Human Nature and Principle (Xingli daquan), which says: “The government of emperors and kings is rooted entirely in the Way.” How great are these imperial words! How single in purpose …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇心乎其真知帝王爲治之本乎且帝王之生
豈偶然哉膺上天付託之重任斯民君師
之責九重之上萬化之攸繫焉一日之間
萬幾之紛至焉禮樂刑政於此而脩舉井
田學校於此而制立民吾同胞而民之衆
也由我以字育物吾同與而物之多也由
我以生遂天地之財成本於我化育之參
賛本於我九夷八蠻之勞來而撫綏也本
===
於我所係爲甚重也所關爲甚大也將欲
治之以智耶智有窮而天下之大無窮智
豈爲治之本乎抑欲治之以力耶力有限
而天下之大也無限力豈爲治之本乎若
此者舉不足以言治然則帝王之致治也
非是道而何歟夫所謂道者原於天而具
於人具於人而根於心非高遠而難行也
非驚世而駭俗也求之人倫日用常行之
punctuated: 皇心乎！其真知帝王爲治之本乎！且帝王之生，豈偶然哉？膺上天付託之重，任斯民君師之責，九重之上，萬化之攸繫焉；一日之間，萬幾之紛至焉。禮樂刑政，於此而脩舉；井田學校，於此而制立。民吾同胞，而民之衆也，由我以字育；物吾同與，而物之多也，由我以生遂。天地之財成，本於我；化育之參賛，本於我；九夷八蠻之勞來而撫綏也，本於我。所係爲甚重也，所關爲甚大也。將欲治之以智耶？智有窮，而天下之大無窮，智豈爲治之本乎？抑欲治之以力耶？力有限，而天下之大也無限，力豈爲治之本乎？若此者，舉不足以言治。然則帝王之致治也，非是道而何歟？夫所謂道者，原於天而具於人，具於人而根於心，非高遠而難行也，非驚世而駭俗也。求之人倫日用常行之
translation_en:
…the imperial mind! Surely he truly understood the foundation upon which emperors and kings establish good government! Moreover, could the birth of an emperor or king be a matter of chance? He bears the weighty trust conferred by Heaven above and assumes responsibility as ruler and teacher of the people. High within the ninefold palace, he is the one upon whom all transformations depend; within a single day, myriad affairs requiring his judgment crowd upon him. Through him, rites, music, punishments, and administration are cultivated and put into effect; through him, the well-field system and schools are instituted. The people are my siblings, and their multitudes depend upon me for nurture. All things are my companions, and their vast numbers depend upon me to live and flourish. Ordering and completing the work of Heaven and Earth rests upon me; participating in and assisting their transforming and nourishing processes rests upon me; comforting, drawing near, pacifying, and securing the Nine Yi and Eight Man peoples rests upon me. What depends upon him is exceedingly weighty; what is involved is exceedingly great.

Would he govern through cleverness? Cleverness is finite, whereas the vastness of all under Heaven is infinite. How could cleverness be the foundation of government? Or would he govern through force? Force has limits, whereas the vastness of all under Heaven has none. How could force be the foundation of government? Such means are altogether inadequate even to speak of governing. If so, by what can emperors and kings bring about good government, if not this Way? What is called the Way originates in Heaven and is inherent in human beings; inherent in human beings, it is rooted in the heart. It is neither lofty and remote, difficult to practice, nor something that astonishes the world and shocks conventional sensibilities. Seek it amid human relationships and the ordinary practices of daily life…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
間則可見矣是故親也義也父子君臣之
道也親義之道行於上殆見人同此心而
天下之爲父子君臣者必是則是效同一
有親而有義矣別也序也信也夫婦長幼
朋友之道也序別信之道篤於上殆見人
同此理而天下之爲夫婦長幼朋友者必
是矜是式同一有別有序而有信矣道乃
天之經也天經正則萬化以之而行道乃
===
地之義也地義立則萬變以之而出由是
以制禮作樂則大禮與天地同節大樂與
天地同和禮樂其有不興乎由是以賞善
罰惡則賞一人而千萬人說罰一人而千
萬人懼刑罰其有不中乎制田里以養民
而民生之厚是道有以厚之也立學校以
教民而民性之復是道有以復之也施於
政而達於事者莫非是道之發越篤於近
punctuated: 間，則可見矣。是故親也、義也，父子君臣之道也。親義之道行於上，殆見人同此心，而天下之爲父子君臣者必是則是效，同一有親而有義矣。別也、序也、信也，夫婦長幼朋友之道也。序別信之道篤於上，殆見人同此理，而天下之爲夫婦長幼朋友者必是矜是式，同一有別有序而有信矣。道乃天之經也，天經正則萬化以之而行；道乃地之義也，地義立則萬變以之而出。由是以制禮作樂，則大禮與天地同節，大樂與天地同和，禮樂其有不興乎？由是以賞善罰惡，則賞一人而千萬人說，罰一人而千萬人懼，刑罰其有不中乎？制田里以養民，而民生之厚，是道有以厚之也；立學校以教民，而民性之復，是道有以復之也。施於政而達於事者，莫非是道之發越；篤於近
translation_en:
…amid these, it can be discerned. Thus, affection and righteousness are the Way governing fathers and sons, rulers and subjects. When the Way of affection and righteousness is practiced by those above, we may expect to see that all people share this same heart: throughout the realm, fathers and sons, rulers and subjects will surely take this as their standard and emulate it, alike possessing affection and righteousness. Distinction, precedence, and trustworthiness are the Way governing husbands and wives, elders and juniors, and friends. When precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness are firmly upheld by those above, we may expect to see that all people share this same principle: throughout the realm, husbands and wives, elders and juniors, and friends will surely take this as their model and pattern, alike observing distinction, precedence, and trustworthiness.

The Way is Heaven’s constant norm. When Heaven’s constant norm is set right, the myriad transformations proceed through it. The Way is Earth’s right order. When Earth’s right order is established, the myriad changes arise through it. If rites are instituted and music created on this basis, the great rites share the measured order of Heaven and Earth, and great music shares their harmony. How could rites and music fail to flourish? If good is rewarded and evil punished on this basis, rewarding one person will gladden millions, and punishing one person will make millions fearful. How could punishments fail to be appropriate? When fields and settlements are regulated to nourish the people and their livelihood becomes abundant, it is this Way that makes it abundant. When schools are established to instruct the people and their innate nature is restored, it is this Way that restores it. Whatever is applied in government and carried through in affairs is an expression of this Way; what is firmly upheld among those nearby…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而舉於遠者莫非是道之流通所以財成
天地者本於此所以叅贊化育者本於此
所以撫九夷而綏八蠻者本於此是則帝
王之治天下其所以致雍熈悠久之盛者
誠不外於此道矣區區之知力烏可與道
同日而語哉雖然此道也聖人未生具在
天地聖人既生具在聖人聖人既往具在
六經六經也者斯道之攸寓也六經之教
===
明於天下斯道之明於天下也其日之中
天乎六經之教行於萬世斯道之行於萬
世也其水之行地乎帝王之生有先後道
不以先後而或殊世運之興有古今道不
以古今而或間千載之下遐陬僻壤疆域
雖不同而同此父子親君臣義者誰之功
斯道之功也百世之遠深山窮谷地勢雖
不同而同此夫婦別長幼序朋友信者誰
punctuated: 而舉於遠者，莫非是道之流通。所以財成天地者本於此，所以叅贊化育者本於此，所以撫九夷而綏八蠻者本於此。是則帝王之治天下，其所以致雍熈悠久之盛者，誠不外於此道矣。區區之知力，烏可與道同日而語哉！雖然，此道也，聖人未生，具在天地；聖人既生，具在聖人；聖人既往，具在六經。六經也者，斯道之攸寓也。六經之教明於天下，斯道之明於天下也，其日之中天乎！六經之教行於萬世，斯道之行於萬世也，其水之行地乎！帝王之生有先後，道不以先後而或殊；世運之興有古今，道不以古今而或間。千載之下，遐陬僻壤，疆域雖不同，而同此父子親、君臣義者，誰之功？斯道之功也。百世之遠，深山窮谷，地勢雖不同，而同此夫婦別、長幼序、朋友信者，誰
translation_en:
…and what is extended to those far away is invariably the circulation of this Way. It is the foundation for ordering and completing the work of Heaven and Earth, for assisting their transforming and nurturing activity, and for pacifying the Nine Yi and bringing tranquillity to the Eight Man. Thus, when emperors and kings govern All under Heaven, the means by which they achieve enduring harmony and prosperity truly lie nowhere outside this Way. How could mere intelligence and strength be spoken of in the same breath as the Way!

Nevertheless, before the sages were born, this Way was fully present in Heaven and Earth; once the sages were born, it was fully present in the sages; after the sages had passed away, it was fully present in the Six Classics. The Six Classics are where this Way resides. When the teaching of the Six Classics shines throughout All under Heaven, this is the Way shining throughout All under Heaven—is it not like the sun at the zenith! When the teaching of the Six Classics is practiced through ten thousand generations, this is the Way being practiced through ten thousand generations—is it not like water flowing over the earth! Emperors and kings are born at different times, yet the Way does not differ on account of their coming earlier or later. The fortunes of the world rise in both ancient and present times, yet the Way is not interrupted by the passage from antiquity to the present.

A thousand years later, in remote corners and outlying lands, although territories differ, affection between father and son and righteousness between ruler and minister remain the same: whose achievement is this? It is the achievement of this Way. A hundred generations hence, in deep mountains and remote valleys, although the terrain differs, distinction between husband and wife, precedence between older and younger, and trustworthiness between friends remain the same: whose…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之力斯道之力也由是觀之帝王之有天
下固不外是道以求治亦豈外六經以求
道歟稽之於古伏羲神農黃帝之世渾渾
然噩噩然道之寓於治也無迹而可見自
是而後堯之親睦九族舜之慎徽五典非
二帝之治一本於道乎禹之祗台德先湯
之肇脩人紀文王之緝熈敬止武王之皇
建有極非三王之治一本於道乎下及漢
===
唐之君或忽之而不行或行之而不純是
以或治或否或久或近率不能如古昔之
盛而人不得蒙至治之澤者夫豈無其故
道之不明不行故也三皇遠矣二帝三王
往矣秦漢以下諸君不足言矣洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝受天景命奄有萬方以身而體道
以道而致治
punctuated:
之力？斯道之力也。由是觀之，帝王之有天下，固不外是道以求治，亦豈外六經以求道歟？稽之於古，伏羲、神農、黃帝之世，渾渾然，噩噩然，道之寓於治也，無迹而可見。自是而後，堯之親睦九族，舜之慎徽五典，非二帝之治一本於道乎？禹之祗台德先，湯之肇脩人紀，文王之緝熈敬止，武王之皇建有極，非三王之治一本於道乎？下及漢唐之君，或忽之而不行，或行之而不純，是以或治或否，或久或近，率不能如古昔之盛，而人不得蒙至治之澤者，夫豈無其故？道之不明不行故也。
三皇遠矣，二帝三王往矣，秦漢以下諸君不足言矣。洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝，受天景命，奄有萬方，以身而體道，以道而致治
translation_en:
…whose power brought this about? It is the power of this Way. Viewed in this light, when emperors and kings possess all under Heaven, they surely do not seek orderly government outside this Way; how, then, could they seek the Way outside the Six Classics? Examining antiquity, in the ages of Fuxi, Shennong, and Huangdi, all was simple and uncontrived: the Way was embodied in government without any visible trace. Thereafter, Yao brought the nine degrees of kinship into affectionate harmony, and Shun carefully promoted the five moral teachings. Was not the government of the Two Emperors rooted entirely in the Way? Yu reverently gave precedence to virtue; Tang began to cultivate the norms of human relationships; King Wen continued to illuminate his virtue, abiding in reverence; and King Wu grandly established the supreme standard. Was not the government of the Three Kings rooted entirely in the Way? Coming down to the rulers of Han and Tang, some neglected it and did not put it into practice, while others practiced it without purity. Consequently, their rule was sometimes orderly and sometimes not, and lasted sometimes long and sometimes only briefly. Generally, they could not equal the flourishing rule of antiquity, and the people could not enjoy the blessings of perfect government. Could this have been without a cause? It was because the Way was neither made clear nor put into practice.
The Three Sovereigns are distant indeed; the Two Emperors and Three Kings have passed away. The rulers from Qin and Han onward are scarcely worth discussing. We reverently reflect that our dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s great mandate and possessed all the myriad regions. In his own person he embodied the Way, and through the Way he brought about orderly government…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承孜孜圖治闡明六經之教昭示五倫
之道百二十餘年
皇風清穆治化休明足以肩二帝超三王而
衍億萬年無疆之
盛治非區區漢唐所可及也然則帝王之治
一本於道正在
今日愚何幸躬逢其
盛
===
表
擬宋以唐介參知政事謝表〔熙寧元年〕
張紹齡
同考試官訓導黃批〔表麗則〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔表豐贍〕
考試官學正朱批〔表得體〕
伏以
金鼎調元絲綸密勿之地
punctuated:
列聖相承，孜孜圖治，闡明六經之教，昭示五倫之道。百二十餘年，皇風清穆，治化休明，足以肩二帝、超三王，而衍億萬年無疆之盛治，非區區漢唐所可及也。然則帝王之治一本於道，正在今日。愚何幸躬逢其盛！

表
擬宋以唐介參知政事謝表〔熙寧元年〕
張紹齡
同考試官訓導黃批〔表麗則〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔表豐贍〕
考試官學正朱批〔表得體〕

伏以：金鼎調元，絲綸密勿之地，
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors have inherited the throne, working tirelessly for good government, elucidating the teachings of the Six Classics and clearly proclaiming the Way of the Five Human Relationships. For more than 120 years, imperial influence has been pure and harmonious, and government and moral transformation admirable and enlightened. These achievements suffice to equal the Two Emperors and surpass the Three Kings, extending boundless flourishing rule through countless millions of years. The comparatively insignificant Han and Tang dynasties could never match this. Thus, rule by emperors and kings rooted wholly in the Way is realized precisely in our own day. How fortunate I, an ignorant man, am to witness such flourishing in person!

Memorial
Draft memorial of thanks on Tang Jie’s appointment as Vice Grand Councilor under the Song dynasty [First year of Xining, 1068].
By Zhang Shaoling.
Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: [The memorial is elegant and accords with the rules.]
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: [The memorial is rich and ample.]
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: [The memorial observes the appropriate form.]

I humbly submit: to harmonize the primordial forces in the golden tripod—the office where one diligently attends to imperial commands …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
玉扆賛化鈞衡崇峻之階詎意凡庸遽蒙抜
擢端拜
白麻之寵與參紫府之班
恩命自天汗容無地兹蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
道同坤厚
德配乾剛於昭不顯之誠用建維皇之極恭
己克勤而克儉事親純孝而純仁法
===
祖敬天誠不世出之主求賢圖治真大有為之
君俊乂滿
朝盡傾心以襄
大化旄倪塞道咸拭目以覩
太平史不絕書人皆滿望用人如用藥不遺
馬渤牛溲取士若取材肯棄竹頭木屑臣
介生逢
盛世名厠賢科昔在
punctuated: 玉扆賛化，鈞衡崇峻之階，詎意凡庸，遽蒙抜擢，端拜白麻之寵，與參紫府之班。恩命自天，汗容無地。兹蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，道同坤厚，德配乾剛，於昭不顯之誠，用建維皇之極。恭己克勤而克儉，事親純孝而純仁，法祖敬天，誠不世出之主；求賢圖治，真大有為之君。俊乂滿朝，盡傾心以襄大化；旄倪塞道，咸拭目以覩太平。史不絕書，人皆滿望。用人如用藥，不遺馬渤牛溲；取士若取材，肯棄竹頭木屑？臣介生逢盛世，名厠賢科，昔在
translation_en:
… assisting the sovereign’s transforming influence before the jade screen, occupying the exalted rank of those who hold the balance of government. How could I, so ordinary and mediocre, have imagined that I would suddenly receive such advancement, solemnly accepting the favor of an appointment proclaimed on white hemp paper and joining the ranks of the imperial council? This gracious command descends from Heaven; sweating with embarrassment, I have nowhere to hide.

This is because I have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇 [?], whose Way shares the capaciousness of Earth and whose virtue matches the strength of Heaven. Through sincerity—glorious even when unseen—you establish the sovereign’s supreme standard. Reverently ordering your own conduct, you practice diligence and frugality; in serving your parents, you are wholly filial and humane. Emulating your ancestors and revering Heaven, you are truly a ruler seldom seen in any age; seeking worthy men and striving for good government, you are indeed a sovereign capable of great achievements. Outstanding men fill the court, all devoting their hearts to assisting your great transforming work; old people and children throng the roads, all clearing their eyes to behold the Great Peace. Historians record your deeds without cease, and everyone’s hopes are fulfilled. You employ men as one employs medicines, overlooking neither puffballs nor ox urine; you select scholars as one selects useful materials—would you discard even bamboo ends and wood shavings?

Your servant Jie was born into this flourishing age, and my name was enrolled among those who succeeded in the examinations for worthy men. Formerly, in …

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
先朝叨居言路擬奪宣徽之使因攻宰執之私
銳意澄清危言剴切出補英州別駕自甘
殘喘投荒為
社稷以生還已缺詞林之望脫風波於險道
未忘淮浦之吟立朝素無益於
明時論事輙有乖於物議揣巳分宜填溝壑
荷
天恩不棄菲葑拔於閑散之濱處以台衡之貳
===
望非意及寵與憂并臣敢不砥礪猷為激
昂節操都俞吁咈用諧虞代之賡歌福禄
壽康擬叶卷阿之諷諫勤于夙勤于夜恪
殫犬馬之勞慎厥始慎厥終仰荅
乾坤之德伏願
皇風清穆
帝德光華永垂
昭代之休厚賚蒼生之慶離明普照日同曜
punctuated: 先朝，叨居言路，擬奪宣徽之使，因攻宰執之私。銳意澄清，危言剴切，出補英州別駕，自甘殘喘投荒。為社稷以生還，已缺詞林之望；脫風波於險道，未忘淮浦之吟。立朝素無益於明時，論事輙有乖於物議。揣巳分宜填溝壑，荷天恩不棄菲葑，拔於閑散之濱，處以台衡之貳。望非意及，寵與憂并。臣敢不砥礪猷為，激昂節操！都俞吁咈，用諧虞代之賡歌；福禄壽康，擬叶卷阿之諷諫。勤于夙，勤于夜，恪殫犬馬之勞；慎厥始，慎厥終，仰荅乾坤之德。伏願皇風清穆，帝德光華，永垂昭代之休，厚賚蒼生之慶。離明普照，日同曜
translation_en:
…in the former reign, I had the unmerited honor of serving in a remonstrance post. I proposed stripping the Xuanhui Commissioner of his office [?], thereby attacking the chief councillors’ pursuit of private interests. Intent on cleansing the administration, I spoke forthrightly and earnestly. Sent out to serve as Assistant Prefect of Yingzhou, I willingly accepted exile in the wilderness with what little breath remained to me. Returning alive to serve the altars of soil and grain, I had already lost hope of a place among the court’s literary officials; escaping the storms along a perilous road, I had not forgotten my verses on the banks of the Huai. My service at court had never benefited this enlightened age, and my discussions of affairs repeatedly ran counter to prevailing opinion. Reflecting on my lot, I thought it fitting that I should end my days in a ditch. Yet through imperial grace, even such humble greens as I were not discarded: I was raised from the margins of idle retirement and appointed deputy to the chief councillor.

This exceeded anything I had hoped or imagined; favor and anxiety came together. How could your servant dare fail to sharpen his resolve and exertions, and uphold his integrity! Through assent and candid dissent, may I join in the responsive songs of the age of Shun; invoking blessings, emoluments, longevity, and well-being, may I accord with the admonitions of “Winding Hills” (Juan e). Diligent at dawn and diligent at night, I shall respectfully exhaust my humble strength in service; careful at the beginning and careful at the end, I shall endeavor to repay the bounty of Heaven and Earth.

I humbly wish that the imperial influence may be pure and harmonious, and the emperor’s virtue radiant; that the excellence of this illustrious age may endure forever, and blessings be bestowed abundantly upon the people. May imperial brightness illuminate all, sharing the sun’s radiance…

title: 成化二十二年廣東鄉試錄
text:

聖壽無疆天與長而地與久臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
策
===
第一問
張紹齡
同考試官訓導王批古今勸懲之典鋪張無
遺博洽之士也高薦何忝

而月同輝，聖壽無疆，天與長而地與久。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

策

張紹齡

同考試官訓導王批：「古今勸懲之典，鋪張無遺，博洽之士也，高薦何忝？」

Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, is overcome with fervent emotion and reverent trepidation. I respectfully submit this memorial to convey my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Zhang Shaoling
